1.188.s:
1.256
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
gandharvāḥ kaṭakaṃ kecidviviśurbharatasya tu ..
puraskṛtya nṛpasyājñāṃ sainikānāṃ vadhepsavaḥ .. 1 ..
1.188.d:
1.256
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
गन्धर्वाः कटकं केचिद्विविशुर्भरतस्य तु ॥
पुरस्कृत्य नृपस्याज्ञां सैनिकानां वधेप्सवः ॥ 1 ॥
1.188.m: 1.256 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Some Gandharvas, however, entered the encampment of Bharata, / placing the king's command before them, desirous of slaying the soldiers.

1.188.s:
māyācchannaśarīrāste dadṛśurniśi ceṣṭitam ..
prātaḥ samarakāmānāṃ kāntotkaṇṭhitacetasām .. 2 ..
1.188.d:
मायाच्छन्नशरीरास्ते ददृशुर्निशि चेष्टितम् ॥
प्रातः समरकामानां कान्तोत्कण्ठितचेतसाम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.188.m: With their bodies concealed by illusion, they beheld at night the conduct / of those who longed for battle in the morning, their hearts yearning for their beloveds.

1.188.s:
manoratharathārūḍhaḥ kaścitprāṇeśvarīṃ vrajan ..
na lebhe śayane nidrāṃ kalye raṇasamutsakaḥ .. 3 ...
1.188.d:
मनोरथरथारूढः कश्चित्प्राणेश्वरीं व्रजन् ॥
न लेभे शयने निद्रां कल्ये रणसमुत्सकः ॥ 3 ॥।
1.188.m: One, mounted on the chariot of desire and travelling to the mistress of his life, / found no sleep on his bed, though eager for battle at dawn.

1.188.s:
kaściccandrakarasparśādviśeṣaparipīḍitaḥ ..
dadarśa candraṃ divyākṣipriyāvadananirjitam .. 4 ..
1.188.d:
कश्चिच्चन्द्रकरस्पर्शाद्विशेषपरिपीडितः ॥
ददर्श चन्द्रं दिव्याक्षिप्रियावदननिर्जितम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.188.m: Another, intensely afflicted by the touch of the moon's rays, / looked upon the moon as surpassed by the face of his divine-eyed beloved.

1.188.s:
kaścicca cintayanneva priyāṃ prāṇadhaneśvarīm ..
uttāna śayanaṃ cakre tārakāgaṇakaṃ divi .. 5 ..
1.188.d:
कश्चिच्च चिन्तयन्नेव प्रियां प्राणधनेश्वरीम् ॥
उत्तान शयनं चक्रे तारकागणकं दिवि ॥ 5 ॥
1.188.m: And another, meditating on his beloved, the mistress of his life and wealth, / lay facing upwards, counting the stars in the sky.

1.188.s:
paśyannāniṣkṛtaṃ diśyaṃ patracchedaṃ visarjitam ..
priyayā svakṛtaṃ kaścinmudā nayati śarvarīm .. 6 ..
1.188.d:
पश्यन्नानिष्कृतं दिश्यं पत्रच्छेदं विसर्जितम् ॥
प्रियया स्वकृतं कश्चिन्मुदा नयति शर्वरीम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.188.m: One spent the night with joy, gazing upon a displayed decorative pattern / of leaf-cuttings made by his beloved and sent to him.

1.188.s:
nirvedamatiramyeṇa dahyate candraraśmibhiḥ ..
kaścidvihīnastanvaṅgyā śayanīye'pi khidyate .. 7 ..
1.188.d:
निर्वेदमतिरम्येण दह्यते चन्द्ररश्मिभिः ॥
कश्चिद्विहीनस्तन्वङ्ग्या शयनीयेऽपि खिद्यते ॥ 7 ॥
1.188.m: Another was burned by the rays of the exceedingly charming moon into despondency; / separated from his slender-limbed woman, he grieved even upon his bed.

1.188.s:
svapnopalabdhatanvaṅgisamāgamamanorathaḥ ..
supto'numito gandharvaiḥ kaścidromāñcasambhavāt .. 8 ..
1.188.d:
स्वप्नोपलब्धतन्वङ्गिसमागममनोरथः ॥
सुप्तोऽनुमितो गन्धर्वैः कश्चिद्रोमाञ्चसम्भवात् ॥ 8 ॥
1.188.m: One who had attained in a dream the wish of union with his slender-limbed beloved / was inferred by the Gandharvas to be asleep from the bristling of his body hair.

1.188.s:
priyāṃ saṃpreṣitā preṣya samālāpaparāyaṇaḥ ..
na veda kaścidrājendra gatāmapi vibhāvarīm .. 9 ..
1.188.d:
प्रियां संप्रेषिता प्रेष्य समालापपरायणः ॥
न वेद कश्चिद्राजेन्द्र गतामपि विभावरीम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.188.m: Sending a female messenger sent by his beloved, another, engrossed in conversation, / did not even know that the night had passed, O king of kings.

1.188.s:
jvalantamaniśaṃ kaściccharīre virahānalam ..
sahasā śamayāmāsa dhyāyam̐ścandramukhīṃ priyām .. 1.256.10 ..
1.188.d:
ज्वलन्तमनिशं कश्चिच्छरीरे विरहानलम् ॥
सहसा शमयामास ध्यायम्̐श्चन्द्रमुखीं प्रियाम् ॥ 1.256.10 ॥
1.188.m: One suddenly quenched the fire of separation blazing incessantly in his body / by meditating upon his moon-faced beloved.

1.188.s:
śyāmāṃ vikañcukāṃ tanvīṃ yūnāṃ prāṇāpahāriṇīm ..
priyāṃ ca khaḍgayaṣṭiṃ ca kaścitsmarati sūtsukaḥ .. 11 ..
1.188.d:
श्यामां विकञ्चुकां तन्वीं यूनां प्राणापहारिणीम् ॥
प्रियां च खड्गयष्टिं च कश्चित्स्मरति सूत्सुकः ॥ 11 ॥
1.188.m: Eagerly, one remembered his beloved—slender, youthful, bodice-less, and stealing away the breath of young men— / and likewise his sword-blade.

1.188.s:
saguṇāṃ tanumadhyāṃ ca navakāñcanabhūṣaṇām ..
sasmāra dayitāṃ kaściccāpayaṣṭiṃ tathaiva ca ..12..
1.188.d:
सगुणां तनुमध्यां च नवकाञ्चनभूषणाम् ॥
सस्मार दयितां कश्चिच्चापयष्टिं तथैव च ॥12॥
1.188.m: Another remembered his darling—virtuous, slender-waisted, and adorned with new gold— / and likewise his bow-staff, strung with a bowstring, slender at the grip, and adorned with fresh gold.

1.188.s:
vicintānapi gandharvā bharatasya ca sainikān ..
na śekurādharṣayituṃ bharatasya samāśrayāt .. 13 ..
1.188.d:
विचिन्तानपि गन्धर्वा भरतस्य च सैनिकान् ॥
न शेकुराधर्षयितुं भरतस्य समाश्रयात् ॥ 13 ॥
1.188.m: Though the soldiers of Bharata were lost in thought, the Gandharvas / were unable to overpower them, because of the protection of Bharata.

1.188.s:
anye'pi ye devavarasya viṣṇoḥ smaraṃti nityaṃ yadunāthapādau ..
gandharvayakṣāsurarākṣasebhyo bhayaṃ na teṣāṃ bhavatīha kiñcit .. 14 .. ..
1.257
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
atha rājagṛhākhyaṃ tu nagaraṃ ye visarjitāḥ ..
gaṃdharvā dadṛśustatra puraśriyamanuttamām .. 1 ..
candrasāpatnyabhūtāni gṛhamukhyāni sarvaśaḥ ..
dadṛśurbahuratnāni vahudhānyadhanāni ca .. 2 ..
purodyānāni ramyāṇi dadṛśuśca samantataḥ ..
alaṃkṛtāni vāpībhirdrumakhaṇḍaiśca yādava .. 3 ..
udyāneṣu vicitreṣu naramukhyānugāminām ..
paśyanti tatra saṅghāni gaṃdharvāḥ pānapāyinām .. 4 ..
vallakīnāṃ ninādena gītena madhureṇa ca ..
ekatāmiva saṃyātaṃ cāruṣaṭpadaśiñjitam .. 5..
veśyāścaivopanṛtyanti kvacittatra ca kāmukān ..
kvacitsābharaṇāḥ suptāḥ kāntaiḥ saha madotkaṭāḥ .. 6 ..
1.188.d:
अन्येऽपि ये देववरस्य विष्णोः स्मरंति नित्यं यदुनाथपादौ ॥
गन्धर्वयक्षासुरराक्षसेभ्यो भयं न तेषां भवतीह किञ्चित् ॥ 14 ॥ ॥
1.257
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
अथ राजगृहाख्यं तु नगरं ये विसर्जिताः ॥
गंधर्वा ददृशुस्तत्र पुरश्रियमनुत्तमाम् ॥ 1 ॥
चन्द्रसापत्न्यभूतानि गृहमुख्यानि सर्वशः ॥
ददृशुर्बहुरत्नानि वहुधान्यधनानि च ॥ 2 ॥
पुरोद्यानानि रम्याणि ददृशुश्च समन्ततः ॥
अलंकृतानि वापीभिर्द्रुमखण्डैश्च यादव ॥ 3 ॥
उद्यानेषु विचित्रेषु नरमुख्यानुगामिनाम् ॥
पश्यन्ति तत्र सङ्घानि गंधर्वाः पानपायिनाम् ॥ 4 ॥
वल्लकीनां निनादेन गीतेन मधुरेण च ॥
एकतामिव संयातं चारुषट्पदशिञ्जितम् ॥ 5॥
वेश्याश्चैवोपनृत्यन्ति क्वचित्तत्र च कामुकान् ॥
क्वचित्साभरणाः सुप्ताः कान्तैः सह मदोत्कटाः ॥ 6 ॥
1.188.m:
Whatever others also constantly remember the feet of the Lord of the Yadus, the foremost of the gods, Viṣṇu, / they have no fear at all in this world from Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, or Rākṣasas.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now those Gandharvas who had been dispatched to the city named Rājagṛha / saw there an unsurpassed urban splendour.
The principal houses everywhere rivalled the moon; / they saw abundant jewels, plentiful grain and wealth.
And all around they saw the delightful city gardens / adorned with step-wells and groves of trees, O descendant of Yadu.
In the wondrous gardens the Gandharvas saw / troops of wine-drinkers following prominent men.
Along with the sounding of lutes and sweet singing, / the charming humming of six-footed bees seemed to become one [with it].
And courtesans were dancing there near the impassioned [lovers]; / elsewhere, adorned with ornaments and overcome with intoxication, they slept with their beloveds.

1.188.s:
suptānāṃ naranārīṇāṃ gandharvāstatra ceṣṭitam ..
dadṛśurbahudārāṇāṃ māyācchāditavigrahāḥ .. 7 ..
gāyantyanye rudantyanye hasantyanye tathaiva ca..
āśliṣyanti tathaivānye madamattāḥ parasparam .. 8 ..
bhāṣante kecidavyaktaṃ vihvalārtāḥ padepade ..
śayane bhramamāṇaiśca kvacidasthitadṛṣṭayaḥ .. 9 ..
kāminīskandhavinyastabāhavaśca tathā pare ..
kalahaṃ cakrire cānye stuvantyanye nirarthakam .. 1.257.10 ..
skhalamānapadā yānti sthānaṃ hṛdyanavasthitam ..
āhvayanti gaṇānkecitpraṇamanti tathā pare .. 11 ..
evaṃ santajanākīrṇe nagare gītanādite ..
dadṛśurgṛhamukhyeṣu naranārīviceṣṭitam .. 12 ..
sañcodyamānā dūtībhistvarākṛta mṛjāḥ dhiyaḥ ..
yānti kāntāsu sambhrāntā madapānasamutsukāḥ .. 13 ..
papuḥ kāścitpriyaiḥ sārdhaṃ pānaṃ madasamīraṇam ..
pāyayantyaparāḥ kāntānbhojayantyaparāḥ priyān .. 14 ..
1.188.d:
सुप्तानां नरनारीणां गन्धर्वास्तत्र चेष्टितम् ॥
ददृशुर्बहुदाराणां मायाच्छादितविग्रहाः ॥ 7 ॥
गायन्त्यन्ये रुदन्त्यन्ये हसन्त्यन्ये तथैव च॥
आश्लिष्यन्ति तथैवान्ये मदमत्ताः परस्परम् ॥ 8 ॥
भाषन्ते केचिदव्यक्तं विह्वलार्ताः पदेपदे ॥
शयने भ्रममाणैश्च क्वचिदस्थितदृष्टयः ॥ 9 ॥
कामिनीस्कन्धविन्यस्तबाहवश्च तथा परे ॥
कलहं चक्रिरे चान्ये स्तुवन्त्यन्ये निरर्थकम् ॥ 1.257.10 ॥
स्खलमानपदा यान्ति स्थानं हृद्यनवस्थितम् ॥
आह्वयन्ति गणान्केचित्प्रणमन्ति तथा परे ॥ 11 ॥
एवं सन्तजनाकीर्णे नगरे गीतनादिते ॥
ददृशुर्गृहमुख्येषु नरनारीविचेष्टितम् ॥ 12 ॥
सञ्चोद्यमाना दूतीभिस्त्वराकृत मृजाः धियः ॥
यान्ति कान्तासु सम्भ्रान्ता मदपानसमुत्सुकाः ॥ 13 ॥
पपुः काश्चित्प्रियैः सार्धं पानं मदसमीरणम् ॥
पाययन्त्यपराः कान्तान्भोजयन्त्यपराः प्रियान् ॥ 14 ॥
1.188.m:
Their bodies concealed by illusory power, the Gandharvas saw there / the movements of sleeping men and women, and of men with many wives.
Some were singing, others weeping, others laughing in that very manner; / yet others, drunk with passion, were embracing one another.
Distressed and confused, some spoke indistinctly at every step; / with eyes turning aimlessly, their gaze rested nowhere on the couch.
And others had placed their arms on the shoulders of desirable women; / some engaged in quarrels, and others uttered meaningless praise.
With stumbling feet they went to a place, their minds unsteady; / some called out to crowds, while others bowed down low.
Thus in the city crowded with good people and echoing with song, / they saw the actions of men and women in the finest houses.
Urged on by female messengers, their understanding cleans[ed] in haste, / agitated, eager for wine-drinking, they went towards their beloved women.
Some drank wine together with their lovers, stirring up passion; / others made their beloveds drink, and others fed their lovers.

1.188.s:
prāsādeṣu vicitreṣu tathā vātāyaneṣu ca ..
ratiśrāntāstathā suptāḥ kāścitkāntaiḥ saha striyaḥ .. 15 ..
1.188.d:
प्रासादेषु विचित्रेषु तथा वातायनेषु च ॥
रतिश्रान्तास्तथा सुप्ताः काश्चित्कान्तैः सह स्त्रियः ॥ 15 ॥
1.188.m: In the wondrous palaces and at the windows, / some women, exhausted by lovemaking, slept with their lovers.

1.188.s:
kācidgaurī priyaṃ śyāmamāliṅgya śayane sthitā ..
utpalasragivābhāti yuktā jātisrajā saha ..16..
1.188.d:
काचिद्गौरी प्रियं श्याममालिङ्ग्य शयने स्थिता ॥
उत्पलस्रगिवाभाति युक्ता जातिस्रजा सह ॥16॥
1.188.m: A fair woman, resting on the couch having embraced her dark lover, / shone like a blue-lotus garland joined with a garland of jasmine.

1.188.s:
gaurīgaurasamāśliṣṭā kācidābhāti sundarī..
āliṅgitā candrakaraiścandrakāntaśilā yathā .. 17 ..
1.188.d:
गौरीगौरसमाश्लिष्टा काचिदाभाति सुन्दरी॥
आलिङ्गिता चन्द्रकरैश्चन्द्रकान्तशिला यथा ॥ 17 ॥
1.188.m: A fair beautiful woman embraced by a fair man shone / like a moonstone embraced by the rays of the moon.

1.188.s:
śyāmā śyāmasamāśliṣṭā kācidābhāti pārthiva ..
payodapaṅktirgagane yathā pārthiva sodakā .. 18 ..
1.188.d:
श्यामा श्यामसमाश्लिष्टा काचिदाभाति पार्थिव ॥
पयोदपङ्क्तिर्गगने यथा पार्थिव सोदका ॥ 18 ॥
1.188.m: A dark woman embraced by a dark man shone, O king, / like a row of water-bearing clouds in the sky, O ruler of the earth.

1.188.s:
alīkasuptamaprauḍhā kāciccumbayate priyam ..
priyeṇa gāḍhamāśliṣṭā vilakṣamuditābhavat .. 19 ..
1.188.d:
अलीकसुप्तमप्रौढा काचिच्चुम्बयते प्रियम् ॥
प्रियेण गाढमाश्लिष्टा विलक्षमुदिताभवत् ॥ 19 ॥
1.188.m: An innocent woman kissed her lover who was feigning sleep; / embraced tightly by her lover, she became shy and joyful.

1.188.s:
kācicca vanitā prauḍhā karpūra rajasā svayam ..
avākirati kāntāṅgaṃ ratisvedapariplutam .. 1.257.20 ..
1.188.d:
काचिच्च वनिता प्रौढा कर्पूर रजसा स्वयम् ॥
अवाकिरति कान्ताङ्गं रतिस्वेदपरिप्लुतम् ॥ 1.257.20 ॥
1.188.m: And an experienced woman with her own hands showered camphor dust / over the limbs of her beloved, drenched in the sweat of lovemaking.

1.188.s:
paśyemāṃ tārakāṃ candro hyaṅkenāliṅgya tiṣṭhati ..
ityāha dayitaṃ kācitprauḍhā ratisukhārthinī .. 21 ..
1.188.d:
पश्येमां तारकां चन्द्रो ह्यङ्केनालिङ्ग्य तिष्ठति ॥
इत्याह दयितं काचित्प्रौढा रतिसुखार्थिनी ॥ 21 ॥
1.188.m: “Look, the moon stands holding this star in his lap!” / So said an experienced woman desiring the pleasures of love to her beloved.

1.188.s:
kācidūruparāmarśādviditvā suratārthinī ..
kāntenāliṅgitā gāḍhaṃ muditena riraṃsunā .. 22 ..
1.188.d:
काचिदूरुपरामर्शाद्विदित्वा सुरतार्थिनी ॥
कान्तेनालिङ्गिता गाढं मुदितेन रिरंसुना ॥ 22 ॥
1.188.m: A woman desiring sexual union, knowing it from the touching of her thighs, / was embraced tightly by her delighted lover wishing to make love.

1.188.s:
kāntena kāciddaṣṭauṣṭhī cumbanāyārpite mukhe..
na yāsye tava viśvāsaṃ bhūyaścedanyathākṛthāḥ .. 23 ..
1.188.d:
कान्तेन काचिद्दष्टौष्ठी चुम्बनायार्पिते मुखे॥
न यास्ये तव विश्वासं भूयश्चेदन्यथाकृथाः ॥ 23 ॥
1.188.m: When her mouth was offered for a kiss, a woman whose lip was bitten by her lover [said]: / “I will not trust you again if you act otherwise!”

1.188.s:
kācitprasuptā kāntena parāmṛṣṭā ratārthinī ..
kāntamāliṅgatātyarthaṃ tyaktanidrā sasambhramā .. 24 ..
1.188.d:
काचित्प्रसुप्ता कान्तेन परामृष्टा रतार्थिनी ॥
कान्तमालिङ्गतात्यर्थं त्यक्तनिद्रा ससम्भ्रमा ॥ 24 ॥
1.188.m: A sleeping woman desiring love, touched by her lover, / awoke with excitement and embraced her lover tightly.

1.188.s:
ityevamapi viśvastānsainikām̐stānyudhājitaḥ..

इत्येवमपि विश्वस्तान्सैनिकाम्̐स्तान्युधाजितः॥
हर्तुं न शेकुर्गन्धर्वा भरतस्य समाश्रयात् ॥ 25 ॥
1.188.m: Yet the Gandharvas could not destroy these soldiers of Yudhājit, / confiding as they were, because of the protection of Bharata.

1.188.d:
एषां पुरे सन्निहितः स विष्णुर्महानुभावो रघुवंशगोप्ता ॥
तेषां पुरे नास्ति भयं नरेन्द्र गन्धर्व यक्षासुरपन्नगेभ्यः ॥ 26 ॥
1.258
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अयोध्यातस्तदाभ्येत्य गन्धर्वाः शिबिरात्तथा ॥
तथा राजगृहात्सर्वे शैलूषाय न्यवेदयन् ॥ 1 ॥
न विग्रहकथा तत्र न रक्षा काचिदीदृशी ॥
केवलं तु प्रभावेण रामस्य भरतस्य च ॥ 2 ॥
नास्माभिः किं कृतं राजन्प्रहर्तुं क्वचिदित्यपि ॥
यत्तत्र शेषं कर्त्तव्यं तत्करोतु महीपतिः॥3॥
एवमुक्तः स गन्धर्वैर्यामिनीविगमे तदा ॥
योगयोगमतिक्षिप्रमाज्ञापयत सत्वरः ॥4॥
भेरी सान्नाहिकी चैव ततः शीघ्रमहन्यत ॥
यस्याः शब्देन गन्धर्वा राजद्वारमुपागताः ॥ 5 ॥
गजवारेण महता तुरगाणां बलेन च ॥
रथैश्च मेघसन्नादैः पत्तिभिश्च मदोत्कटैः ॥ 6 ॥
1.188.m:
That high-minded Viṣṇu, protector of the Raghu lineage, was present in their city; / in their city there is no fear, O king, from Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, or serpents.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Returning then from Ayodhyā, from the camp, / and from Rājagṛha, all the Gandharvas reported to Śailūṣa:
“There was no talk of conflict there, nor any such protection; / it is solely through the power of Rāma and of Bharata.
Why was nothing done by us anywhere to strike, O king? / Whatever remains to be done in this matter, let the ruler of the earth do it.”
Thus addressed by the Gandharvas at the end of the night, / he quickly and promptly gave the command to prepare for action.
Then the kettle-drum of assembly was immediately struck, / at whose sound the Gandharvas approached the king’s gate.
With a large troop of elephants and an army of horses, / with chariots rumbling like clouds, and foot-soldiers fierce with fury,

1.188.d:
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितरवैः शङ्खभेरीनिनादितैः ॥
ह्रादेन गजघण्टानां गजानां चैव बृंहितैः ॥ 7 ॥
ह्रेषितैस्तुरगाणां तु बभूव तुमलं महत ॥
शैलूषोऽपि तदा स्नात्वा हुत्वाग्निं द्विजपूजनम् ॥ 8 ॥
कृत्वा विनिर्ययौ श्रीमान्वरचन्दनभूषितः ॥
मौली वपुष्मान्सन्नद्धः स्रग्वी रुचिरभूषणः ॥ 9 ॥
आमपात्रप्रतीकाशैस्तुरगैर्योजितं रथम् ॥
आरुरोह महातेजा विमानं सुकृती यथा ॥ 1.258.10 ॥
यथोक्तस्य रथस्यासीत्पुरो रणविशारदः ॥
नरकेतुरिति ख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः ॥ 11 ॥
केतौ तस्य रथे भाति वसन्तो मूर्तिमान्कृतः ॥
ततः स सह सैन्येन निर्ययौ नगराद्बहिः ॥ 12 ॥
व्यूहं च सर्वतोभद्रं समाधाय बलं तथा ॥
कृत्वा प्रत्यैक्षत तदा भरतागमनं रुषा ॥ 13 ॥
सैन्येन महता राजन्भास्करस्योदयं प्रति॥14॥
1.188.m:
with battle-cries and the sound of clapping arms, with the blasts of conches and kettle-drums, / with the clanging of elephant bells and the trumpeting of elephants,
and with the neighing of horses, a great tumult arose. / Śailūṣa too, having bathed, offered into the fire, and honoured the twice-born,
went forth, glorious, adorned with choice sandalwood, / wearing a diadem, handsome, clad in armour, wearing garlands and splendid ornaments.
Of great splendour, he mounted his chariot yoked to horses / resembling raw earthenware vessels, as a virtuous man mounts a celestial car.
In front of the chariot as described was one skilled in battle, / celebrated as Naraketu, renowned in the three worlds.
Upon his chariot, spring embodied was depicted on the banner. / Then he went forth outside the city together with his army.
Having arranged the army in the ‘auspicious-on-all-sides’ array / and deployed the force, he then awaited with wrath the arrival of Bharata,
with a mighty army, O king, facing the rise of the sun.

1.188.d:
आत्तायुधाः क्ष्वेडितशङ्खनादैरानन्दयन्तः सुहृदां मनांसि ॥
गन्धर्वमुख्या रणचण्डवेगाः प्रतीक्षमाणा भरतस्य तस्थुः ॥ 15 ॥
1.259
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
विबुद्धा यामिनीशेषे सर्व एव महीक्षितः ॥
निर्ययुर्नगराकारै रथैः संग्रामलालसाः ॥1॥
बलेन चतुरङ्गेण नानावादित्रवादिना ॥
बन्दिभिः स्तूयमानाश्च वन्द्यमानाश्च सैनिकैः ॥ 2 ॥
पृथक्पृथक्सुसन्नद्धा नगरद्वारमागताः ॥
कृत्वा चावश्यकं सर्वं भरतोऽपि महायशाः ॥ 3 ॥
रथेन काञ्चनाङ्गेन निर्ययौ नगराद्बहिः ॥
यन्ता रथस्य तस्यासीद्युधाजिन्मातुलः स्वयम्॥ ॥ 4 ॥
विरराज ध्वजं तस्य कोविदारमहाद्रुमम् ॥
स तेन रथमुख्येन बहिर्निर्गम्य पार्थिवः ॥ 5 ॥
समेत्य पार्थिवैः सर्वैः पूजयित्वा च तान्नृपान् ॥
वज्रं कृत्वा महाव्यूहं प्रययौ लघुविक्रमः ॥ 6 ॥
1.188.m:
Weapons taken up, delighting the minds of their allies with war-cries and conch-blasts, / the chiefs of the Gandharvas, of fierce fury in battle, stood waiting for Bharata.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Awakened at the end of the night, all the rulers of the earth, / longing for battle, went forth in chariots resembling cities.
with a fourfold army, sounding diverse musical instruments, / praised by bards and hailed by soldiers,
each well-accoutred individually, they arrived at the city gate. / And having performed all essential rites, the highly renowned Bharata also
went forth out of the city in a chariot of golden parts. / The driver of his chariot was his maternal uncle Yudhājit himself.
His banner shone, [bearing] a great kovidāra tree. / Having marched out with that foremost chariot, the king,
joined with all the kings and, having honored those rulers, / formed the great battle-array [called] vajra and marched forth with swift strides.

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam ..

1.188.d:
प्रयाणे तस्य सैन्यस्य कम्पन्तीव वसुन्धरा ॥
शब्देन महता तस्य दीर्यते च नभस्तलम् ॥ 7 ॥
बभूव रजसैवान्यः निशाकालः सुदारुणः॥
नृपाभरमाणिक्यतेजसा भुवि राजिता ॥ 8 ॥
रजोन्धकारेऽपि चमूः सा प्रयाति यथासुखम् ॥
स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति॥ 9 ॥
आससाद महत्सैन्यं गन्धर्वाणां दुरत्ययम् ॥1.259.10॥
तौ सैन्यतोयौघमहादुरन्तौ संहारनागाविव तुल्यरूपौ ॥
बलार्णवौ गाढमथ प्रहारं प्रचक्रतुर्मन्युवशानुयातौ ॥ 11 ॥
1.260
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम् ॥
शूराणां हर्षजननं भीतानां भयवर्धनम्॥1॥
सेनाविनिर्गमे तत्र रजसाच्छादितं जगत्॥
न प्रज्ञायत राजेन्द्र किञ्चिदेव समन्ततः ॥ 2 ॥
कूजतां धनुषां शब्दः श्रूयते तुमुलो महान्॥
शङ्खभेरीनिनादश्च कुञ्जराणां च बृंहितम् ॥3॥
1.188.m:
As that army marched, the earth seemed to tremble; / and at its immense sound the vault of the sky seemed to split.
There arose from the dust alone an unnatural, dread night. / Radiant on the earth with the brilliance of jewels on royal ornaments,
even in the darkness of the dust that army marched at its ease. / Having traversed a long road toward the sunrise,
he reached the vast, insuperable army of the gandharvas.
Those two boundless oceans of armies, like two equal dragons of dissolution, / those oceans of forces, driven by wrath, struck violent blows at each other.
1.260
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then began a tumultuous battle that made the hair stand on end, / causing joy to heroes and augmenting fear in the frightened.
As the army advanced there, the world was covered in dust; / nothing at all could be discerned on any side, O best of kings.
The great, tumultuous twang of sounding bows was heard, / and the blast of conches and kettledrums, and the trumpeting of elephants,

1.188.d:
हयानां ह्रेषमाणानां शूराणां चैव गर्जताम् ॥
शस्त्राणां पात्यमानानां योधानां कवचेष्वपि ॥4॥
तिष्ठतिष्ठ न मे जीवन्गन्तासि रणमूर्धनि ॥5॥
स्थितोऽस्मि प्रहरस्वेति किं न जानाति मां भवान् ॥6 ॥
प्रहरस्व तथा छिन्धि भिन्धि घातय मा चिरम् ॥
एवमादीनि वाक्यानि श्रूयन्ते रणमूर्धनि॥ 7 ॥
तथा तुमुलसंग्रामे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे ॥
प्रशशाम रजो भौममुत्थितं रणशोणितैः ॥ 8 ॥
पूर्वोत्थितेन रजसा मेघेनेव नभस्तलम् ॥
व्याप्तं तद्विरजस्केन तदा राजन्रणाङ्गणे ॥9॥
ततो युयुधिरे वीराः पश्यमाना परस्परम् ॥
गोत्रापदाननामानि कीर्तयन्तः पुनःपुनः ॥ 1.260.10 ॥
सेनानां भज्यमानानां सैन्यखण्डैर्बलीयसाम् ॥
भूयश्चावर्तमानानां शुश्रवे तमुलः स्वनः ॥11॥
चित्राणां च ध्वजानां च पताकानां च भूभुजः ॥
अदृश्यत समासिक्तं रुधिरं रणमूर्धनि ॥ 12 ॥
1.188.m:
and the neighing of horses, and the roaring of heroes, / and [the clash] of weapons falling upon the armor of warriors:
“Halt, halt! You will not depart alive from the front of battle!”
“Here I stand, strike! Do you not know me?”
“Strike! Cut down! Pierce! Kill, delay not!” / Such words were heard at the front of battle.
As that dread, tumultuous battle proceeded thus, / the earthly dust that had arisen was quelled by the blood of battle.
The sky, which had earlier been covered by rising dust as if by a cloud, / then became free of dust over the field of battle, O king.
Then the heroes fought, looking upon one another, / proclaiming their lineages, heroic exploits, and names again and again.
A tumultuous clamor was heard of armies being shattered by stronger detachments of forces, / and returning once more [to the fight].
Blood was seen bespattering the variegated banners / and pennants of the kings at the front of battle.

1.188.m: When that dust-cloud had vanished and the sky cleared, O great king, / the great battle proceeded in pristine directions.
