khaṅgadhārānikṛttānāṃ padātīnāṃ padātibhiḥ .. 18 ..
dvidhā kṛtāni gātrāṇi nipatanti mahītale ..
gṛhītvā khaṅgapātāni rejuḥ kecicca varmiṇaḥ .. 19 ..
khaṅgamuddharatāṃ teṣāṃ cicchidurnṛpa vigrahān ..
kecidgadāvinirbhinnamastakā gadibhiḥ kṣitau .. 1.260.20 ..
patitāstatra dṛśyante raṇe śatasahasraśaḥ ..
bhagnāsiśeṣanikṣepa nihatārātayastathā .. 21 ..
1.188.d:
तथा प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे देवगन्धर्वदानवैः ॥
सिद्धैर्विद्याधरैश्चैव मुनिसंघैः समन्ततः ॥34॥
आवृतं सहसा व्योम वज्रयुद्धकुतूहलैः ॥
व्यदृश्यन्त विमानानि तेषां खे विमलान्यपि ॥ 15 ॥
किङ्किणीशतघुष्टानि पताकाशोभितानि च ॥
शुभं गन्धमथादाय सुरभिर्मारुतो ववौ ॥ 16 ॥
पपात पुष्पवर्षं च योधानां तत्र मूर्धनि ॥
तथा प्रवृत्ते तुमुले क्ष्वेडितोत्कृष्टनादिते ॥ 17 ॥
पदातयस्तदा जघ्नुः पदातीनि च संयुगे ॥
खङ्गधारानिकृत्तानां पदातीनां पदातिभिः ॥ 18 ॥
द्विधा कृतानि गात्राणि निपतन्ति महीतले ॥
गृहीत्वा खङ्गपातानि रेजुः केचिच्च वर्मिणः ॥ 19 ॥
खङ्गमुद्धरतां तेषां चिच्छिदुर्नृप विग्रहान् ॥
केचिद्गदाविनिर्भिन्नमस्तका गदिभिः क्षितौ ॥ 1.260.20 ॥
पतितास्तत्र दृश्यन्ते रणे शतसहस्रशः ॥
भग्नासिशेषनिक्षेप निहतारातयस्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.188.m:
As the battle thus proceeded, by gods, gandharvas, and dānavas, / by siddhas, vidyādharas, and hosts of sages on all sides,
the sky was suddenly filled, eager to witness the thunderous battle; / their immaculate aerial chariots were seen in the sky,
ringing with hundreds of tiny bells and adorned with pennants. / Then a fragrant breeze blew, carrying an auspicious scent,
and a shower of flowers fell upon the heads of the warriors there. / As it thus proceeded tumultuously, resounding with shouts and battle-cries,
foot-soldiers then slew foot-soldiers in the encounter. / Of foot-soldiers severed by the sword-edges of foot-soldiers,
limbs cut in two fell down upon the surface of the earth. / Some armored men shone forth, parrying blows of swords;
they cut the bodies of those drawing their swords, O king. / Some, their heads shattered with maces by mace-bearers upon the ground,
were seen fallen by hundreds of thousands in that battle. / Striking down enemies by hurling the remaining fragments of broken swords,

1.188.s:
siṃhanādaravāṃścakruḥ parasainyavidāraṇān ..
keśeṣvanyonyamākṛṣya khaḍgaiḥ kecitparasparam .. 22 ..
āsedurvasudhāṃ kṛtvā gataprāṇāstathā pare ..
pṛṣṭhavinyastavarmāṇaḥ sannaddhāṃsturagāṃstathā .. 23 ..
kṛtvā vipādānsamare nijaghnuḥ sādināṃ gaṇam ..
āruhya varmiṇaḥ kecidvegācchatrurathānraṇe .. 24 ..
sārathīnvigataprāṇām̐ścakuryuddhaviśāradāḥ ..
cicchidurvāraṇendrāṇāṃ karānkecitpadātinaḥ .. 25 ..
keciddaśanavinyastapādāścāruruhurgajān ..
sādinaśca tathā kecidviśiraskānraṇājire .. 26 ..
cakruḥ padātino dhmātāḥ khaḍgairākāśasannibhaiḥ ..
kecicca sādinaḥ prāsaiḥ pañca sapta tathā śarān .. 27 ..
śreṇīkṛtānvai bibhiduḥ śikṣayā raṇakovidāḥ ..
kecicchārṅgadhanurnyastabāṇajālākulīkṛtān .. 28 ..
padātīnsamare cakrurvāyuvegaisturaṅgamaiḥ ..
sādinaśca tathaivānye sādibhiḥ saha saṃgatāḥ .. .. 29 ..
1.188.d:
सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुः परसैन्यविदारणान् ॥
केशेष्वन्योन्यमाकृष्य खड्गैः केचित्परस्परम् ॥ 22 ॥
आसेदुर्वसुधां कृत्वा गतप्राणास्तथा परे ॥
पृष्ठविन्यस्तवर्माणः सन्नद्धांस्तुरगांस्तथा ॥ 23 ॥
कृत्वा विपादान्समरे निजघ्नुः सादिनां गणम् ॥
आरुह्य वर्मिणः केचिद्वेगाच्छत्रुरथान्रणे ॥ 24 ॥
सारथीन्विगतप्राणाम्̐श्चकुर्युद्धविशारदाः ॥
चिच्छिदुर्वारणेन्द्राणां करान्केचित्पदातिनः ॥ 25 ॥
केचिद्दशनविन्यस्तपादाश्चारुरुहुर्गजान् ॥
सादिनश्च तथा केचिद्विशिरस्कान्रणाजिरे ॥ 26 ॥
चक्रुः पदातिनो ध्माताः खड्गैराकाशसन्निभैः ॥
केचिच्च सादिनः प्रासैः पञ्च सप्त तथा शरान् ॥ 27 ॥
श्रेणीकृतान्वै बिभिदुः शिक्षया रणकोविदाः ॥
केचिच्छार्ङ्गधनुर्न्यस्तबाणजालाकुलीकृतान् ॥ 28 ॥
पदातीन्समरे चक्रुर्वायुवेगैस्तुरङ्गमैः ॥
सादिनश्च तथैवान्ये सादिभिः सह संगताः ॥ ॥ 29 ॥
1.188.m:
they uttered lion-roars that tore apart the enemy army. / Some, dragging each other by the hair, [striking] one another with swords,
fell dead to the earth; and others / bearing armor on their backs made armored steeds
footless in battle and slew hosts of horsemen. / Some armored men, skilled in warfare, having swiftly mounted the enemy's chariots in battle,
deprived the charioteers of life. / Some foot-soldiers severed the trunks of lordly elephants;
some climbed the elephants, placing their feet upon the tusks; / and some foot-soldiers, enraged, made horsemen
headless on the battle-field with swords resembling the sky. / And some horsemen, skilled in battle, by their training split
five or seven arrows lined up [in flight] with their javelins. / Some, on steeds swift as the wind, routed foot-soldiers in battle
who were bewildered by a dense net of arrows shot from horn-bows. / And other horsemen, joining battle with horsemen,

1.188.s:
darśayanto raṇe bhikṣāṃ cakruryuddhamanekadhā ..
kecitpāśāgranirbhinnahatasārathināyakāḥ .. 1.260.30 ..
vineduruccaiḥ sahasā siṃhanādaravānvanān ..
kuñjarairākulīkṛtya hayayānaviśāradāḥ .. 31 ..
vipucchahastānsamare cakruḥ sādigaṇānraṇe ..
nihataṃ va śaravrātaiḥ pādātaṃ bahudhā raṇe..32..
rathibhirbhāti bhūpāla kamalotkarasannibham ..
turagāsturagārohā rathibhirvinipātitāḥ .. 33 ..
āvavrurvasudhāṃ tatra śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
rathināṃ rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ yuddhamāsītsudāruṇam ..34..
1.188.d:
दर्शयन्तो रणे भिक्षां चक्रुर्युद्धमनेकधा ॥
केचित्पाशाग्रनिर्भिन्नहतसारथिनायकाः ॥ 1.260.30 ॥
विनेदुरुच्चैः सहसा सिंहनादरवान्वनान् ॥
कुञ्जरैराकुलीकृत्य हययानविशारदाः ॥ 31 ॥
विपुच्छहस्तान्समरे चक्रुः सादिगणान्रणे ॥
निहतं व शरव्रातैः पादातं बहुधा रणे॥32॥
रथिभिर्भाति भूपाल कमलोत्करसन्निभम् ॥
तुरगास्तुरगारोहा रथिभिर्विनिपातिताः ॥ 33 ॥
आवव्रुर्वसुधां तत्र शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
रथिनां रथिभिः सार्धं युद्धमासीत्सुदारुणम् ॥34॥
1.188.m:
fought in many ways, begging no quarter in battle. / Some, whose driver-commanders were pierced and slain by noose-points,
suddenly bellowed loudly with wild lion-roars. / Those skilled in horsemanship, throwing [the enemy] into confusion with elephants,
deprived the hosts of riders in battle of tails and hands. / The infantry slain in many ways in the battle by swarms of arrows
by chariot-warriors shone like an expanse of lotuses, O ruler of the earth. / Horses and horse-riders struck down by chariot-warriors
covered the earth there by hundreds and thousands. / A dreadful battle took place between chariot-warriors and chariot-warriors,

1.188.s:
bāṇatomarapātaiśca gadākampanamudgaraiḥ ..
rathināṃ ca mahadyuddhamāsītkuñjaradhūrgataiḥ ..35..
1.188.d:
बाणतोमरपातैश्च गदाकम्पनमुद्गरैः ॥
रथिनां च महद्युद्धमासीत्कुञ्जरधूर्गतैः ॥35॥
1.188.m: with showers of arrows and javelins, and clubs, mallets, and hammers. / And a great battle took place between chariot-warriors and elephant-riders.

1.188.s:
prāsabāṇamahāpāta durnirīkṣyaṃ samantataḥ ..
nihataṃ bahu pādātaṃ kuñjaraistatra dṛśyate..36..
1.188.d:
प्रासबाणमहापात दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ततः ॥
निहतं बहु पादातं कुञ्जरैस्तत्र दृश्यते॥36॥
1.188.m: Dreadful to behold on all sides with the heavy shower of barbed darts and arrows, / many infantrymen were seen there slaughtered by elephants.

1.188.s:
raṇe nṛpatiśārdūla vinikīrṇaṃ sahasradhā ..
sādināṃ saturaṅgāṇāṃ sumahatkadanaṃ kṛtam .. 37 ..
1.188.d:
रणे नृपतिशार्दूल विनिकीर्णं सहस्रधा ॥
सादिनां सतुरङ्गाणां सुमहत्कदनं कृतम् ॥ 37 ॥
1.188.m: Scattered in thousands on the battlefield, O tiger among kings, / an immense destruction was wrought upon horsemen along with their mounts.

1.188.s:
mahāmātrapramuditaiḥ kuñjarairbaladarpitaiḥ ..
ākramya rathavṛndāni cūrṇitāni turaṅgamaiḥ..38..
1.188.d:
महामात्रप्रमुदितैः कुञ्जरैर्बलदर्पितैः ॥
आक्रम्य रथवृन्दानि चूर्णितानि तुरङ्गमैः॥38॥
1.188.m: By elephants, puffed up with strength, whose mahouts rejoiced, / assaulting hosts of chariots, and crushed by horses,

1.188.s:
vyadṛśyanta mahārāja viprakīrṇāni bhūtale..
evaṃ madhyāhnasamaye tīkṣṇaṃ tapati bhāskare .. 39 ..
1.188.d:
व्यदृश्यन्त महाराज विप्रकीर्णानि भूतले॥
एवं मध्याह्नसमये तीक्ष्णं तपति भास्करे ॥ 39 ॥
1.188.m: they were seen, O great king, strewn across the surface of the earth. / Thus, at the hour of midday, while the sun blazed fiercely,

1.188.s:
babhūvākulasaṃgrāmaṃ ghoraṃ rudhirakardamam ..
rathāśvakuñjaraiḥ sārdhaṃ pattayaśca samāgatāḥ .. 1.260.40 ..
1.188.d:
बभूवाकुलसंग्रामं घोरं रुधिरकर्दमम् ॥
रथाश्वकुञ्जरैः सार्धं पत्तयश्च समागताः ॥ 1.260.40 ॥
1.188.m: a confused, frightful battle arose, muddy with blood. / Foot-soldiers met together with chariots, horses, and elephants,

1.188.s:
kuñjarāśca mahākāyā pattyaśvarathinastathā ..
pattibhiśca padātīnāṃ sādināṃ saha sādibhiḥ .. 41 ..
1.188.d:
कुञ्जराश्च महाकाया पत्त्यश्वरथिनस्तथा ॥
पत्तिभिश्च पदातीनां सादिनां सह सादिभिः ॥ 41 ॥
1.188.m: as well as gigantic elephants, infantry, cavalry, and charioteers; / and foot-soldiers with foot-soldiers, horsemen with horsemen,

1.188.s:
rathināṃ rathibhiryuddhaṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca kuñjaraiḥ ..
babhūva rājam̐stumule saṃgrāme śoṇitodake .. 42 ..
1.188.d:
रथिनां रथिभिर्युद्धं कुञ्जराणां च कुञ्जरैः ॥
बभूव राजम्̐स्तुमुले संग्रामे शोणितोदके ॥ 42 ॥
1.188.m: charioteers fought with charioteers, and elephants with elephants, / in that tumultuous battle, O king, where the water was blood,

1.188.s:
śūrāṇāṃ raṇalubdhānāmamarṣākrāntacetasām ..
pattinā nihataḥ sādī gajena nihato naraḥ .. 43 ..
1.188.d:
शूराणां रणलुब्धानाममर्षाक्रान्तचेतसाम् ॥
पत्तिना निहतः सादी गजेन निहतो नरः ॥ 43 ॥
1.188.m: between heroes eager for battle whose minds were overcome with rage. / A horseman was slain by an infantryman, a man was slain by an elephant;

1.188.s:
rathinā nihato nāgaḥ kvacidāsīdaghātitaḥ ..
hatāḥ padātibhiścānye vyadṛśyanta raṇājire .. 44 ..
1.188.d:
रथिना निहतो नागः क्वचिदासीदघातितः ॥
हताः पदातिभिश्चान्ये व्यदृश्यन्त रणाजिरे ॥ 44 ॥
1.188.m: an elephant was slain by a charioteer, and elsewhere lay unhurt; / and others were seen slain by foot-soldiers upon the field of battle.

1.188.s:
padātirathanāgāśca sādibhirvinipātitāḥ ..
rathanāgahayā yuddhe nihatāśca padātibhiḥ .. 45 ..
1.188.d:
पदातिरथनागाश्च सादिभिर्विनिपातिताः ॥
रथनागहया युद्धे निहताश्च पदातिभिः ॥ 45 ॥
1.188.m: Foot-soldiers, chariots, and elephants were struck down by horsemen, / and chariots, elephants, and horses were slain in the fight by foot-soldiers.

1.188.s:
nareṇa ca hato hastī śūreṇa kṛtabuddhinā ..
sādinā ca hato hastī sādī caiva padātinā ..46..
1.188.d:
नरेण च हतो हस्ती शूरेण कृतबुद्धिना ॥
सादिना च हतो हस्ती सादी चैव पदातिना ॥46॥
1.188.m: An elephant was killed by a resolute heroic man, / an elephant was killed by a horseman, and a horseman by an infantryman.

1.188.s:
rathinā ca hataḥ pattiḥ pattinā ca hato rathī ..
rathinā nihataḥ sādī saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe .. 47 ..
1.188.d:
रथिना च हतः पत्तिः पत्तिना च हतो रथी ॥
रथिना निहतः सादी संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे ॥ 47 ॥
1.188.m: An infantryman was killed by a charioteer, and a charioteer was killed by an infantryman; / a horseman was slain by a charioteer in that hair-raising battle.

1.188.s:
reṇunā ca diśo vyāptāstumule bhṛśasaṃkule ..
vyarājanta mahārāja samare gatajīvitāḥ .. 48 ..
1.188.d:
रेणुना च दिशो व्याप्तास्तुमुले भृशसंकुले ॥
व्यराजन्त महाराज समरे गतजीविताः ॥ 48 ॥
1.188.m: The directions were filled with dust in that tumultuous, exceedingly dense melee; / the dead lay glorious, O great king, on the battlefield.

1.188.s:
patatāṃ bāṇajālānāṃ dhanuṣāṃ caiva kūjatām ..
mudgarāṇāṃ bhuśuṇḍīnāṃ tomarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ..49..
1.188.d:
पततां बाणजालानां धनुषां चैव कूजताम् ॥
मुद्गराणां भुशुण्डीनां तोमराणां तथैव च ॥49॥
1.188.m: Of falling flights of arrows and twanging bows, / of mallets, bhuśuṇḍi-catapults, and javelins,

1.188.s:
paṭṭiśānāṃ ca ṛṣṭīnāṃ kṣepaṇānāṃ ca yādava ..
ayoguḍānāṃ prāsānāṃ carmaṇāmatha varmaṇām .. 1.260.50 ..
1.188.d:
पट्टिशानां च ऋष्टीनां क्षेपणानां च यादव ॥
अयोगुडानां प्रासानां चर्मणामथ वर्मणाम् ॥ 1.260.50 ॥
1.188.m: of broad axes, spears, and slings, O Yādava, / of iron balls, barbed darts, shields, and armours,

1.188.s:
aniśaṃ śrūyate śabdo ghorastasminraṇājire ..
hayaiśca vigatārohairdhāvamānairitastataḥ .. 51 ..
1.188.d:
अनिशं श्रूयते शब्दो घोरस्तस्मिन्रणाजिरे ॥
हयैश्च विगतारोहैर्धावमानैरितस्ततः ॥ 51 ॥
1.188.m: a dreadful sound was heard unceasingly on that battleground. / With horses riderless, running this way and that,

1.188.s:
bhagneṣākūbarākṣaiśca rathairvigatanāyakaiḥ ..
chinnadantaiśca mātaṅgairbhinnakumbhaghaṭānanaiḥ 52 ..
1.188.d:
भग्नेषाकूबराक्षैश्च रथैर्विगतनायकैः ॥
छिन्नदन्तैश्च मातङ्गैर्भिन्नकुम्भघटाननैः 52 ॥
1.188.m: with chariots lacking masters, their poles, yokes, and axles broken, / and with elephants whose tusks were snapped and frontal globes smashed open,

1.188.s:
latāveṣṭita vṛkṣābhaiḥ śobhāṃ yāti raṇājiram ..
kuñjarairvigatārohaistrāsitairdṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ .. 53 ..
1.188.d:
लतावेष्टित वृक्षाभैः शोभां याति रणाजिरम् ॥
कुञ्जरैर्विगतारोहैस्त्रासितैर्दृढधन्विभिः ॥ 53 ॥
1.188.m: the field of battle attained a beauty like that of trees entwined with creepers; / with riderless elephants, terrified by sturdy archers,

1.188.s:
mardyamānāni sainyāni śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ..
bhinnānsudantaiḥ puruṣāndantāsaktāṃstathā gajāḥ..54..
1.188.d:
मर्द्यमानानि सैन्यानि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
भिन्नान्सुदन्तैः पुरुषान्दन्तासक्तांस्तथा गजाः॥54॥
1.188.m: armies were trampled down by hundreds and thousands. / Bearing men impaled upon their fine tusks and clung to their teeth,

1.188.s:
vahamānā vyarājanta karṇavyajanavījitāḥ ..
lagnāntrajālairdaśanairdantinaḥ parvatopamāḥ..55..
1.188.d:
वहमाना व्यराजन्त कर्णव्यजनवीजिताः ॥
लग्नान्त्रजालैर्दशनैर्दन्तिनः पर्वतोपमाः॥55॥
1.188.m: the mountain-like elephants shone as they were fanned by their ear-fans, / their tusks caught in nets of entrails;

1.188.s:
latāveṣṭitavṛkṣābhaiḥ śobhayanti raṇājiram ..
tasmim̐stathāvidhe raudre saṃgrāme ghoradarśane ..56..
1.188.d:
लतावेष्टितवृक्षाभैः शोभयन्ति रणाजिरम् ॥
तस्मिम्̐स्तथाविधे रौद्रे संग्रामे घोरदर्शने ॥56॥
1.188.m: resembling trees entwined with creepers, they adorned the field of battle. / In such a terrible battle, dreadful to behold,

1.188.s:
narāśvanāgarudhirairvisasruḥ śoṇitāpagāḥ ..
khaḍgamīnā mahāchatrarājahaṃsavibhūṣitāḥ ..
yodhamastakapāṣāṇāḥ keśaśaivālabhūṣaṇāḥ..57..
1.188.d:
नराश्वनागरुधिरैर्विसस्रुः शोणितापगाः ॥
खड्गमीना महाछत्रराजहंसविभूषिताः ॥
योधमस्तकपाषाणाः केशशैवालभूषणाः॥57॥
1.188.m: rivers of blood flowed with the blood of men, horses, and elephants, / with swords for fish, adorned with great parasols for royal swans, / with the heads of warriors for stones, and hair for their mossy ornaments,

1.188.s:
mahāphenaughavatyaśca bhītānāṃ bhayavardhanāḥ ..
tāstaranti tadā yodhāḥ śūrā jayadhanaiṣiṇaḥ..58..
1.188.d:
महाफेनौघवत्यश्च भीतानां भयवर्धनाः ॥
तास्तरन्ति तदा योधाः शूरा जयधनैषिणः॥58॥
1.188.m: having great masses of foam, increasing the terror of the frightened. / The brave warriors, longing for the wealth of victory, then crossed them,

1.188.s:
rājanvāhananaubhiste vyavasāyaparasparāḥ ..
chinnāni svāni gātrāṇi na jānanti raṇe paraiḥ .. 59 ..
1.188.d:
राजन्वाहननौभिस्ते व्यवसायपरस्पराः ॥
छिन्नानि स्वानि गात्राणि न जानन्ति रणे परैः ॥ 59 ॥
1.188.m: O king, using mounts as boats, intent upon one another; / in the fight, they did not even know that their own limbs had been severed by their foes.

1.188.s:
tatra śūrā mahābhāgāstvamarṣākrāntacetasaḥ ..
āyudhakṣayamāsādya muṣṭiyuddhāni cakrire .. 1.260.60 ..
1.188.d:
तत्र शूरा महाभागास्त्वमर्षाक्रान्तचेतसः ॥
आयुधक्षयमासाद्य मुष्टियुद्धानि चक्रिरे ॥ 1.260.60 ॥
1.188.m: There, the illustrious heroes, their minds overcome with rage, / having exhausted their weapons, engaged in fist-fights.

1.188.s:
keśākeśi tathā keciddantādanti nakhānakhi ..
cakruryuddhaṃ mahārāja brahmalokajigīṣavaḥ ..61 ..
1.188.d:
केशाकेशि तथा केचिद्दन्तादन्ति नखानखि ॥
चक्रुर्युद्धं महाराज ब्रह्मलोकजिगीषवः ॥61 ॥
1.188.m: Some fought hair-to-hair, tooth-to-tooth, nail-to-nail, / O great king, striving to conquer the world of Brahmā.

1.188.s:
krandanto'nye pitṝnputrānbhrātṝnanye pitāmahān ..
mātulānbhāgineyāṃśca syālānsambandhinastathā .. 62..
1.188.d:
क्रन्दन्तोऽन्ये पितॄन्पुत्रान्भ्रातॄनन्ये पितामहान् ॥
मातुलान्भागिनेयांश्च स्यालान्सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥ 62॥
1.188.m: Others were crying out for fathers, sons, and brothers, others for grandfathers, / for maternal uncles, nephews, brothers-in-law, and kinsmen,

1.188.s:
pitṛvyānāryakānanye dauhitrānapare tathā ..
dhāvantyanye patantyanye garjantyanye jigīṣayā .. 63 ..
1.188.d:
पितृव्यानार्यकानन्ये दौहित्रानपरे तथा ॥
धावन्त्यन्ये पतन्त्यन्ये गर्जन्त्यन्ये जिगीषया ॥ 63 ॥
1.188.m: others for paternal uncles, grandfathers, and daughters' sons; / some were running, others were falling, others were roaring in their desire for victory,

1.188.s:
svanantyanye patantyanye mriyante cāpare tathā ..
śocantyanye tathā bandhūñśocyāstvanye tu bandhubhiḥ .. 64 ..
1.188.d:
स्वनन्त्यन्ये पतन्त्यन्ये म्रियन्ते चापरे तथा ॥
शोचन्त्यन्ये तथा बन्धूञ्शोच्यास्त्वन्ये तु बन्धुभिः ॥ 64 ॥
1.188.m: others were groaning, others were falling, and others were dying; / some were grieving for their relatives, while others were grieved for by their kin.

1.188.s:
yācante'nye mahārāja tṛṣṇārttāśca tathā jalam ..
vāhaneṣu samāropya nīyantyanye ca bandhubhiḥ .. 65 ..
1.188.d:
याचन्तेऽन्ये महाराज तृष्णार्त्ताश्च तथा जलम् ॥
वाहनेषु समारोप्य नीयन्त्यन्ये च बन्धुभिः ॥ 65 ॥
1.188.m: Others, afflicted with thirst, begged for water, O great king, / and others were placed upon mounts and carried away by their kinsmen

1.188.s:
śibirāya mahārāja śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
anye saṃvṛtya cātmānaṃ bhītā jagmurupahvaram .. 66 ..
1.188.d:
शिबिराय महाराज शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
अन्ये संवृत्य चात्मानं भीता जग्मुरुपह्वरम् ॥ 66 ॥
1.188.m: to the camp, O great king, by hundreds and thousands; / while others, terrified, concealing themselves, went into hiding.

1.188.s:
jalārthamanye ca narā bāndhavaiśca pracoditāḥ ..
āgamya dṛṣṭvā ca mṛtaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ bhaṅtvā vicukruśuḥ .. 67 ..
1.188.d:
जलार्थमन्ये च नरा बान्धवैश्च प्रचोदिताः ॥
आगम्य दृष्ट्वा च मृतं भाण्डं भङ्त्वा विचुक्रुशुः ॥ 67 ॥
1.188.m: Other men, urged by their kinsmen to fetch water, / returned, saw [the relative] dead, smashed the pot, and wailed aloud.

1.188.s:
hatabandhumanādṛtya svāmikāryaikatatparāḥ ..
parānabhimukhāneva tatrāyudhyanta mānavāḥ .. 68 ..
1.188.d:
हतबन्धुमनादृत्य स्वामिकार्यैकतत्पराः ॥
परानभिमुखानेव तत्रायुध्यन्त मानवाः ॥ 68 ॥
1.188.m: Disregarding dead kin and devoted solely to their lord's business, / men fought there, facing their enemies head-on.

1.188.s:
yudhyatāmeva teṣāṃ tu śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
utthitāni gaṇe yāni kabandhāni mahīpate .. 69 ..
1.188.d:
युध्यतामेव तेषां तु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
उत्थितानि गणे यानि कबन्धानि महीपते ॥ 69 ॥
1.188.m: Even as they fought, hundreds and thousands of headless trunks / arose in the throng, O lord of the earth.

1.188.s:
kaścinnanarta samare kabandhastu dhanurdharaḥ ..
gadāpāṇistathaivānyaḥ khaḍgacarmadharo'paraḥ .. 1.260.70 ..
1.188.d:
कश्चिन्ननर्त समरे कबन्धस्तु धनुर्धरः ॥
गदापाणिस्तथैवान्यः खड्गचर्मधरोऽपरः ॥ 1.260.70 ॥
1.188.m: One headless trunk danced in the battle wielding a bow, / another with a mace in hand, another bearing a sword and shield,

1.188.s:
paraśvadhadharaḥ kaścitprāsapāṇistathā paraḥ ..
nṛtyatkabandhabhūyiṣṭhe devadundubhinādite .. 71 ..
1.188.d:
परश्वधधरः कश्चित्प्रासपाणिस्तथा परः ॥
नृत्यत्कबन्धभूयिष्ठे देवदुन्दुभिनादिते ॥ 71 ॥
1.188.m: one bearing an axe, and another with a barbed dart in hand. / In that battle teeming with dancing headless trunks, resounded by the drums of the gods,

1.188.s:
pravartamāne saṃgrāme śūrāṇāṃ svargalokade..
vyadṛśyanta mahārāja piśācā ghoradarśanāḥ ..72..
1.188.d:
प्रवर्तमाने संग्रामे शूराणां स्वर्गलोकदे॥
व्यदृश्यन्त महाराज पिशाचा घोरदर्शनाः ॥72॥
1.188.m: as it raged, bestowing the heavenly world upon heroes, / piśācas of dreadful appearance were seen, O great king,

1.188.s:
rākṣasāśca mahākāyāḥ kravyādāśca tathā pare ..
jagāma cāstaṃ savitā tadā raktavapurdharaḥ ..
saṃgrāmātsarvayodhānāṃ pītveva rudhiraṃ karaiḥ ..73..
1.188.d:
राक्षसाश्च महाकायाः क्रव्यादाश्च तथा परे ॥
जगाम चास्तं सविता तदा रक्तवपुर्धरः ॥
संग्रामात्सर्वयोधानां पीत्वेव रुधिरं करैः ॥73॥
1.188.m: as well as gigantic rākṣasas and other flesh-eaters. / Then the sun, bearing a blood-red body, went to his setting, / as if having drunk the blood of all the warriors from the battlefield with his rays.

1.188.s:
tato'staśailaṃ bhagavatyathārke gate japāpuṣpakadambakābhe ..
senādvayaṃ tacchibirāya yānaṃ kṛtvāvarohaṃ parabāṇataptam .. 74 ..
1.188.d:
ततोऽस्तशैलं भगवत्यथार्के गते जपापुष्पकदम्बकाभे ॥
सेनाद्वयं तच्छिबिराय यानं कृत्वावरोहं परबाणतप्तम् ॥ 74 ॥
1.188.m: Then, when the blessed sun, shining like a cluster of hibiscus flowers, had gone to the setting mountain, / the two armies made their way to camp, halting, scorched by enemy arrows.

1.189.s:
1.261
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
niśāvasāne gandharvāḥ kṛtvā vyūhaṃ sudurjayam ..
saṃpratīkṣyanta bharatamāyāntaṃ raṇakovidam .. 1 ..
1.189.d:
1.261
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
निशावसाने गन्धर्वाः कृत्वा व्यूहं सुदुर्जयम् ॥
संप्रतीक्ष्यन्त भरतमायान्तं रणकोविदम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.189.m:
1.261
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
At the end of the night, having formed an array that was very hard to conquer, / the gandharvas awaited Bharata, skilled in battle, as he approached.

1.189.s:
bharato'pi ca rātryante vajravyūhena daṃśitaḥ ..
āsasāda mahatsainyaṃ gandharvāṇāṃ sudurjayam ... 2 ..
1.189.d:
भरतोऽपि च रात्र्यन्ते वज्रव्यूहेन दंशितः ॥
आससाद महत्सैन्यं गन्धर्वाणां सुदुर्जयम् ॥। 2 ॥
1.189.m: Bharata too, at the end of the night, mail-clad, in a thunderbolt array, / approached the great, invincible army of the gandharvas.

1.189.s:
tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ yamarāṣṭravivarddhanam..
devāsurasamaprakhyaṃ trailokyabhayakārakama .. 3 ..
1.189.d:
ततः प्रववृते युद्धं यमराष्ट्रविवर्द्धनम्॥
देवासुरसमप्रख्यं त्रैलोक्यभयकारकम ॥ 3 ॥
1.189.m: Then a battle began, enlarging the realm of Yama, / resembling the battle of gods and demons, causing terror in the three worlds.

1.189.s:
pattīnāṃ pattibhiḥ sārdhaṃ sādināṃ caiva sādibhiḥ ..
rathināṃ rathibhiścaiva kuñjarāṇāṃ ca kuñjaraiḥ .. 4 ..
1.189.d:
पत्तीनां पत्तिभिः सार्धं सादिनां चैव सादिभिः ॥
रथिनां रथिभिश्चैव कुञ्जराणां च कुञ्जरैः ॥ 4 ॥
1.189.m: Foot-soldiers [fought] with foot-soldiers, and cavalry with cavalry, / chariot-warriors with chariot-warriors, and elephants with elephants.

1.189.s:
bhāṣatāṃ nāmagotrāṇi śūrāṇāṃ caiva garjatām ..
dhanuṣāṃ kūjatāṃ caiva śabdaḥ samabhavattadā .. 5 ..
1.189.d:
भाषतां नामगोत्राणि शूराणां चैव गर्जताम् ॥
धनुषां कूजतां चैव शब्दः समभवत्तदा ॥ 5 ॥
1.189.m: As the heroes proclaimed their names and lineages and roared, / and as bows twanged, a tumultuous sound arose then.

1.189.s:
tataḥ pravṛtte saṃgrāme bhāratiḥ puṣkaro raṇe ..
āsasāda viśālākṣaṃ gandharvaṃ raṇagarvitam .. 6 ..
1.189.d:
ततः प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे भारतिः पुष्करो रणे ॥
आससाद विशालाक्षं गन्धर्वं रणगर्वितम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.189.m: Then, when the battle had begun, Bharata's son Puṣkara in the fight / encountered Viśālākṣa, a Gandharva proud in battle.

1.189.s:
takṣaśca bhāratiḥ śrīmānyuyudhe vīrabāhunā ..
senānīrvijayaḥ śrīmānnamuciśca tamāgataḥ .. 7 ..
1.189.d:
तक्षश्च भारतिः श्रीमान्युयुधे वीरबाहुना ॥
सेनानीर्विजयः श्रीमान्नमुचिश्च तमागतः ॥ 7 ॥
1.189.m: And the glorious Takṣa, son of Bharata, fought with Vīrabāhu; / the glorious commander Vijaya and Namuci came together.

1.189.s:
bhūmanyuḥ kauravaḥ śrīmānkāmapālena saṃgataḥ ..
kirātarājo damanaścandrāpīḍena saṃgataḥ .. 8 ..
1.189.d:
भूमन्युः कौरवः श्रीमान्कामपालेन संगतः ॥
किरातराजो दमनश्चन्द्रापीडेन संगतः ॥ 8 ॥
1.189.m: The glorious Kaurava Bhūmanyu clashed with Kāmapāla; / the king of the Kirātas, Damana, clashed with Candrāpīḍa.

1.189.s:
prabhadrakeṇa śibinā tathaivājikaro raṇe ..
mahodayaḥ munirdeśo harikeśena saṃgataḥ .. 9 ..
1.189.d:
प्रभद्रकेण शिबिना तथैवाजिकरो रणे ॥
महोदयः मुनिर्देशो हरिकेशेन संगतः ॥ 9 ॥
1.189.m: Prabhadraka clashed with the Śibi, and likewise Ajikara in battle; / Mahodaya, king of the Munis, clashed with Harikeśa.

1.189.s:
traigarto vasudānaśca sūryaraśmiśca saṃgatau ..
gandharvaḥ kumudāpīḍaḥ kulūtādhipatirjayaḥ .. 1.261.10 ..
1.189.d:
त्रैगर्तो वसुदानश्च सूर्यरश्मिश्च संगतौ ॥
गन्धर्वः कुमुदापीडः कुलूताधिपतिर्जयः ॥ 1.261.10 ॥
1.189.m: Vasudāna from Trigarta and Sūryaraśmi clashed together; / the Gandharva Kumudāpīḍa and Jaya, lord of Kulūta, [clashed].

1.189.s:
cakratustumulaṃ yuddhaṃ devāsurasamaṃ tadā ..
dāśerakastathā rājā yavano vāśanaḥ paraḥ .. 11 ..
1.189.d:
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं युद्धं देवासुरसमं तदा ॥
दाशेरकस्तथा राजा यवनो वाशनः परः ॥ 11 ॥
1.189.m: They fought a tumultuous battle then, equal to that of the gods and Asuras; / likewise the Dāśeraka king and the foe Yavana Vāśana [clashed].

1.189.s:
ekalavyaśca saṃgrāme tenāsītsumahātmanā ..
kumudaḥ śoṇimā śūro balabandhuḥ suyodhanaḥ .. 12 ..
1.189.d:
एकलव्यश्च संग्रामे तेनासीत्सुमहात्मना ॥
कुमुदः शोणिमा शूरो बलबन्धुः सुयोधनः ॥ 12 ॥
1.189.m: And Ekalavya [fought] in battle with that great-souled one; / Kumuda, Śoṇiman, the heroic Balabandhu, and Suyodhana—

1.189.s:
gandharvaiḥ pañcabhiḥ pañca pārvatīyāḥ samāgatāḥ ..
balākābalakābhyāṃ tu gadinā maulinā tathā .. 10 ..
1.189.d:
गन्धर्वैः पञ्चभिः पञ्च पार्वतीयाः समागताः ॥
बलाकाबलकाभ्यां तु गदिना मौलिना तथा ॥ 10 ॥
1.189.m: five mountaineers clashed with five Gandharvas; / and by Balāka and Abalaka, by the mace-bearer, and by Maulika,

1.189.s:
kumudena tu vīreṇa sadasīṣvanivarttinā ..
madrarājoṃ'śumānnāma caturbhiḥ saṃgato raṇe .. 14 ..
1.189.d:
कुमुदेन तु वीरेण सदसीष्वनिवर्त्तिना ॥
मद्रराजोंऽशुमान्नाम चतुर्भिः संगतो रणे ॥ 14 ॥
1.189.m: and by the hero Kumuda who never retreats before arrows, / the king of Madra named Aṃśumat was engaged in battle by these four.

1.189.s:
bhīmanādamahānādavasuṣeṇagajākaraiḥ ..
dārvaḥ śrutañjanaḥ śrīmānabhimānaḥ kṛtañjayaḥ .. 15 ..
1.189.d:
भीमनादमहानादवसुषेणगजाकरैः ॥
दार्वः श्रुतञ्जनः श्रीमानभिमानः कृतञ्जयः ॥ 15 ॥
1.189.m: With Bhīmanāda, Mahānāda, Vasuṣeṇa, and Gajākāra, / the glorious Darva king Śrutañjana, Abhimāna, and Kṛtañjaya—

1.189.s:
yuddhaṃ tau cakraturghoraṃ sahitau candravarmaṇā..
kāśmīrakaḥ subāhuśca gandharveṇa subāhunā .. 16 ..
1.189.d:
युद्धं तौ चक्रतुर्घोरं सहितौ चन्द्रवर्मणा॥
काश्मीरकः सुबाहुश्च गन्धर्वेण सुबाहुना ॥ 16 ॥
1.189.m: the two of them, joined with Candravarman, fought a dreadful battle. / The Kaśmīran Subāhu and the Gandharva Subāhu

1.189.s:
cakāra tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavarddhanam ..
bharatasyāparaṃ yodhā gandharvaibhīmavikramaiḥ .. 17 ..
1.189.d:
चकार तुमुलं युद्धं भीरूणां भयवर्द्धनम् ॥
भरतस्यापरं योधा गन्धर्वैभीमविक्रमैः ॥ 17 ॥
1.189.m: fought a tumultuous battle that increased the terror of the timid. / Other warriors of Bharata, with Gandharvas of terrible valour,

1.189.s:
samāgatāstadā yuddhe śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
bharataśca mahātejāḥ śailūṣeṇa samāgataḥ .. 18 ..
1.189.d:
समागतास्तदा युद्धे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
भरतश्च महातेजाः शैलूषेण समागतः ॥ 18 ॥
1.189.m: clashed then in battle by hundreds and by thousands; / and Bharata, of great splendour, clashed with Śailūṣa.

1.189.s:
cakāra tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvabhūtabhayaṅkaram ..
parvatābhena nāgena tridhā prasravatā madam .. 19 ..
1.189.d:
चकार तुमुलं युद्धं सर्वभूतभयङ्करम् ॥
पर्वताभेन नागेन त्रिधा प्रस्रवता मदम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.189.m: He fought a tumultuous battle that terrified all beings. / [Mounted] on an elephant resembling a mountain, trickling musth in three streams,

1.189.s:
bādhamānamarīnsaṃkhye mahendramiva dānavān ..
viśālo varayāmāsa rathenābhyetya puṣkaram..1.261.20 ..
1.189.d:
बाधमानमरीन्संख्ये महेन्द्रमिव दानवान् ॥
विशालो वरयामास रथेनाभ्येत्य पुष्करम्॥1.261.20 ॥
1.189.m: afflicting his enemies in battle as great Indra does the Dānavas, / Viśāla, coming up on his chariot, checked Puṣkara.

1.189.s:
bāṇaughena raṇe bhittvā vegaṃ puṣkaradantinaḥ ..
puṣkaraṃ tāḍayāmāsa nārācairbahubhistadā .. 21 ..
1.189.d:
बाणौघेन रणे भित्त्वा वेगं पुष्करदन्तिनः ॥
पुष्करं ताडयामास नाराचैर्बहुभिस्तदा ॥ 21 ॥
1.189.m: Having checked the charge of Puṣkara's elephant with a flood of arrows in battle, / he struck Puṣkara then with many iron shafts.

1.189.s:
ripubhistāḍyamānastu bhāratirbhīmavikramaḥ ..
vavarṣa śarasaṃghātairviśālaṃ senayā saha .. 22 ..
1.189.d:
रिपुभिस्ताड्यमानस्तु भारतिर्भीमविक्रमः ॥
ववर्ष शरसंघातैर्विशालं सेनया सह ॥ 22 ॥
1.189.m: Being struck by enemies, Bharata's son of terrible valour / showered Viśāla along with his army with clouds of arrows.

1.189.s:
puṣkarasya viśālo'tha madhye ciccheda kārmukam ..
chinnadhanvā viśālasya sa jaghānātha sārathim .. 23 ..
1.189.d:
पुष्करस्य विशालोऽथ मध्ये चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् ॥
छिन्नधन्वा विशालस्य स जघानाथ सारथिम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.189.m: Then Viśāla severed Puṣkara's bow in the middle; / his bow broken, he then struck down Viśāla's charioteer.

1.189.s:
ākramya yodhayāmāsa viśālasya mahāratham ..
yadā raṇe mahārāja puṣkarasya rathottamam .. 24 ..
1.189.d:
आक्रम्य योधयामास विशालस्य महारथम् ॥
यदा रणे महाराज पुष्करस्य रथोत्तमम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.189.m: Attacking, he fought against Viśāla's great chariot. / O great king, when in battle he [attacked] Puṣkara's excellent chariot,

1.189.s:
hantuṃ sa rathamutsṛjya viśālopi mahīpateḥ ..
gadayā yodhayāmāsa puṣkarasya tu vāraṇam .. 25 ..
1.189.d:
हन्तुं स रथमुत्सृज्य विशालोपि महीपतेः ॥
गदया योधयामास पुष्करस्य तु वारणम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.189.m: in order to slay [him], Viśāla too abandoned the king's chariot / and fought against Puṣkara's elephant with a mace.

1.189.s:
puṣkaro'pi gadāpāṇirviśālābhimukhaṃ yayau ..
gadābhistau tato vīrau parasparajigīṣayā .. 26 ..
1.189.d:
पुष्करोऽपि गदापाणिर्विशालाभिमुखं ययौ ॥
गदाभिस्तौ ततो वीरौ परस्परजिगीषया ॥ 26 ॥
1.189.m: Puṣkara also, mace in hand, advanced facing Viśāla; / then those two heroes, wishing to conquer each other with maces,

1.189.s:
savyadakṣiṇatastatra maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ ..
prajahratustathānyonyamanyonyasya vadhaiṣiṇau .. 27 ..
1.189.d:
सव्यदक्षिणतस्तत्र मण्डलानि विचेरतुः ॥
प्रजह्रतुस्तथान्योन्यमन्योन्यस्य वधैषिणौ ॥ 27 ॥
1.189.m: moved in circles to the left and to the right there; / each seeking to kill the other, they struck each other.

1.189.s:
puṣkareṇa raṇe yogādviśālasya gadā hatā ..
mumoca pāvakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sasphuliṅgaṃ mahīpate .. 28 ..
1.189.d:
पुष्करेण रणे योगाद्विशालस्य गदा हता ॥
मुमोच पावकं तीक्ष्णं सस्फुलिङ्गं महीपते ॥ 28 ॥
1.189.m: By Puṣkara's skill in battle, Viśāla's mace was struck; / it emitted fierce fire with sparks, O lord of the earth!

1.189.s:
viśālena tato yuddhe gadayā puṣkaro hataḥ ..
himavatsannikāśastu na cacāla padātpadam ..29..
1.189.d:
विशालेन ततो युद्धे गदया पुष्करो हतः ॥
हिमवत्सन्निकाशस्तु न चचाल पदात्पदम् ॥29॥
1.189.m: Then in the fight Puṣkara was struck by Viśāla with his mace; / yet, resembling the Himavat, he did not stir a single step.

1.189.s:
puṣkareṇa mahārāja viśālo gadayā hataḥ ..
tataḥ śailūṣavacanānmahāmātrapracoditam .. 1.261.30 ..
1.189.d:
पुष्करेण महाराज विशालो गदया हतः ॥
ततः शैलूषवचनान्महामात्रप्रचोदितम् ॥ 1.261.30 ॥
1.189.m: Viśāla was struck with the mace by Puṣkara, O great king; / then, at Śailūṣa's word, urged by an elephant-driver,

1.189.s:
āruroha mahānāgaṃ viśālo raṇadarpitaḥ ..
āruroha rathaṃ śrīmāngandharvasya ca puṣkaraḥ .. 31 ..
1.189.d:
आरुरोह महानागं विशालो रणदर्पितः ॥
आरुरोह रथं श्रीमान्गन्धर्वस्य च पुष्करः ॥ 31 ॥
1.189.m: Viśāla, proud in battle, mounted a great elephant; / and the glorious Puṣkara mounted the chariot of the Gandharva.

1.189.s:
tāvekarathamārūḍho tadā rājendrapuṣkarau ..
nijaghnaturviśālasya saṃgrāme varavāraṇam .. 32 ..
1.189.d:
तावेकरथमारूढो तदा राजेन्द्रपुष्करौ ॥
निजघ्नतुर्विशालस्य संग्रामे वरवारणम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.189.m: Both having mounted a single chariot then, the king and Puṣkara / struck down Viśāla's excellent elephant in battle.

1.189.s:
yasyāvarji tan sya kuñjarānnipatiṣyataḥ ..
cicchedātha viśālasya śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam.. 33 ..
1.189.d:
यस्यावर्जि तन् स्य कुञ्जरान्निपतिष्यतः ॥
चिच्छेदाथ विशालस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम्॥ 33 ॥
1.189.m: When he, thrown off, was about to fall from his elephant, / [Puṣkara] then severed Viśāla's head adorned with glittering earrings.

1.189.s:
hatvā viśālaṃ saṃgrāme rathamāruhya cāparam ..
chādayāmāsa tatsainyaṃ gandharvāṇāṃ śarotkaraiḥ .. 34 ..
1.189.d:
हत्वा विशालं संग्रामे रथमारुह्य चापरम् ॥
छादयामास तत्सैन्यं गन्धर्वाणां शरोत्करैः ॥ 34 ॥
1.189.m: Having slain Viśāla in battle and mounting another chariot, / he covered that army of the Gandharvas with showers of arrows.

1.189.s:
viśālaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā ruhaḥ paramakopanaḥ ..
sādī jaghāna prāsena gāndhāraṃ raṇagarvitam.. 35 ..
1.189.d:
विशालं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रुहः परमकोपनः ॥
सादी जघान प्रासेन गान्धारं रणगर्वितम्॥ 35 ॥
1.189.m: Seeing Viśāla slain, Ruha, exceedingly enraged, / being a horseman, struck the Gāndhāra hero proud in battle with a dart.

1.189.s:
tasya ciccheda gāndhāraḥ saprāsaṃ tu bhujadvayam ..
śiraśca saśirastrāṇaṃ kṣurapreṇa mahīpate .. 36 ..
1.189.d:
तस्य चिच्छेद गान्धारः सप्रासं तु भुजद्वयम् ॥
शिरश्च सशिरस्त्राणं क्षुरप्रेण महीपते ॥ 36 ॥
1.189.m: The Gāndhāra severed his two arms together with the dart, / and his head together with the helmet using a razor-sharp arrow, O lord of the earth.

1.189.s:
takṣo rathena śubhreṇa kiṅkiṇījālamālinā ..
āsasāda mahābāhuṃ vīrabāhuṃ raṇājire .. 37 ..
1.189.d:
तक्षो रथेन शुभ्रेण किङ्किणीजालमालिना ॥
आससाद महाबाहुं वीरबाहुं रणाजिरे ॥ 37 ॥
1.189.m: Takṣa, on a bright chariot adorned with garlands of little bells, / encountered the mighty-armed Vīrabāhu on the battlefield.

1.189.s:
ekacchāya ivākāśastayorāsīccharotkaraiḥ ..
na vāti pavanastatra na vibhrājati bhāskaraḥ .. 38 ..
1.189.d:
एकच्छाय इवाकाशस्तयोरासीच्छरोत्करैः ॥
न वाति पवनस्तत्र न विभ्राजति भास्करः ॥ 38 ॥
1.189.m: The sky became as if a single shade from their showers of arrows; / no wind blew there, and the sun did not shine.

1.189.s:
takṣaḥ sapuṅkhamākṛṣya bāṇaṃ bhāskaraprabham ..
ciccheda sārathestasya śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam .. 39 ..
1.189.d:
तक्षः सपुङ्खमाकृष्य बाणं भास्करप्रभम् ॥
चिच्छेद सारथेस्तस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.189.m: Takṣa, drawing an arrow, feathered and radiant as the sun, / severed the head of his charioteer adorned with glittering earrings.

1.189.s:
niryantṛṇā rathenāsau samarādapavāhitaḥ ..
tasminraṇājirānnīte takṣaṃ kuñjaradhūrgataḥ .. 1.261.40 ..
1.189.d:
निर्यन्तृणा रथेनासौ समरादपवाहितः ॥
तस्मिन्रणाजिरान्नीते तक्षं कुञ्जरधूर्गतः ॥ 1.261.40 ॥
1.189.m: He was carried away from the battle by his driverless chariot; / when he was borne away from the battlefield, mounted on the front of an elephant,

1.189.s:
ājagāma mahārāja gandharvastu sudarśanaḥ ..
tasyāpatitamātrasya śareṇa nataparvaṇā .. 41 ..
1.189.d:
आजगाम महाराज गन्धर्वस्तु सुदर्शनः ॥
तस्यापतितमात्रस्य शरेण नतपर्वणा ॥ 41 ॥
1.189.m: the Gandharva Sudarśana advanced against Takṣa, O great king; / as soon as he rushed forward, with an arrow of bent joints,

1.189.s:
ciccheda nāgamūrdhānaṃ bhāratirbhīmavikramaḥ ..
senānīrvijayaḥ śrīmānnamuciśca samāgatau .. 42 ..
1.189.d:
चिच्छेद नागमूर्धानं भारतिर्भीमविक्रमः ॥
सेनानीर्विजयः श्रीमान्नमुचिश्च समागतौ ॥ 42 ॥
1.189.m: Bharata's son of terrible valour severed the elephant's head. / The glorious commander Vijaya and Namuci came together;

1.189.s:
sārathiṃ turagānketumadṛśyaṃ cakratuḥ śaraiḥ ..
anyo'nyasya mahārāja samare bhīmavikramau .. 43 ..
1.189.d:
सारथिं तुरगान्केतुमदृश्यं चक्रतुः शरैः ॥
अन्योऽन्यस्य महाराज समरे भीमविक्रमौ ॥ 43 ॥
1.189.m: they made each other's charioteer, horses, and standard invisible / with arrows in battle, O great king, both of terrible valour.

1.189.s:
caturbhiḥ sāyakairhatvā namuceḥ sa turaṅgamān ..
pañcamena śiraḥ kāyājjahāra rathasāratheḥ .. 44 ..
1.189.d:
चतुर्भिः सायकैर्हत्वा नमुचेः स तुरङ्गमान् ॥
पञ्चमेन शिरः कायाज्जहार रथसारथेः ॥ 44 ॥
1.189.m: Having killed Namuci's horses with four arrows, / with a fifth he took the chariot-driver's head from his body.

1.189.s:
namucirvirathaḥ khaḍgamādāya paravīrahā ..
jagāmābhimukhastūrṇaṃ senāpatimarindama .. 45 ..
1.189.d:
नमुचिर्विरथः खड्गमादाय परवीरहा ॥
जगामाभिमुखस्तूर्णं सेनापतिमरिन्दम ॥ 45 ॥
1.189.m: Namuci, deprived of his chariot, taking up a sword, that slayer of enemy heroes, / quickly advanced facing the general, O tamer of foes.

1.189.s:
vegenāpatatastasya cakramādāya bhāsvaram ..
vivṛttākṣantu ciccheda tasya mūrdhānamañjasā .. 46 ..
1.189.d:
वेगेनापततस्तस्य चक्रमादाय भास्वरम् ॥
विवृत्ताक्षन्तु चिच्छेद तस्य मूर्धानमञ्जसा ॥ 46 ॥
1.189.m: As he rushed on with speed, taking up a radiant discus, / he swiftly severed his head with wide-open eyes.

1.189.s:
bhūmanyuḥ kāmapālaśca cakraturyuddhamuttamama ..
yathā devāsure yuddhe balaśakrau mahābalī .. 47 ..
1.189.d:
भूमन्युः कामपालश्च चक्रतुर्युद्धमुत्तमम ॥
यथा देवासुरे युद्धे बलशक्रौ महाबली ॥ 47 ॥
1.189.m: Bhūmanyu and Kāmapāla fought a superb battle, / just as Bala and Śakra, of great might, did in the war between gods and Asuras.

1.189.s:
tāvubhau kuñjarārūḍhau paraspagvadhaiṣiṇau ..
tomaraiścakraturyuddhaṃ sūryāṃśusadṛśaprabhaiḥ .. 48 ..
1.189.d:
तावुभौ कुञ्जरारूढौ परस्पग्वधैषिणौ ॥
तोमरैश्चक्रतुर्युद्धं सूर्यांशुसदृशप्रभैः ॥ 48 ॥
1.189.m: Both mounted on elephants, each seeking the other's death, / they fought with javelins that had the brilliance of sunbeams.

1.189.s:
yudhyatāmeva teṣāṃ tu bhūmanyurvaravāraṇaḥ ..
pārśve jaghāna dantābhyāṃ kāmapālasya vāraṇam ..49..
1.189.d:
युध्यतामेव तेषां तु भूमन्युर्वरवारणः ॥
पार्श्वे जघान दन्ताभ्यां कामपालस्य वारणम् ॥49॥
1.189.m: Even as they were fighting, Bhūmanyu's excellent elephant / struck the elephant of Kāmapāla in the flank with its two tusks.

1.189.s: sahitastena nāgena kṛtvā rāvaṃ bhayānakam ..1.261.50..
1.189.d: सहितस्तेन नागेन कृत्वा रावं भयानकम् ॥1.261.50॥
1.189.m: Along with that elephant, having made a terrifying roar,

1.189.s:
āsītparāṅmukho yuddhe varttamānaḥ svakaṃ balam ..
kāmapālaṃ raṇe jitvā bhūmanyurbhīmavikramaḥ ..51..
1.189.d:
आसीत्पराङ्मुखो युद्धे वर्त्तमानः स्वकं बलम् ॥
कामपालं रणे जित्वा भूमन्युर्भीमविक्रमः ॥51॥
1.189.m: he turned his face away from battle, retreating toward his own force. / Having conquered Kāmapāla in battle, Bhūmanyu of terrible prowess

1.189.s:
gandharvasenāṃ sahasā jaghāna niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ..
kirātarājo damanaścandrāpīḍaśca saṃgatau .. 52 ..
1.189.d:
गन्धर्वसेनां सहसा जघान निशितैः शरैः ॥
किरातराजो दमनश्चन्द्रापीडश्च संगतौ ॥ 52 ॥
1.189.m: suddenly struck down the Gandharva army with sharpened arrows. / Damana, king of the Kirātas, and Candrāpīḍa clashed,

1.189.s:
cakratustumulaṃ yuddhaṃ samare rathadhūrgato ..
candrāpīḍaśaravrātanihatau pārṣṇisārathī .. 56 ..
1.189.d:
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं युद्धं समरे रथधूर्गतो ॥
चन्द्रापीडशरव्रातनिहतौ पार्ष्णिसारथी ॥ 56 ॥
1.189.m: and fought a tumultuous battle, both mounted upon the chariot's yoke. / His rear guard and charioteer having been slain by Candrāpīḍa’s volley of arrows,

1.189.s:
kirātarājasturagāṇāṃ svayaṃ raśmigraho'bhavat ..
vivyādha sa śaravrātaiścandrāpīḍaṃ raṇe tadā .. 54 ..
1.189.d:
किरातराजस्तुरगाणां स्वयं रश्मिग्रहोऽभवत् ॥
विव्याध स शरव्रातैश्चन्द्रापीडं रणे तदा ॥ 54 ॥
1.189.m: the king of the Kirātas took the reins of the horses himself. / Then in the fight he pierced Candrāpīḍa with swarms of arrows.

1.189.s:
candrāpīḍaśaravrātaiḥ kṛtāpīḍo raṇājire ..
jaghāna turagāstasya damanasya mahīpateḥ .. 55 ..
1.189.d:
चन्द्रापीडशरव्रातैः कृतापीडो रणाजिरे ॥
जघान तुरगास्तस्य दमनस्य महीपतेः ॥ 55 ॥
1.189.m: Candrāpīḍa, crowned with swarms of arrows on the battlefield, / slew the horses of King Damana.

1.189.s:
śaktyā vegācca vivyādha tadā taṃ bhīmavikramam ..
śaktyā vibhinnahṛdayaḥ papāta vasudhātale .. 56 ..
1.189.d:
शक्त्या वेगाच्च विव्याध तदा तं भीमविक्रमम् ॥
शक्त्या विभिन्नहृदयः पपात वसुधातले ॥ 56 ॥
1.189.m: With great velocity he then pierced that [king] of terrible prowess with a javelin; / with his heart torn open by the javelin, he fell upon the surface of the earth.

1.189.s:
jaghāna bhārataṃ sainyaṃ candrāpīḍo'pi sāyakaiḥ ..
āropya svarathe vīraṃ madhumāndamanaṃ tathā .. 57 ..
1.189.d:
जघान भारतं सैन्यं चन्द्रापीडोऽपि सायकैः ॥
आरोप्य स्वरथे वीरं मधुमान्दमनं तथा ॥ 57 ॥
1.189.m: Candrāpīḍa also struck down the Bhārata host with arrows. / Then Madhumat, having lifted the heroic Damana onto his own chariot,

1.189.s:
cakāra virujaṃ śīghramavraṇaṃ ca mahauṣadhaiḥ ..
yuyudhe ca nikumbhena matsyarāṭ sarathastathā .. 58 ..
1.189.d:
चकार विरुजं शीघ्रमव्रणं च महौषधैः ॥
युयुधे च निकुम्भेन मत्स्यराट् सरथस्तथा ॥ 58 ॥
1.189.m: speedily made him free from pain and woundless with potent herbs. / And the king of the Matsyas, mounted on a chariot, fought with Nikumbha.

1.189.s:
rathasthitau mahāvīrau varacāpamahākarau ..
anyo'nyaṃ śaravarṣeṇa chādayetāṃ ghanāviva .. 59 ..
1.189.d:
रथस्थितौ महावीरौ वरचापमहाकरौ ॥
अन्योऽन्यं शरवर्षेण छादयेतां घनाविव ॥ 59 ॥
1.189.m: Standing in their chariots, the two great heroes, their mighty arms bearing excellent bows, / covered each other with showers of arrows, like two clouds.

1.189.s:
surathastu nikumbhasya śareṇa nataparvaṇā ..
cāpamṛṣṭau praciccheda bhujadaṃḍaṃ tathāhave .. 1.261.60 ..
1.189.d:
सुरथस्तु निकुम्भस्य शरेण नतपर्वणा ॥
चापमृष्टौ प्रचिच्छेद भुजदंडं तथाहवे ॥ 1.261.60 ॥
1.189.m: Then Suratha, with a straight-jointed arrow in the battle, / cut through the bow-grip and arm of Nikumbha.

1.189.s:
nikumbho'pi praciccheda surathasya tu kārmukam ..
tāvanye dhanuṣī sajye kṛtvā vīrau parasparam .. 61 ..
1.189.d:
निकुम्भोऽपि प्रचिच्छेद सुरथस्य तु कार्मुकम् ॥
तावन्ये धनुषी सज्ये कृत्वा वीरौ परस्परम् ॥ 61 ॥
1.189.m: Nikumbha also severed Suratha's bow. / The two heroes, having strung other bows, mutually

1.189.s:
chādayetāṃ tathānyo'nyaṃ vīrau sāyakavṛṣṭibhiḥ ..
anyo'nyasya hayānhatvā ciccheda dhanuṣī tataḥ .. 62 ..
1.189.d:
छादयेतां तथान्योऽन्यं वीरौ सायकवृष्टिभिः ॥
अन्योऽन्यस्य हयान्हत्वा चिच्छेद धनुषी ततः ॥ 62 ॥
1.189.m: covered each other in turn with rains of arrows. / Then, having slain each other's horses, each severed the other's bow.

1.189.s:
hayānrathābhyāṃ kālasya nirjityāvaśamojasā ..
dhanuṣo madhyabhāge tu anyo'nyasya nyakṛntatām .. 53 ..
1.189.d:
हयान्रथाभ्यां कालस्य निर्जित्यावशमोजसा ॥
धनुषो मध्यभागे तु अन्योऽन्यस्य न्यकृन्तताम् ॥ 53 ॥
1.189.m: Having forcefully overpowered the horses from both chariots by their might, / they severed each other's bow right at the middle.

1.189.s:
virathāvasiyuddhāya cakraturyatnamuttamam ..
ādāya vipulaṃ carma śatacandraṃ ca bhāsvaram .. 64 ..
1.189.d:
विरथावसियुद्धाय चक्रतुर्यत्नमुत्तमम् ॥
आदाय विपुलं चर्म शतचन्द्रं च भास्वरम् ॥ 64 ॥
1.189.m: Deprived of their chariots, they made supreme exertion for a sword-fight, / taking up broad, radiant shields adorned with a hundred moons.

1.189.s:
ādadhāte khaṅgavarāvanyo'nyavadhakāṃkṣiṇau ..
khaḍgamākāśasadṛśamanyo'nyaṃ pravijaghnatuḥ .. 65 ..
1.189.d:
आदधाते खङ्गवरावन्योऽन्यवधकांक्षिणौ ॥
खड्गमाकाशसदृशमन्योऽन्यं प्रविजघ्नतुः ॥ 65 ॥
1.189.m: Eager to slay each other, they grasped their excellent swords; / they struck against one another with swords resembling the sky.

1.189.s:
maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi gatapratyāgatāni ca ..
kaiśikāni tu mārgāṇi darśayāmāsatustadā .. 66 ..
1.189.d:
मण्डलानि विचित्राणि गतप्रत्यागतानि च ॥
कैशिकानि तु मार्गाणि दर्शयामासतुस्तदा ॥ 66 ॥
1.189.m: Then they displayed varied circular movements, advances and retreats, / and fine footwork maneuvers.

1.189.s:
bhrāntamudbhrāntamāviddhamāplutaṃ visṛtaṃ sṛtam ..
saṃpātasamudīrṇaṃ ca khaḍgavarmavidāraṇama .. 67 ..
1.189.d:
भ्रान्तमुद्भ्रान्तमाविद्धमाप्लुतं विसृतं सृतम् ॥
संपातसमुदीर्णं च खड्गवर्मविदारणम ॥ 67 ॥
1.189.m: Whirling, wheeling up, sweeping around, leaping, darting, dashing forward, / clashing violently, and tearing through sword and armor,

1.189.s:
īkṣitṛprītijananaṃ yuddhamāsīttayostadā ..
kṛtvā tau suciraṃ yuddhaṃ paraspararaṇe hatau .. 68 ..
1.189.d:
ईक्षितृप्रीतिजननं युद्धमासीत्तयोस्तदा ॥
कृत्वा तौ सुचिरं युद्धं परस्पररणे हतौ ॥ 68 ॥
1.189.m: their battle then brought delight to the onlookers. / Having fought for a very long time, both struck down in mutual combat,

1.189.s:
jagmaturvasudhāṃ vegācchakracāpasamāvubhau ..
tataḥ svarathamāropya suratho rathivardhanaḥ .. 69 ..
1.189.d:
जग्मतुर्वसुधां वेगाच्छक्रचापसमावुभौ ॥
ततः स्वरथमारोप्य सुरथो रथिवर्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
1.189.m: the two fell swiftly to the ground like Indradhanus rainbows. / Then Suratha, increaser of car-warriors, having mounted his own chariot,

1.189.s:
tasmāddeśādapovāhya sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ ..
nikumbhe cātha samare surathena tadā ruṣā .. 1.261.70 ..
1.189.d:
तस्माद्देशादपोवाह्य सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ॥
निकुम्भे चाथ समरे सुरथेन तदा रुषा ॥ 1.261.70 ॥
1.189.m: was carried away from that place while the whole army looked on. / And when Nikumbha [fell] in battle, then in anger with Suratha,

1.189.s:
govāsanena sālvena tvaramāṇaḥ samāgataḥ ..
bāṇajālena samare cakruryuddhaṃ subhairavam .. 71 ..
1.189.d:
गोवासनेन साल्वेन त्वरमाणः समागतः ॥
बाणजालेन समरे चक्रुर्युद्धं सुभैरवम् ॥ 71 ॥
1.189.m: the Govāsana Sālva hurried and approached. / With a mass of arrows they fought a most terrifying battle.

1.189.s:
tāvubhau rathagau vīrau rejaturdivyadhanvinau ..
tatakṣatuḥ śaravrātaistadānyo'nyaṃ tathānvitau ..72..
1.189.d:
तावुभौ रथगौ वीरौ रेजतुर्दिव्यधन्विनौ ॥
ततक्षतुः शरव्रातैस्तदान्योऽन्यं तथान्वितौ ॥72॥
1.189.m: Both heroes, standing in their chariots, shone like heavenly archers; / thus matched, they carved each other with flights of arrows.

1.189.s:
anyonyasya hayānhatvā chittvā ca dhanuṣī tathā..
virathau cakraturyuddhaṃ gadābhiritaretaram .. 73..
1.189.d:
अन्योन्यस्य हयान्हत्वा छित्त्वा च धनुषी तथा॥
विरथौ चक्रतुर्युद्धं गदाभिरितरेतरम् ॥ 73॥
1.189.m: Having killed each other's horses and severed each other's bows, / deprived of chariots, they fought one another with maces.

1.189.s:
viceratustau saṃgrāme gadāhastau madoddhatau ..
vāsitārthe vane mattau kuñjarāviva yūthapau ..74..
1.189.d:
विचेरतुस्तौ संग्रामे गदाहस्तौ मदोद्धतौ ॥
वासितार्थे वने मत्तौ कुञ्जराविव यूथपौ ॥74॥
1.189.m: Bearing maces in their hands, inflated with pride, they moved about in the battle / like two lordly elephants maddened for a cow in the forest.

1.189.s:
suciraṃ tau tadā yuddhaṃ kṛtvā vyāyāmakarṣitau ..
prahāravarasaṃtaptau jagmaturvasudhātalam .. 75 ..
1.189.d:
सुचिरं तौ तदा युद्धं कृत्वा व्यायामकर्षितौ ॥
प्रहारवरसंतप्तौ जग्मतुर्वसुधातलम् ॥ 75 ॥
1.189.m: Having fought for a long time, exhausted by physical exertion / and scorched by heavy blows, they fell to the surface of the earth.

1.189.s:
vihvalau rathayoḥ kṛtvā nītau tau svasvasainikaiḥ ..
virujau ca kṛtau bhūyo raṇaśīrṣamupāgatau .. 76 ..
1.189.d:
विह्वलौ रथयोः कृत्वा नीतौ तौ स्वस्वसैनिकैः ॥
विरुजौ च कृतौ भूयो रणशीर्षमुपागतौ ॥ 76 ॥
1.189.m: Placed unconscious upon two chariots, they were carried away by their own soldiers; / and once made free of pain, they came back to the head of the battle.

1.189.s:
prabhadrakaśca saṃgrāmaṃ cakārājagareṇa ha ..
īkṣitṛprītijananaśarasaṃchāditāmbarama .. 77 ..
1.189.d:
प्रभद्रकश्च संग्रामं चकाराजगरेण ह ॥
ईक्षितृप्रीतिजननशरसंछादिताम्बरम ॥ 77 ॥
1.189.m: And Prabhadraka fought a battle with Ajagara, / covering the sky with arrows that delighted the beholders.

1.189.s:
sumukhe varttamānasya tadā gajāprabhadrakaḥ ..
cicchedājagarasyājau śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam .. 78 ..
1.189.d:
सुमुखे वर्त्तमानस्य तदा गजाप्रभद्रकः ॥
चिच्छेदाजगरस्याजौ शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् ॥ 78 ॥
1.189.m: Then Prabhadraka, standing right in front of him on an elephant, / severed in battle the head of Ajagara, which was adorned with burning earrings.

1.189.s:
mahodayaḥ kuṇideśo harikeśasya saṃyuge ..
gajena pothayāmāsa surathaṃ sarathasārathim 79 ..
1.189.d:
महोदयः कुणिदेशो हरिकेशस्य संयुगे ॥
गजेन पोथयामास सुरथं सरथसारथिम् 79 ॥
1.189.m: Mahodaya, ruler of Kuṇi, in Harikeśa's engagement, / crushed Suratha with an elephant along with his chariot and driver.

1.189.s:
hatāśvarathamutsṛjya gadayā sudṛḍhaṃ raṇe ..
harikeśaṃ mahābāhuṃ cakāra gatajīvitam .. 1.261.80 ..
1.189.d:
हताश्वरथमुत्सृज्य गदया सुदृढं रणे ॥
हरिकेशं महाबाहुं चकार गतजीवितम् ॥ 1.261.80 ॥
1.189.m: Leaping down from the chariot whose horses were killed, with a mace in battle / he firmly deprived mighty-armed Harikeśa of his life.

1.189.s:
traigarto vasudhānaśca sūryaraśmiśca saṃgatau ..
cakratustumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bali śakrāvivāparau ..81..
1.189.d:
त्रैगर्तो वसुधानश्च सूर्यरश्मिश्च संगतौ ॥
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं युद्धं बलि शक्राविवापरौ ॥81॥
1.189.m: Vasudhāna, the Trigarta warrior, and Sūryaraśmi met / and fought a tumultuous battle, like another Bali and Śakra.

1.189.s:
kṛtvā tau suciraṃ yuddhaṃ parasparasamāhatau ..
vicetasau rathopasthe niṣedaturarindamau .. 82..
1.189.d:
कृत्वा तौ सुचिरं युद्धं परस्परसमाहतौ ॥
विचेतसौ रथोपस्थे निषेदतुररिन्दमौ ॥ 82॥
1.189.m: Having fought for a long time, struck mutually by one another, / the two subduers of foes sank down unconscious on the chariot floors.

1.189.s:
visaṃjñau tu tadā nītau sārathibhyāṃ raṇājirāt ..
gandharvaḥ kumudāpīḍaḥ kulūtādhipatirjayaḥ ..83..
1.189.d:
विसंज्ञौ तु तदा नीतौ सारथिभ्यां रणाजिरात् ॥
गन्धर्वः कुमुदापीडः कुलूताधिपतिर्जयः ॥83॥
1.189.m: Senseless, they were then led away from the battlefield by their charioteers. / The Gandharva Kumudāpīḍa and Jaya, the lord of Kulūta,

1.189.s:
cakratustumulaṃ yuddhaṃ devāsurasamaṃ tadā ..
anyo'nyasya hayānhatvā chittvā ca dhanuṣī dṛḍhe .. 84 ..
1.189.d:
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं युद्धं देवासुरसमं तदा ॥
अन्योऽन्यस्य हयान्हत्वा छित्त्वा च धनुषी दृढे ॥ 84 ॥
1.189.m: then fought a tumultuous battle equal to that between gods and asuras. / Having killed each other's horses and severed their sturdy bows,

1.189.s:
khaḍgayuddhaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā chinnakhaḍgau parasparam ..
niyuddhaṃ cakraturvīrau bāhudraviṇaśālinau .. 85 ..
1.189.d:
खड्गयुद्धं चिरं कृत्वा छिन्नखड्गौ परस्परम् ॥
नियुद्धं चक्रतुर्वीरौ बाहुद्रविणशालिनौ ॥ 85 ॥
1.189.m: and having fought with swords for a long time until each shattered the other's sword, / the two heroes, endowed with the strength of their arms, engaged in hand-to-hand combat.

1.189.s:
niyuddhasyāvasāne tu kulūtādhipatiṃ jayam ..
gandharvaḥ kumudāpīḍo niṣpipeṣa mahītale .. 86 ..
1.189.d:
नियुद्धस्यावसाने तु कुलूताधिपतिं जयम् ॥
गन्धर्वः कुमुदापीडो निष्पिपेष महीतले ॥ 86 ॥
1.189.m: At the conclusion of the wrestling match, Kumudāpīḍa the Gandharva / crushed Jaya, the lord of Kulūta, upon the earth.

1.189.s:
tataḥ khaḍgaṃ rayādgṛhya śiraśchettuṃ samudyataḥ ..
nṛśaṃsaṃ taṃ samālocya senāpatimarindama .. .. 87 ..
1.189.d:
ततः खड्गं रयाद्गृह्य शिरश्छेत्तुं समुद्यतः ॥
नृशंसं तं समालोच्य सेनापतिमरिन्दम ॥ ॥ 87 ॥
1.189.m: Then, having swiftly seized his sword, he prepared to cut off his head. / Observing that cruelty toward the army commander, O subduer of enemies,

1.189.s:
vijayastasya mūrdhānaṃ pātayāmāsa bhūtale ..
dāśerakastathā rājā yaśca govāśanośanaḥ .. 88 ..
1.189.d:
विजयस्तस्य मूर्धानं पातयामास भूतले ॥
दाशेरकस्तथा राजा यश्च गोवाशनोशनः ॥ 88 ॥
1.189.m: Vijaya brought down his head onto the ground. / Then the king of the Dāśerakas and Uśana, the Govāsana,

1.189.s:
ekalavyasya saṃgrāmaṃ tairāsītsumahātmanaḥ ..
tasyaikalavyasturagāñjaghānātha śilīmukhaiḥ .. 89 ..
1.189.d:
एकलव्यस्य संग्रामं तैरासीत्सुमहात्मनः ॥
तस्यैकलव्यस्तुरगाञ्जघानाथ शिलीमुखैः ॥ 89 ॥
1.189.m: fought a battle against the high-souled Ekalavya. / Ekalavya then slew his horses with arrows,

1.189.s:
gadayā ghātayāmāsa sa ca tasya turaṅgamān ..
tayorvirathayorbhṛtyairupanītau turaṅgamau .. .. 1.261.90 ..
1.189.d:
गदया घातयामास स च तस्य तुरङ्गमान् ॥
तयोर्विरथयोर्भृत्यैरुपनीतौ तुरङ्गमौ ॥ ॥ 1.261.90 ॥
1.189.m: and the other struck down Ekalavya's horses with a mace. / When the two were deprived of their chariots, horses were brought by their attendants.

1.189.s:
pṛṣṭhataśca tathā rūḍhau varaprāsadharāvubhau ..
prāsavibhrāmaṇotkṣepaparivarttavivarttanau .. 91 ..
1.189.d:
पृष्ठतश्च तथा रूढौ वरप्रासधरावुभौ ॥
प्रासविभ्रामणोत्क्षेपपरिवर्त्तविवर्त्तनौ ॥ 91 ॥
1.189.m: Mounted upon the backs of those [horses], both bearing excellent darts, / brandishing, hurling, wheeling, and spinning their darts,

1.189.s:
cakratustumulaṃ yuddhaṃ citraṃ laghu ca suṣṭhu ca ..
maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi tayoścakrusturaṅgamāḥ .. 92 ..
1.189.d:
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं युद्धं चित्रं लघु च सुष्ठु च ॥
मण्डलानि विचित्राणि तयोश्चक्रुस्तुरङ्गमाः ॥ 92 ॥
1.189.m: they fought a tumultuous battle, wonderful, swift, and adroit; / their horses described variegated circles.

1.189.s:
īkṣitṛprītijananaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā tato raṇam ..
anyonyavegābhihatau petatussa turaṅgamau .. 93 ..
1.189.d:
ईक्षितृप्रीतिजननं चिरं कृत्वा ततो रणम् ॥
अन्योन्यवेगाभिहतौ पेततुस्स तुरङ्गमौ ॥ 93 ॥
1.189.m: Having fought for a long time a battle delighting the onlookers, / struck by each other's momentum, they fell together with their horses.

1.189.s:
bhṛtyaiśca rathamāropya samarādapavāhitau ..
kumāraḥ śreṇimāñchūro balabandhuḥ suyodhanaḥ .. 94 ..
1.189.d:
भृत्यैश्च रथमारोप्य समरादपवाहितौ ॥
कुमारः श्रेणिमाञ्छूरो बलबन्धुः सुयोधनः ॥ 94 ॥
1.189.m: Placed upon a chariot by their attendants, they were carried away from the battle. / Prince Śreṇimat, the heroic Balabandhu, and Suyodhana,

1.189.s:
gandharvaiḥ pañcabhiḥ pañca parvatīyāḥ samāgatāḥ ..
balākā balakābhyāṃ tu gadinā mālinā tathā..95..
1.189.d:
गन्धर्वैः पञ्चभिः पञ्च पर्वतीयाः समागताः ॥
बलाका बलकाभ्यां तु गदिना मालिना तथा॥95॥
1.189.m: Five mountaineers met with five Gandharvas, / namely Balāka and Balaka, along with Gadin, Mālin,

1.189.s:
kumudena ca vīreṇa samareṣvanivarttinā ..
caturbhiḥ sāyakaistīkṣṇaiḥ kumāro baladarpitaḥ ..96..
1.189.d:
कुमुदेन च वीरेण समरेष्वनिवर्त्तिना ॥
चतुर्भिः सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैः कुमारो बलदर्पितः ॥96॥
1.189.m: and Kumuda, the hero who does not retreat in battle. / Kumāra, puffed up with strength, with four sharp arrows

1.189.s:
hayām̐ścakāra nirjīvānbalākasya mahātmanaḥ ..
hatāśvarathamutsṛjya balākābhrāturañjasā..97..
1.189.d:
हयाम्̐श्चकार निर्जीवान्बलाकस्य महात्मनः ॥
हताश्वरथमुत्सृज्य बलाकाभ्रातुरञ्जसा॥97॥
1.189.m: deprived the horses of the great-souled Balāka of life. / Abandoning the chariot whose horses were slain, Balāka swiftly [approached] his brother

1.189.s:
āruroha rathaṃ śrīmadbalākasya susaṃyutam ..
tāvekarathamārūḍhau bhrātarau samarapriyau ..98..
1.189.d:
आरुरोह रथं श्रीमद्बलाकस्य सुसंयुतम् ॥
तावेकरथमारूढौ भ्रातरौ समरप्रियौ ॥98॥
1.189.m: and mounted the splendid, well-equipped chariot of Balaka. / Those two brothers, fond of battle, mounted upon a single chariot,

1.189.s:
chādayāmāsa viśikhaiḥ kumāro baladarpitaḥ ..
balakastu kumārasya madhye ciccheda kārmukam .. 99 ..
1.189.d:
छादयामास विशिखैः कुमारो बलदर्पितः ॥
बलकस्तु कुमारस्य मध्ये चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् ॥ 99 ॥
1.189.m: Kumāra, puffed up with strength, covered with arrows. / But Balaka cut Kumāra's bow in the middle.

1.189.s:
sa cchinnadhanvā vegena gadāmādāya vegavān..
tāmādāya jaghānātha balākaṃ samarapriyam..1.261.100..
1.189.d:
स च्छिन्नधन्वा वेगेन गदामादाय वेगवान्॥
तामादाय जघानाथ बलाकं समरप्रियम्॥1.261.100॥
1.189.m: With his bow severed, that swift warrior swiftly seized a mace; / having taken it up, he then struck Balāka, who was fond of battle.

1.189.s:
balākaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā roṣādaśru nivartayan ..
kumāraṃ prati cikṣepa balakaścaiva tomaram..101..
1.189.d:
बलाकं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रोषादश्रु निवर्तयन् ॥
कुमारं प्रति चिक्षेप बलकश्चैव तोमरम्॥101॥
1.189.m: Seeing Balāka slain, checking his tears in wrath, / Balaka hurled a javelin toward Kumāra.

1.189.s:
tomareṇa ca nirbhinno rathopastha upāviśat ..
taṃ visaṃjñamathovāha sārathirhayayānavit .. 102 ..
1.189.d:
तोमरेण च निर्भिन्नो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ॥
तं विसंज्ञमथोवाह सारथिर्हययानवित् ॥ 102 ॥
1.189.m: Pierced by the javelin, he sat down upon the floor of the chariot; / his charioteer, skilled in horse-driving, then carried him away unconscious.

1.189.s:
śroṇimānatha saṃkruddho balakasya tadā raṇe ..
kṣuraparyantadhāreṇa cakreṇāpaharacchiraḥ !. 103 ..
1.189.d:
श्रोणिमानथ संक्रुद्धो बलकस्य तदा रणे ॥
क्षुरपर्यन्तधारेण चक्रेणापहरच्छिरः !। 103 ॥
1.189.m: Then enraged Śreṇimat in that battle / severed Balaka's head with a discus having a razor-sharp edge.

1.189.s:
nipātito'tha tatraiva śareṇa gadayā gadī ..
taṃ nihatya tadā śūro maulinaḥ sārathiṃ raṇe..104..
1.189.d:
निपातितोऽथ तत्रैव शरेण गदया गदी ॥
तं निहत्य तदा शूरो मौलिनः सारथिं रणे॥104॥
1.189.m: Then right there Gadin was brought down with an arrow and a mace. / Having slain him then, that hero in battle [attacked] the charioteer of Maulin;

1.189.s:
gadayā pothayāmāsa merugauravayā tadā ..
kumudasya jaghānātha gadayā sa turaṅgamān .. 105..
1.189.d:
गदया पोथयामास मेरुगौरवया तदा ॥
कुमुदस्य जघानाथ गदया स तुरङ्गमान् ॥ 105॥
1.189.m: with a mace having the weight of Mount Meru, he crushed [him] then. / Then with his mace he killed the horses of Kumuda.

1.189.s:
hatāśvaṃ rathamutsṛjya kumudo gadino ratham ..
āruroha tadā śīghraṃ khaḍgabāṇadhanurdharaḥ .. 106 ..
1.189.d:
हताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य कुमुदो गदिनो रथम् ॥
आरुरोह तदा शीघ्रं खड्गबाणधनुर्धरः ॥ 106 ॥
1.189.m: Abandoning the chariot whose horses were killed, Kumuda quickly / mounted the chariot of Gadin, holding a sword, arrows, and a bow.

1.189.s:
rathārūḍhasya tasyātha balakaśca mahārathaḥ ..
jaghāna caturo vāhāṃścaturbhissāyakaistadā .. 107 ..
1.189.d:
रथारूढस्य तस्याथ बलकश्च महारथः ॥
जघान चतुरो वाहांश्चतुर्भिस्सायकैस्तदा ॥ 107 ॥
1.189.m: Then, as he stood mounted on the chariot, the great car-warrior Balaka / slew his four horses with four arrows.

1.189.s:
jahāra pañcamenātha śirastasya sakuṇḍalam ..
sārathiṃ tu rathāttasmānmaulino rathamuttamam .. 108 ..
1.189.d:
जहार पञ्चमेनाथ शिरस्तस्य सकुण्डलम् ॥
सारथिं तु रथात्तस्मान्मौलिनो रथमुत्तमम् ॥ 108 ॥
1.189.m: Then with a fifth arrow he took off his head adorned with earrings. / Leaving that chariot, the charioteer [went] to the excellent chariot of Maulin,

1.189.s:
hatasārathinaṃ pūrvamāruroha mahāraṇe ..
maulī yuddhāya tasthau ca mahābalaparākramaḥ .. 109..
1.189.d:
हतसारथिनं पूर्वमारुरोह महारणे ॥
मौली युद्धाय तस्थौ च महाबलपराक्रमः ॥ 109॥
1.189.m: whose charioteer had been killed earlier in the great battle, and mounted it. / And Maulin, of great strength and valor, stood ready to fight.

1.189.s:
āruhya sarathaṃ divyaṃ kiṅkiṇījālanāditam ..
tataḥ sa maulinākrāntaḥ suyodhanaratho raṇe ..1.261.110..
1.189.d:
आरुह्य सरथं दिव्यं किङ्किणीजालनादितम् ॥
ततः स मौलिनाक्रान्तः सुयोधनरथो रणे ॥1.261.110॥
1.189.m: Having mounted that divine chariot resounding with a net of small bells, / then Suyodhana's chariot was assailed in battle by Maulin.

1.189.s:
avākiradameyātmā śaraissannataparvabhiḥ ..
suyodhano'pi vikramya maulinaṃ maulibhūṣitam .. 111 ..
1.189.d:
अवाकिरदमेयात्मा शरैस्सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥
सुयोधनोऽपि विक्रम्य मौलिनं मौलिभूषितम् ॥ 111 ॥
1.189.m: The immeasurable-souled one showered him with arrows of bent joints. / Suyodhana also, showing his prowess against Maulin, who was adorned with a diadem,

1.189.s:
jahāra saśirastrāṇaṃ śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam ..
madrarājoṃśumānnāma caturbhiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ .. 112 ..
1.189.d:
जहार सशिरस्त्राणं शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् ॥
मद्रराजोंशुमान्नाम चतुर्भिः सायकोत्तमैः ॥ 112 ॥
1.189.m: severed his head adorned with brilliant earrings and wearing a helmet. / With four excellent arrows, the king of Madra named Aṃśumat

1.189.s:
bhīmanādamahānādavasumeṣarujākaraiḥ ..
catvāraste mahārāja madrarājasya sāyakaiḥ .. 113 ..
1.189.d:
भीमनादमहानादवसुमेषरुजाकरैः ॥
चत्वारस्ते महाराज मद्रराजस्य सायकैः ॥ 113 ॥
1.189.m: [was opposed] by Bhīmanāda, Mahānāda, Vasuṣeṇa, and Rujākara. / Those four, O great king, with their arrows

1.189.s:
nijaghnuścaturo vāhānsārathiṃ ca tathā raṇe ..
aṃśumānrathamutsṛjya gadāmādāya vīryavān .. 114 ..
1.189.d:
निजघ्नुश्चतुरो वाहान्सारथिं च तथा रणे ॥
अंशुमान्रथमुत्सृज्य गदामादाय वीर्यवान् ॥ 114 ॥
1.189.m: slew the four horses and also the charioteer of the king of Madra in battle. / Aṃśumat, abandoning his chariot and seizing a mace, powerful,

1.189.s:
jaghāna caturo vāhānbhīmanādasya saṃyuge ..
sārathiṃ pothayāmāsa mahānādarathāṃstathā .. 115 ..
1.189.d:
जघान चतुरो वाहान्भीमनादस्य संयुगे ॥
सारथिं पोथयामास महानादरथांस्तथा ॥ 115 ॥
1.189.m: slew the four horses of Bhīmanāda in the encounter; / he crushed the charioteer and likewise the horses of Mahānāda's chariot.

1.189.s:
gatāśvaṃ rathamutsṛjya gadāvegena yādava ..
mahodayasya taṃ nāgaṃ pothayāmāsa vīryavān .. 116 ..
1.189.d:
गताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य गदावेगेन यादव ॥
महोदयस्य तं नागं पोथयामास वीर्यवान् ॥ 116 ॥
1.189.m: Abandoning his horseless chariot with the swiftness of his mace, O Yādava, / the powerful one crushed that elephant of Mahodaya.

1.189.s:
sārathirbhīmanādasya mahānādarathaṃ yayau ..
bhīmanādaṃ ca gadayā nijaghānātha madrarāṭ .. 117 ..
1.189.d:
सारथिर्भीमनादस्य महानादरथं ययौ ॥
भीमनादं च गदया निजघानाथ मद्रराट् ॥ 117 ॥
1.189.m: The charioteer of Bhīmanāda went to Mahānāda's chariot; / and then the king of Madra struck Bhīmanāda with his mace.

1.189.s:
sa madrarājo gadayā samare tāḍito bhṛśam ..
jagāma tridivaṃ rājam̐styaktvā dehaṃ raṇapriyaḥ .. 118 ..
1.189.d:
स मद्रराजो गदया समरे ताडितो भृशम् ॥
जगाम त्रिदिवं राजम्̐स्त्यक्त्वा देहं रणप्रियः ॥ 118 ॥
1.189.m: Severely struck with the mace in battle, that king of Madra, / fond of battle, abandoned his body and went to heaven, O king.

1.189.s:
mahānādo'pi samare sāyakairlomavāhibhiḥ ..
bibheda madrarājānaṃ śataśotha sahasraśaḥ .. 119 ..
1.189.d:
महानादोऽपि समरे सायकैर्लोमवाहिभिः ॥
बिभेद मद्रराजानं शतशोथ सहस्रशः ॥ 119 ॥
1.189.m: Mahānāda also, in battle, with feathered arrows / pierced the king of Madra hundreds and thousands of times.

1.189.s:
sa bādhyamāno nārācairmahānādabhujacyutaiḥ ..
āruroha rathaṃ śīghraṃ vasuṣeṇasya satvaraḥ .. 1.261.120 ..
1.189.d:
स बाध्यमानो नाराचैर्महानादभुजच्युतैः ॥
आरुरोह रथं शीघ्रं वसुषेणस्य सत्वरः ॥ 1.261.120 ॥
1.189.m: Afflicted by the iron arrows loosed from the arms of Mahānāda, / he quickly mounted the chariot of Vasuṣeṇa in haste.

1.189.s:
rathamāruhya vegena gadayā bhīmavegayā ..
cakāra yuddhe nirjīvaṃ vasuṣeṇaṃ samarapriyam .. 121 ..
1.189.d:
रथमारुह्य वेगेन गदया भीमवेगया ॥
चकार युद्धे निर्जीवं वसुषेणं समरप्रियम् ॥ 121 ॥
1.189.m: Having swiftly mounted the chariot, with his mace of terrible speed / he deprived Vasuṣeṇa, who was fond of battle, of life in the encounter.

1.189.s:
avaruhya rathāttasmādgadayā bhīmavegayā ..
gajākarasya turagānsārathiṃ cāhanadbhṛśam .. 122 ..
1.189.d:
अवरुह्य रथात्तस्माद्गदया भीमवेगया ॥
गजाकरस्य तुरगान्सारथिं चाहनद्भृशम् ॥ 122 ॥
1.189.m: Descending from that chariot, with his mace of terrible speed / he violently struck down the horses and charioteer of Gajākaran.

1.189.s:
hateṣu teṣu rājendra tadā vīro gajākaraḥ ..
rathaṃ taṃ tu samāruhya bhūya eva tadaṃśumān .. 123 ..
1.189.d:
हतेषु तेषु राजेन्द्र तदा वीरो गजाकरः ॥
रथं तं तु समारुह्य भूय एव तदंशुमान् ॥ 123 ॥
1.189.m: When they were slain, O lord of kings, then the hero Gajākaran— / having mounted that chariot, once again then Aṃśumat

1.189.s:
cakāra yuddhe nirjīvaṃ gāndharvaṃ taṃ gajākaram ..
utplutya turagāttasmānmahānādarathaṃ gataḥ .. 124 ..
1.189.d:
चकार युद्धे निर्जीवं गान्धर्वं तं गजाकरम् ॥
उत्प्लुत्य तुरगात्तस्मान्महानादरथं गतः ॥ 124 ॥
1.189.m: deprived that Gandharva Gajākaran of life in the fight. / Leaping from that horse, he went to Mahānāda's chariot;

1.189.s:
gadayā pothayāmāsa mahānādaṃ tadā raṇe ..
roṣadīrghāṃkuśaṃ kṛtvā kuñjaraṃ bharatājñayā ..125..
1.189.d:
गदया पोथयामास महानादं तदा रणे ॥
रोषदीर्घांकुशं कृत्वा कुञ्जरं भरताज्ञया ॥125॥
1.189.m: he crushed Mahānāda with his mace then in battle. / Extending his goad in wrath, by Bharata's command,

1.189.s:
āruhya nijaghānātha gandharvāñśataśo raṇe ..
dārvaḥ śrutañjayaḥ śrīmānābhisāraḥ kṛtañjayaḥ .. 126 ..
1.189.d:
आरुह्य निजघानाथ गन्धर्वाञ्शतशो रणे ॥
दार्वः श्रुतञ्जयः श्रीमानाभिसारः कृतञ्जयः ॥ 126 ॥
1.189.m: he mounted an elephant and then slew Gandharvas by hundreds in battle. / The illustrious Dārva Śrutañjaya and the Ābhisāra Kṛtañjaya,

1.189.s:
yuddhaṃ tau cakraturvīrau sahitau candravarmaṇā ..
candravarmā mahātejāḥ śrutañjayarathāddhvajam .. 127 ..
1.189.d:
युद्धं तौ चक्रतुर्वीरौ सहितौ चन्द्रवर्मणा ॥
चन्द्रवर्मा महातेजाः श्रुतञ्जयरथाद्ध्वजम् ॥ 127 ॥
1.189.m: those two heroes fought together with Candravarmā. / Candravarmā, of great splendor, felled the banner from Śrutañjaya's chariot

1.189.s:
śareṇa pātayāmāsa vaṭavṛkṣamivocchritam ..
śrutañjayopi saṃkuddhaścandravarmakarasthitam .. 128 ..
1.189.d:
शरेण पातयामास वटवृक्षमिवोच्छ्रितम् ॥
श्रुतञ्जयोपि संकुद्धश्चन्द्रवर्मकरस्थितम् ॥ 128 ॥
1.189.m: with an arrow, like an exalted banyan tree. / Śrutañjaya also, enraged, split in two with a sharp arrow

1.189.s:
dvidhā cakāra tīkṣṇena sāyakena mahaddhanuḥ ..
taṃ chinnadhanuṣaṃ vīraṃ śaraiḥ sannataparvabhiḥ .. 129 ..
1.189.d:
द्विधा चकार तीक्ष्णेन सायकेन महद्धनुः ॥
तं छिन्नधनुषं वीरं शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥ 129 ॥
1.189.m: the great bow held in the hand of Candravarmā. / With his bow severed, that hero was covered in battle with arrows

1.189.s:
chādayāmāsa samare pārvatīyaḥ kṛtañjayaḥ ..
candravarmā samādāya tataḥ śaktiṃ sudāruṇām .. 1.261.130 ..
1.189.d:
छादयामास समरे पार्वतीयः कृतञ्जयः ॥
चन्द्रवर्मा समादाय ततः शक्तिं सुदारुणाम् ॥ 1.261.130 ॥
1.189.m: of bent joints by the mountaineer Kṛtañjaya. / Then Candravarmā, taking up a very terrible spear,

1.189.s:
bibheda samare rājanrājānaṃ taṃ kṛtañjayam ..
savibhinnastayā śaktyā rathopastha upāviśat .. 131 ..
1.189.d:
बिभेद समरे राजन्राजानं तं कृतञ्जयम् ॥
सविभिन्नस्तया शक्त्या रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ॥ 131 ॥
1.189.m: pierced that king Kṛtañjaya in the battle, O king. / Pierced by that spear, he sat down upon the floor of the chariot.

1.189.s:
taṃ visaṃjñamapovāha saṃgrāmādatha sārathiḥ ..
kṛtañjayaṃ mahārāja raṇe dṛṣṭvā vicetasam..132..
1.189.d:
तं विसंज्ञमपोवाह संग्रामादथ सारथिः ॥
कृतञ्जयं महाराज रणे दृष्ट्वा विचेतसम्॥132॥
1.189.m: His charioteer then carried him unconscious away from the battle. / Seeing Kṛtañjaya senseless in battle, O great king,

1.189.s:
sakuṇḍalaṃ samukuṭaṃ cārucandrasamaprabham ..
śiraściccheda tīkṣṇena sāyakena mahātmanā .. 133 ..
1.189.d:
सकुण्डलं समुकुटं चारुचन्द्रसमप्रभम् ॥
शिरश्चिच्छेद तीक्ष्णेन सायकेन महात्मना ॥ 133 ॥
1.189.m: [Candravarmā] with a sharp arrow severed the head of that great-souled one, / which was adorned with earrings and a diadem, shining like the lovely moon.

1.189.s:
samare yatamānasya subhṛśaṃ candravarmaṇā ..
kāśmīrakaḥ subāhuśca gandharveṇa subāhunā .. 134 ..
1.189.d:
समरे यतमानस्य सुभृशं चन्द्रवर्मणा ॥
काश्मीरकः सुबाहुश्च गन्धर्वेण सुबाहुना ॥ 134 ॥
1.189.m: While he was striving greatly in battle with Candravarmā, / the Kāśmīraka Subāhu [fought] with the Gandharva Subāhu;

1.189.s:
cakāra tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavarddhanam ..
ubhau tau taruṇau vīrāvubhau samaradurmadau ..135..
1.189.d:
चकार तुमुलं युद्धं भीरूणां भयवर्द्धनम् ॥
उभौ तौ तरुणौ वीरावुभौ समरदुर्मदौ ॥135॥
1.189.m: he fought a tumultuous battle that increased the fear of the timid. / Both were youthful heroes, both drunk with the fury of battle,

1.189.s:
darśanīyāvubhau vīrāvubhau bāṇadhanurdharau ..
tāvubhau sadṛśau vīrye śambarāmararājayoḥ ..136..
1.189.d:
दर्शनीयावुभौ वीरावुभौ बाणधनुर्धरौ ॥
तावुभौ सदृशौ वीर्ये शम्बरामरराजयोः ॥136॥
1.189.m: both handsome to behold, both bearers of arrows and bow; / they were both equal in valor to Śambara and the king of the gods.

1.189.s:
ubhau prakāraiścalitau tathobhau dṛḍhavikramau ..
cicchiduste tathānyonyaṃ dhvajacchatre narādhipa .. 137 ..
1.189.d:
उभौ प्रकारैश्चलितौ तथोभौ दृढविक्रमौ ॥
चिच्छिदुस्ते तथान्योन्यं ध्वजच्छत्रे नराधिप ॥ 137 ॥
1.189.m: Both were versatile in movements, and both of firm prowess; / they severed each other's banner and parasol, O ruler of men.

1.189.s:
anyonyasya hayānhatvā tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī ..
anyonyaṃ dhanuṣī chittvā sudṛḍhe samarapriye..138..
1.189.d:
अन्योन्यस्य हयान्हत्वा तथोभौ पार्ष्णिसारथी ॥
अन्योन्यं धनुषी छित्त्वा सुदृढे समरप्रिये॥138॥
1.189.m: Having slain each other's horses and both their side-charioteers, / and having broken each other's very strong bows, fond of battle,

1.189.s:
kṛte pratikṛtaṃ caiva kurvāṇau bhīmavikramau ..
virathāvasiyuddhāya cakraturyatnamuttamam .. 139 ..
1.189.d:
कृते प्रतिकृतं चैव कुर्वाणौ भीमविक्रमौ ॥
विरथावसियुद्धाय चक्रतुर्यत्नमुत्तमम् ॥ 139 ॥
1.189.m: retaliating deed for deed, those two of fierce prowess, / deprived of chariots, made an excellent effort for a sword-fight.

1.189.s:
asiyuddhaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā khaḍgamāvidhya satvaraḥ ..
pātayāmāsa mūrdhānaṃ gandharvasya narādhipa..1.261.140..
1.189.d:
असियुद्धं चिरं कृत्वा खड्गमाविध्य सत्वरः ॥
पातयामास मूर्धानं गन्धर्वस्य नराधिप॥1.261.140॥
1.189.m: Having fought with swords for a long time, he whirled his sword and swiftly / struck off the gandharva’s head, O ruler of men.

1.189.s:
āruroha rathaṃ cānyaṃ suśīghraṃ bharatājñayā ..
tatrārūḍhassa gandharvāñjaghāna śataśo raṇe .. 141 ..
1.189.d:
आरुरोह रथं चान्यं सुशीघ्रं भरताज्ञया ॥
तत्रारूढस्स गन्धर्वाञ्जघान शतशो रणे ॥ 141 ॥
1.189.m: Then, by Bharata’s command, he swiftly mounted another chariot; / mounted upon it, he slew hundreds of gandharvas in battle.

1.189.s:
etasminnantare kruddhaḥ śailūṣaḥ sa sahāyavān ..
cakāra yudhi nirjīvānnaranāgaturaṅgamān .. 142 ..
1.189.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धः शैलूषः स सहायवान् ॥
चकार युधि निर्जीवान्नरनागतुरङ्गमान् ॥ 142 ॥
1.189.m: Meanwhile, the enraged Śailūṣa, supported by his companions, / rendered men, elephants, and horses lifeless in the fight.

1.189.s:
babhūva bhāratī senā śailūṣeṇopamarditā ..
nidāghe puṣpaśabaladviradeneva padminī .. 143 ..
1.189.d:
बभूव भारती सेना शैलूषेणोपमर्दिता ॥
निदाघे पुष्पशबलद्विरदेनेव पद्मिनी ॥ 143 ॥
1.189.m: Bharata’s army, battered by Śailūṣa, / became like a lotus bed [crushed] in the hot season by an elephant dappled with flowers.

1.189.s:
etasminbhārate sainye kaścidāsīnmahārathaḥ ..
pratyudyayau yaḥ samare śailūṣaṃ raṇakarkaśam .. 144 ..
1.189.d:
एतस्मिन्भारते सैन्ये कश्चिदासीन्महारथः ॥
प्रत्युद्ययौ यः समरे शैलूषं रणकर्कशम् ॥ 144 ॥
1.189.m: In that army of Bharata there was a certain great car-warrior / who went out in battle against Śailūṣa, who was fierce in war.

1.189.s:
śailūṣaśarasampātaruddhagomaṇḍale ravau ..
na prājñāyata rājendra tadā kiñcidraṇājire .. 145 ..
1.189.d:
शैलूषशरसम्पातरुद्धगोमण्डले रवौ ॥
न प्राज्ञायत राजेन्द्र तदा किञ्चिद्रणाजिरे ॥ 145 ॥
1.189.m: When the sun’s disc of rays was blocked by the descent of Śailūṣa’s arrows, / nothing at all could be discerned on the battlefield then, O lord of kings.

1.189.s:
aśrūyata mahācchabdastālānāṃ patatāmiva ..
naranāgāśvakāyebhyo visasruḥ śoṇitāpagāḥ .. 146 ..
1.189.d:
अश्रूयत महाच्छब्दस्तालानां पततामिव ॥
नरनागाश्वकायेभ्यो विसस्रुः शोणितापगाः ॥ 146 ॥
1.189.m: A great crash was heard, like the falling of palmyra trees; / rivers of blood flowed forth from the bodies of men, elephants, and horses.

1.189.s:
evaṃ tu bhārataṃ sainyaṃ kālyamānamitastataḥ ..
śailūṣeṇa mahārāja bharataṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau .. 147 ..
1.189.d:
एवं तु भारतं सैन्यं काल्यमानमितस्ततः ॥
शैलूषेण महाराज भरतं शरणं ययौ ॥ 147 ॥
1.189.m: Driven here and there in this manner by Śailūṣa, O great king, / Bharata’s army sought refuge with Bharata.

1.189.s:
bharato'pi mahātejā dṛṣṭvā śailūṣamāgatama ..
pratyudyayau rathenājau kiṅkiṇījālamālinā .. 148 ..
1.189.d:
भरतोऽपि महातेजा दृष्ट्वा शैलूषमागतम ॥
प्रत्युद्ययौ रथेनाजौ किङ्किणीजालमालिना ॥ 148 ॥
1.189.m: Bharata too, endowed with great splendor, seeing Śailūṣa approach, / advanced against him in battle on a chariot garlanded with nets of tinkling bells.

1.189.s:
tatastau cakraturyuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam ..
trailokyavijayāsaktau yathobhau balivāsavau .. 149 ..
1.189.d:
ततस्तौ चक्रतुर्युद्धं घोररूपं भयानकम् ॥
त्रैलोक्यविजयासक्तौ यथोभौ बलिवासवौ ॥ 149 ॥
1.189.m: Then the two engaged in a fight of dreadful form, terrifying, / like Bali and Vāsava bent on victory over the three worlds.

1.189.s:
gandharvarāṭ tataḥ kruddhaḥ siṃhavadvinadanmuhuḥ ..
bharatasya rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ śaravarṣairavākirat ..1.261.150..
1.189.d:
गन्धर्वराट् ततः क्रुद्धः सिंहवद्विनदन्मुहुः ॥
भरतस्य रथं तूर्णं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ॥1.261.150॥
1.189.m: Then the king of the gandharvas, enraged, roaring repeatedly like a lion, / swiftly showered Bharata’s chariot with volleys of arrows.

1.189.s:
krameṇa sarathastasya sahayaḥ saha sārathiḥ ..
śaravarṣeṇa mahatā saṃchanno na prakāśitaḥ .. 151 ..
1.189.d:
क्रमेण सरथस्तस्य सहयः सह सारथिः ॥
शरवर्षेण महता संछन्नो न प्रकाशितः ॥ 151 ॥
1.189.m: By degrees, his chariot along with its horses and charioteer / was covered by the great rain of arrows and could not be seen.

1.189.s:
yudhājitkhalvasambhrānto dhairyamāsādya vīryavān ..
codayāmāsa tānaśvānvibhugnānripusāyakaiḥ .. 152 ..
1.189.d:
युधाजित्खल्वसम्भ्रान्तो धैर्यमासाद्य वीर्यवान् ॥
चोदयामास तानश्वान्विभुग्नान्रिपुसायकैः ॥ 152 ॥
1.189.m: Then the valiant Yudhājit, unperturbed, summoned his courage / and urged on those horses that were crippled by the enemy’s arrows.

1.189.s:
bharato'tha dhanurgṛhya divyaṃ jaladaniḥsvanam ..
śailūṣasya dvidhā cakre kṣurapreṇa mahaddhanuḥ .. .. 153 ..
1.189.d:
भरतोऽथ धनुर्गृह्य दिव्यं जलदनिःस्वनम् ॥
शैलूषस्य द्विधा चक्रे क्षुरप्रेण महद्धनुः ॥ ॥ 153 ॥
1.189.m: Then Bharata, taking up a celestial bow that sounded like a raincloud, / split Śailūṣa’s great bow in two with a crescent-tipped arrow.

1.189.s:
gandharvaśchinnadhanvā sa punaranyanmahaddhanuḥ ..
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa sajjaṃ cakre mahābalaḥ .. 154 ..
1.189.d:
गन्धर्वश्छिन्नधन्वा स पुनरन्यन्महद्धनुः ॥
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण सज्जं चक्रे महाबलः ॥ 154 ॥
1.189.m: With his bow severed, that gandharva of mighty strength / strung another great bow in the mere twinkling of an eye.

1.189.s:
vicakarṣa tato dorbhyāṃ cikṣepa ca tataḥ śarān ..
athāsya tadapi kruddhaściccheda bharato dhanuḥ .. 155 ..
1.189.d:
विचकर्ष ततो दोर्भ्यां चिक्षेप च ततः शरान् ॥
अथास्य तदपि क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद भरतो धनुः ॥ 155 ॥
1.189.m: He drew it back with both arms and shot his arrows; / then the enraged Bharata severed that bow of his as well.

1.189.s:
tasya tatpūjayāmāsa lāghavaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ ..
śailūṣo'pi tataḥ kruddhaḥ pragṛ'hyānyanmahaddhanuḥ .. 156 ..
1.189.d:
तस्य तत्पूजयामास लाघवं त्रिदशाधिपः ॥
शैलूषोऽपि ततः क्रुद्धः प्रगृऽह्यान्यन्महद्धनुः ॥ 156 ॥
1.189.m: The lord of the gods praised his lightness of hand. / Śailūṣa too, enraged, seized another great bow,

1.189.s:
mumoca samare bāṇānbharatasya rathaṃ prati ..
yudhājinmātulastasya saha yānena lāghavam .. 157 ..
1.189.d:
मुमोच समरे बाणान्भरतस्य रथं प्रति ॥
युधाजिन्मातुलस्तस्य सह यानेन लाघवम् ॥ 157 ॥
1.189.m: And loosed arrows in the battle toward Bharata’s chariot. / His maternal uncle Yudhājit displayed agility with the vehicle in battle,

1.189.s:
darśayāmāsa samare moghānkurvañśaravrajān ..
turagāścodyamānāste maṇḍalānīva babhramuḥ .. 158 ..
1.189.d:
दर्शयामास समरे मोघान्कुर्वञ्शरव्रजान् ॥
तुरगाश्चोद्यमानास्ते मण्डलानीव बभ्रमुः ॥ 158 ॥
1.189.m: Rendering the swarms of arrows futile; / and those horses, being driven, wheeled in circles as it were.

1.189.s:
yathāyathā śaravrātā moghā yānti mahītalam ..
bharato'pi mahātejā maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukaḥ.. 159 ..
1.189.d:
यथायथा शरव्राता मोघा यान्ति महीतलम् ॥
भरतोऽपि महातेजा मण्डलीकृतकार्मुकः॥ 159 ॥
1.189.m: As the swarms of arrows fell futile to the earth, / the radiant Bharata, bending his bow into a circle,

1.189.s:
vīraketuṃ śaravrātairvivyādha raṇamūrdhani ..
tāḍitaṃ sārathiṃ dṛṣṭvā vīraketuṃ tathā sutam .. 1.261.160 ..
1.189.d:
वीरकेतुं शरव्रातैर्विव्याध रणमूर्धनि ॥
ताडितं सारथिं दृष्ट्वा वीरकेतुं तथा सुतम् ॥ 1.261.160 ॥
1.189.m: Pierced Vīraketu at the front of the battle with multitudes of arrows. / Seeing the charioteer and likewise his son Vīraketu struck,

1.189.s:
gandharvastāḍayāmāsa sāyakaistu yudhājitam ..
yudhājiti mahābāhau samare bhṛśavikṣate ..161..
1.189.d:
गन्धर्वस्ताडयामास सायकैस्तु युधाजितम् ॥
युधाजिति महाबाहौ समरे भृशविक्षते ॥161॥
1.189.m: The gandharva struck Yudhājit with arrows. / When the mighty-armed Yudhājit was severely wounded in battle,

1.189.s:
ciccheda cchatraṃ bāṇena śailūṣasya tu rāghavaḥ ..
dvitīyena tu bāṇena lasantaṃ dhvajamucchritam .. 162 ..
1.189.d:
चिच्छेद च्छत्रं बाणेन शैलूषस्य तु राघवः ॥
द्वितीयेन तु बाणेन लसन्तं ध्वजमुच्छ्रितम् ॥ 162 ॥
1.189.m: The descendant of Raghu severed Śailūṣa’s parasol with an arrow, / and with a second arrow his glittering, upraised banner,

1.189.s:
tṛtīyena dhanurmuṣṭau tathā jaladaniḥsvanam ..
sa cchinnadhanvā vegena śaktimādāya satvaraḥ .. 163 ..
1.189.d:
तृतीयेन धनुर्मुष्टौ तथा जलदनिःस्वनम् ॥
स च्छिन्नधन्वा वेगेन शक्तिमादाय सत्वरः ॥ 163 ॥
1.189.m: And with a third the bow that sounded like a raincloud at its grip. / His bow broken, he swiftly took up a spear with force,

1.189.s:
vivyādha bharataṃ vīraṃ bhuje vāme narādhipa ..
prahāravarabhinnasya bharatasya mahātmanaḥ .. 164 ..
1.189.d:
विव्याध भरतं वीरं भुजे वामे नराधिप ॥
प्रहारवरभिन्नस्य भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥ 164 ॥
1.189.m: And pierced the heroic Bharata in the left arm, O ruler of men. / Pierced by that excellent stroke, the bow of the noble Bharata,

1.189.s:
karātpapāta vegena cāpaścāpadharasya ca ..
avānyaddhanurādāya bharato raghunandanaḥ..165..
1.189.d:
करात्पपात वेगेन चापश्चापधरस्य च ॥
अवान्यद्धनुरादाय भरतो रघुनन्दनः॥165॥
1.189.m: Though he held the bow, fell forcefully from his hand. / But Bharata, the delight of the Raghus, took up another bow,

1.189.s:
śarairanekasāhasrairgaṃdharvaṃ tamavākirat ..
pātayāmāsa ca tathā kavacaṃ ratnabhūṣitam..166..
1.189.d:
शरैरनेकसाहस्रैर्गंधर्वं तमवाकिरत् ॥
पातयामास च तथा कवचं रत्नभूषितम्॥166॥
1.189.m: And showered that gandharva with many thousands of arrows, / and likewise brought down his gem-adorned armor.

1.189.s:
āpadaṃ paramāṃ prāptaḥ śailūṣopyatha satvaraḥ..
āgneyamastraṃ cikṣepa bharataṃ prati vīryavān .. 167 ..
1.189.d:
आपदं परमां प्राप्तः शैलूषोप्यथ सत्वरः॥
आग्नेयमस्त्रं चिक्षेप भरतं प्रति वीर्यवान् ॥ 167 ॥
1.189.m: Having fallen into extreme distress, the valiant Śailūṣa then quickly / hurled the fiery weapon against Bharata.

1.189.s:
vāruṇena tadastraṃ tu śamayāmāsa rāghavaḥ ..
vāyavyamastraṃ śailūṣastadā cikṣepa pārthiva .. 168 ..
1.189.d:
वारुणेन तदस्त्रं तु शमयामास राघवः ॥
वायव्यमस्त्रं शैलूषस्तदा चिक्षेप पार्थिव ॥ 168 ॥
1.189.m: The descendant of Raghu quenched that weapon with the watery weapon. / Then Śailūṣa hurled the wind weapon, O king.

1.189.s:
śailāstreṇātha bharataḥ śamayāmāsa tatpunaḥ ..
śailāstramatha cikṣepa gandharvanṛpatistathā .. 169 ..
1.189.d:
शैलास्त्रेणाथ भरतः शमयामास तत्पुनः ॥
शैलास्त्रमथ चिक्षेप गन्धर्वनृपतिस्तथा ॥ 169 ॥
1.189.m: Then Bharata pacified it again with the mountain weapon. / Thereupon the king of the gandharvas likewise hurled the mountain weapon.

1.189.s:
vajreṇāstreṇa tatkruddhaḥ śamayāmāsa rāghavaḥ ..
utsasarja tato rājā brahmāstraṃ prāṇasaṃśaye .. 1.261.170 ..
1.189.d:
वज्रेणास्त्रेण तत्क्रुद्धः शमयामास राघवः ॥
उत्ससर्ज ततो राजा ब्रह्मास्त्रं प्राणसंशये ॥ 1.261.170 ॥
1.189.m: Enraged, the descendant of Raghu neutralized it with the thunderbolt weapon. / Then, his life in danger, the king released the Brahmā weapon.

1.189.s:
kākutsthaḥ śamayāmāsa brahmāstreṇaiva tattadā ..
astrayuddhe vyatikrānte krodhādāraktalocanaḥ .. 171 ..
1.189.d:
काकुत्स्थः शमयामास ब्रह्मास्त्रेणैव तत्तदा ॥
अस्त्रयुद्धे व्यतिक्रान्ते क्रोधादारक्तलोचनः ॥ 171 ॥
1.189.m: The descendant of Kakutstha quenched it then with the Brahmā weapon itself. / When the duel of supernatural weapons had passed, his eyes reddened with rage,

vīraketośca ciccheda śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam .. 172 ..

जघान चतुरो वाहान्भरतस्य स सायकैः ॥
वीरकेतोश्च चिच्छेद शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् ॥ 172 ॥
1.189.m: He slew Bharata’s four horses with arrows, / severed Vīraketu’s head adorned with radiant earrings,

तस्य राज्ञश्च चिच्छेद मुकुटं रत्नभूषितम् ॥
उवाच भरतश्रेष्ठः शैलूषं प्रहसंस्तदा ॥ 173 ॥
1.189.m: And severed that king’s gem-adorned diadem. / Then the best of the Bharatas said to Śailūṣa, laughing:

tatra gatvā tato yātaḥ parvataṃ gandhamādanam ..174..

कृतकर्मा रणश्रांतो गच्छाद्य स्वं निवेशनम् ॥
तत्र गत्वा ततो यातः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम् ॥174॥
1.189.m: “You have done your deed, exhausted by battle; go today to your own dwelling. / Having gone there, go then to Mount Gandhamādana.

अन्यथा श्वो न मे जीवन्गन्तासि रणमूर्धनि ॥
अस्तं च सविता याति कृतकर्मा दिनक्षये ॥ 175 ॥
1.189.m: Otherwise, tomorrow you will not leave the front of the battle alive from me. / The sun, having completed its work, is setting at the close of day,

वयञ्च शिबिरायैव गमिष्यामो जनाधिप ॥
एतावदुक्त्वा शैलूषं चोत्सृज्य भरतस्तदा ॥
कृत्वावहारं प्रययौ शिबिरायैव यादव ॥ 176 ॥
1.189.m: And we shall return to our camp, O ruler of men.” / Having spoken thus and dismissed Śailūṣa, Bharata then, / having sounded the retreat, went back to his camp, O Yādava.
