1.189.d:
गन्धर्वराजोऽथ गृहं प्रविश्य निश्चित्य कार्यं मरणाय बुद्धिम् ॥
कृत्वा रणायैव मनश्चकार रात्रिं तथोवाह गृहे नरेन्द्रः ॥ 177 ॥
1.262
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ततो रजन्यां व्युष्टायां मरणे कृतनिश्चयः ॥
सन्नह्यत विना व्यूहं भरतं प्रत्युदैक्षत ॥ 1 ॥
भरतोऽपि महातेजाः कृतपूर्वाह्णिकक्रियः ॥
निर्गम्य नगरात्सर्वान्पार्थिवानिदमब्रवीत् ॥ 2 ॥
गन्धर्वैर्भवतां युद्धं मम बुद्ध्या न रोचते ॥
एक एव समर्थोऽहं युष्माकं तेजसा नृपाः ॥ 3 ॥
हन्तुं गन्धर्वसैन्यं तद्भवद्भिः परिपीडितम् ॥
युध्यमाना भवन्तश्च रक्षितव्या मया रणे ॥ 4 ॥
सकलत्राम्̐स्ततो भूपानेताञ्शक्नोमि घातितुम्।
भवतामार्जवं युद्धे गन्धर्वाः कूटयोधिनः ॥ 5 ॥
अद्य तान्सायकैः सर्वान्दिव्यास्त्रप्रतिमन्त्रितैः ॥
घातयिष्यामि भूपालांस्तदनुज्ञातुमर्हथ ॥ 6 ॥
1.189.m:
Then the king of the gandharvas, having entered his home, resolving on what was to be done, set his mind on death / and resolved on battle alone; and thus the king passed the night in his house.
1.262 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, when the night had dawned, having resolved on death, / he armed himself, without battle array, and waited for Bharata.
Bharata too, endowed with great splendor, having performed his morning rites, / marched out of the city and addressed all the kings thus:
“Battle with the gandharvas does not seem right to me for you. / By your power, O kings, I alone am capable
Of slaying that army of gandharvas harassed by you; / and you, fighting, must be protected by me in battle.”
Therefore, O kings, these [foes] can kill you along with your wives.
Your conduct in battle is upright, whereas the Gandharvas fight with deceit.
Today, with arrows consecrated with divine weapons,
I will slaughter them all, O rulers of the earth; you should give me your assent.

1.189.d:
भरतेनैवमुक्तास्तु राजानो वाक्यमब्रुवन् ॥
त्वया कलत्रमस्माकं रक्ष्यं स्वामिन्प्रयत्नतः ॥ 7 ॥
भवतो रक्षणं कार्यं समस्तैर्वसुधाधिपैः ॥
पत्रच्छेदे फलच्छेदे वृक्षः शाखावकर्तने ॥ 8 ॥
भूयो वृद्धिमवाप्नोति मूलच्छेदे विनश्यति ॥
ते वयं भवतां वीर्यं जानन्तोऽपि रघूद्वह ॥ 9 ॥
नैकं संत्यक्तुमिच्छामो भवन्तं रणमूर्धनि ॥
एकैकस्य तथास्माकं गन्धर्वाणां महद्बलम् ॥ 1.262.10 ॥
वयं रणे हि पर्याप्ताः किं पुनस्तव पार्थिव ॥
किन्तु भृत्येषु तिष्ठत्सु स्वामिनो गर्हितं रणम् ॥ 11 ॥
ते वयं घातयिष्यामो गन्धर्वानद्य सत्वरम् ॥
एवमुक्तो महातेजा भरतो नृपसत्तमैः ॥ 12 ॥
वारयामास सान्त्वेन ततस्तु वसुधाधिपान् ॥
शापिताः स्थ मम प्राणै राज्ञो रामस्य चाप्यथ ॥13॥
1.189.m:
Addressed in this manner by Bharata, the kings replied:
"Our wives must be protected by you, O lord, with diligence.
Your protection must be ensured by all the lords of the earth.
When leaves are cut, when fruit is cut, or when a tree's branches are hewn away,
it grows again; but when its root is cut, it perishes.
Though we know your prowess, O descendant of Raghu,
we do not wish to abandon you alone in the forefront of battle.
For each one of us is matched against a great army of Gandharvas;
we are indeed sufficient in battle, so what need be said of you, O protector of the earth?
Yet, when servants are present, it is reprehensible for the master to fight.
We ourselves will destroy the Gandharvas today without delay."
Addressed thus by the best of kings, Bharata of great splendour
restrained the lords of the earth with gentle words:
"You are adjured by my life-breaths and also by King Rāma:

saṃyataiśca mahadyuddhaṃ paśyadbhirmama pārthivaiḥ .. 14 ..

gandharvāṇāṃ ca dīptāyāṃ diśyavāśanta pakṣiṇaḥ.. 21 ..
1.189.d:
अद्यैव विनिवर्तध्वं संग्रामात्पृथिवीक्षितः ॥
संयतैश्च महद्युद्धं पश्यद्भिर्मम पार्थिवैः ॥ 14 ॥
इत्येवमुक्ताः कृच्छ्रेण रणं मुक्त्वा नराधिपाः ॥
एकान्तस्थाः सुसन्नद्धा ददृशुस्तन्महद्रणम् ॥ 15 ॥
एकस्य च बहूनां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम् ॥
रथेन काञ्चनाङ्गेन किङ्किणीजालमालिना ॥ 16 ॥
युधाजिता गृहीतेन सतोयाम्बुदचारिणा ॥
चञ्चद्बहुपताकेन कोविदारध्वजेन च ॥ 17 ॥
आससाद रणे यक्षान्गन्धर्वान्रणकर्कशान्।
शरैः सञ्छादयामास गभस्तिभिरिवांशुमान् ॥ 18 ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले च सहसा गगनच्युता ॥
उल्का पपात मध्येन भित्त्वा सूर्यस्य मण्डलम् ॥ 19 ॥
आसीद्घोरो महीकम्पः शैलूषाङ्गविदारणः ॥
आदित्यमण्डले राजन्कबन्धश्चाप्यदृश्यत ॥ 1.262.20 ॥
ववर्ष च तदा देवो गन्धर्वान्रक्तवृष्टिभिः ॥
गन्धर्वाणां च दीप्तायां दिश्यवाशन्त पक्षिणः॥ 21 ॥
1.189.m:
withdraw this very day from the battle, O kings!
Restrained, you kings shall watch my great battle."
Having been addressed in this manner, the rulers of men reluctantly quitted the battle;
standing aside well-armoured, they watched that great conflict,
a duel of one against many that increased the realm of Yama.
Mounted on a chariot of golden frame, adorned with a network of tinkling bells,
supplied by Yudhājit, traversing like a water-laden cloud,
with many fluttering banners and bearing an orchid-tree standard,
he confronted in battle the Gandharvas who were fierce in war, like Yakṣas;
he covered them with arrows as the sun [covers the world] with rays.
At that very moment, suddenly falling from the sky,
a meteor plunged down, cleaving through the centre of the sun's orb.
There was a dreadful earthquake that tore at Śailūṣa's limbs,
and a headless trunk was seen within the sun's disc, O king.
Then the god rained down showers of blood upon the Gandharvas,
and birds shrieked in the blazing quarter of the Gandharvas.

1.189.d:
मृगाश्च घोरा राजेन्द्र शिवाश्चाशिवनिःस्वनाः॥
प्रतिलोमस्तथैवासीद्वायुस्तेषां सुशङ्ककृत् ॥ 22 ॥
न्यलीयत तथा गृधः शैलूषस्य ध्वजाग्रतः ॥
समे पथि निराबाधे प्रस्खलन्तस्तुरङ्गमाः॥23॥
शतपत्राश्च चाषाश्च हंसाश्चैव प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
भरतस्य तदा चक्रुः सव्यो बाहुरथास्फुरत् ॥ 24 ॥
दृष्ट्वा निमित्ताम्̐स्तु शुभान्युधाजित्सुमहायशाः ॥
चोदयामास तुरगान्गन्धर्वाणां चमूं प्रति ॥ 25 ॥
भरतोऽपि शरव्रातैर्घातयामास वाहिनीम् ॥
गन्धर्वाणामुदीर्णानां घोरैः शतसहस्रशः ॥ 26 ॥
वध्यमानास्तु गन्धर्वा भरतेन महात्मना ॥
तमेवाभिमुखा जग्मुः शलभाः पावकं यथा॥27॥
तेषामापततामेव शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥
पातयामास शीर्षाणि भरतो वाहिनीपतिः ॥ 28 ॥
भरतं कोष्ठकीकृत्वा गन्धर्वाः सुमहारथाः ॥
ववर्षुरायुधैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मेघा वृष्ट्येव पर्वतम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.189.m:
Fierce beasts, O bull among kings, and jackals wailed with inauspicious cries;
likewise, an adverse wind blew against them, causing great terror.
A vulture settled on the tip of Śailūṣa's standard;
and his horses stumbled on an even, unobstructed path.
Woodpeckers, blue jays, and swans then circumambulated Bharata clockwise,
and his left arm twitched.
Beholding these auspicious omens, Yudhājit of very great renown
urged his horses against the Gandharva host.
Bharata too, with masses of dreadful arrows in their hundreds and thousands,
slaughtered the army of the surging Gandharvas.
Being struck down by the noble Bharata,
the Gandharvas rushed towards him alone, like moths towards a fire.
Even as they rushed forward, with arrows of bent joints,
Bharata, the commander of the army, brought down their heads.
Having surrounded Bharata in an enclosure, the Gandharvas, mighty car-warriors,
showered him with sharp weapons as clouds shower a mountain with rain.

तान्यायुधानि मुख्यानि गन्धर्वैर्भरतस्तथा ॥
चिच्छेद राजन्नाराचैर्गन्धर्वांश्चावधीद्बली ॥ 1.262.30 ॥
मस्तकान्सशिरस्त्राणान्बाहूनपि च साङ्गदान् ॥
हस्तिहस्तोपमन्रूरूंश्चिच्छेद भरतो रणे ॥ 31 ॥
नावधान न सन्धानं न मुञ्चन्तं च सायकान् ॥
ददर्श भरतं कश्चिल्लाघवाद्रणमूर्धनि ॥ 32 ॥
केवलं दृश्यते युद्धे गन्धर्वाणां महाचमूः ॥
दह्यमाना शरव्रातैर्युगान्ताग्निरिव ज्वलन् ॥ 33 ॥
बाणगोचरमायातान्भरतस्य विनिघ्नतः ॥
शात्रवान्सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्जगामास्तं दिवाकरः ॥ 34 ॥
रणे जयं प्राप्य ततो निवृत्तः समागतश्चापि नरेन्द्रमुख्यैः ॥
प्रायान्महात्मा शिबिराय राजन्संस्तूयमानस्त्रिदशद्विजेन्द्रैः ॥ 35 ॥
1.189.m:
Those foremost weapons [loosed] by the Gandharvas, Bharata likewise
severed with iron shafts, O king, and the mighty one slew the Gandharvas.
Heads along with helmets, arms adorned with armlets,
and thighs resembling elephant trunks Bharata lopped off in battle.
Neither taking aim nor drawing the bow nor releasing arrows
did anyone see Bharata do, because of his lightness of hand at the head of battle.
Only the great host of Gandharvas was seen in the battle,
being consumed by flights of arrows as if by the blazing fire at the end of an aeon.
As Bharata was slaying with sharp arrows his enemies
who had come within range of his shafts, the sun set.
Having attained victory in battle, he then turned back and, joined by the foremost kings,
the noble one proceeded to his camp, O king, praised by the gods and foremost twice-born.

इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे तृतीययुद्धदिवसवर्णनं नाम द्विषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 262 ॥
1.263
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
चतुर्थेऽहनि संप्राप्ते कृतपूर्वाह्णिकक्रियः ॥
शैलूषस्तु विनिष्क्रम्य गन्धर्वानिदमब्रवीत् ॥ 1 ॥
योधयध्वं रणे सर्वे भरतं रिपुमागतम् ॥
अहं मध्ये प्रवेक्ष्यामि भरतस्य बलार्णवम् ॥ 2 ॥
तत्र तान्घातयिष्यामि भरतस्यानुयायिनः ॥
एतदुक्ते तथेत्युक्त्वा संप्रतीक्षन्त राघवम् ॥ 3 ॥
भरतोऽपि महातेजा रथेनैकेन दृश्यते ॥
भरतस्यानुसैन्यं च भूभुजा समपद्यत ॥ 4 ॥
तत्सैन्यं प्राविशदघोरं शैलूषो रणदर्पितः॥
चकार कदनं तत्र नरवारणवाजिनाम् ॥ 5 ॥
गन्धर्वसैन्ये च तथा भरतोऽपि शरोत्करैः ॥
चकार कदनं घोरं वैश्वानरसमप्रभैः ॥ 6 ॥
1.189.m:
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Third Day of Battle', in the First Book of the holy Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
1.263
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When the fourth day arrived, having performed his morning rites,
Śailūṣa came forth and spoke thus to the Gandharvas:
"All of you fight in battle against Bharata, the enemy who has arrived;
I shall plunge into the midst of Bharata's ocean of an army.
There I will slay those followers of Bharata."
When this was said, replying "So be it," they waited for the descendant of Raghu.
Bharata of great splendour was seen in a single chariot,
and the king accompanied Bharata's army.
Śailūṣa, arrogant in battle, entered that dreadful army;
he wrought slaughter there of men, elephants, and horses.
Likewise, in the Gandharva army, Bharata too with masses of arrows
possessing splendour like fire, wrought terrible slaughter.

राजानं कोष्ठके कृत्वा शैलूषं विविधैः शरैः ॥
छादयामासुरव्यग्रा मेघा इव महीधरम् ॥ 7 ॥
गोवासनस्तु सप्तत्या बिभेद समरे शरैः ॥
द्विजिह्वश्च त्रिसप्तत्या राजा दाशेरकस्तु यः ॥ 8 ॥
सुबाहुस्तं चतुष्षष्ट्या दशभिस्तं सुयोधनः ॥
कुमारः सप्तसप्तत्या श्रेणिमान्दशभिस्त्रिभिः ॥9 ॥
शूरः षष्ट्या च निर्भिद्य बलबन्धुः शतेन च॥
द्वाविंशत्या ततस्तक्षः पुष्करो नवभिः शरैः ॥ 1.263.10 ॥
शतेन विजयश्चैनं जयो जित्वा त्रिभिः शरैः ॥
प्रत्यविध्यत तान्सर्वाच्छैलूषो दशभिः शरैः ॥ 11 ॥
नृत्यन्निव रथोपस्थे महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन सुबाहोः सुमहात्मनः ॥ ॥ 12 ॥
हयाम्̐श्चकार निर्जीवांस्तथैवांशुमतो नृप ॥
पद्मं रथस्थं चिच्छेद चिह्नं गोवासनस्य तु ॥ 13 ॥
1.189.m:
Enclosing King Śailūṣa in an ambush with various arrows,
they covered him unswervingly, like clouds covering a mountain.
Govāsana pierced him with seventy arrows in battle,
and Dvijihva, the king who was a Dāśeraka, with seventy-three;
Subāhu [pierced] him with sixty-four, Suyodhana with ten,
Kumāra with seventy-seven, Śreṇimat with thirteen,
Śūra with sixty, and having pierced him, Balabandhu with a hundred,
then Takṣa with twenty-two, Puṣkara with nine arrows,
Vijaya with a hundred, and Jaya having overcome him with three arrows;
Śailūṣa pierced all of them in return with ten arrows each.
As if dancing on the floor of his chariot, the warrior of great strength and valour / cut through the bow of the high-souled Subāhu with a broad-headed arrow.
He likewise rendered the horses of Aṃśumat lifeless, O king, / and sliced through the lotus emblem standing on Govāsana's chariot.

1.189.d:
सुयोधनरथात्क्षिप्रं पातयामास सारथिम् ॥
बलबन्धोस्तथा छत्रं पातयामास यादव ॥ 14 ॥
तथान्यान्विमुखाम्̐श्चक्रे शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥
ततस्तस्य क्षुरप्रेण धनुश्चिच्छेद पुष्करः ॥ 15 ॥
अथान्यं चापमादाय पुष्करस्य रणे रुषा ॥
चकार तुरगान्सर्वान्निर्जीवान्समरप्रियः ॥ 16 ॥
पुष्करश्च समारुह्य तक्षस्य रथमुत्तमम् ॥
ववर्ष शरवर्षेण शैलूषरणमूर्धनि ॥ 17 ॥
शैलूषोपि जघानाश्वान्रथात्तक्षस्य यादव ॥
विरथौ तौ गदापाणी भ्रातरौ युद्धदुर्मदौ ॥ 18 ॥।
शैलूषेण समारूढौ गदाहस्तौ तरस्विनौ ॥
अभ्याशे भ्रातरौ दृष्ट्वा जगामादर्शनं ततः ॥ 19 ॥
मायावी स तु गन्धर्वो रथमुत्सृज्य यादव ॥
शून्यं दृष्ट्वा रथोपस्थं विलक्षौ भ्रातरौ तदा ॥ 1.263.20 ॥
1.189.m:
Quickly he struck down the charioteer from Suyodhana's chariot, / and likewise brought down Balabandhu's umbrella, O Yādava.
In the same way, he turned back the others with straight-jointed arrows. / Thereupon Puṣkara cut through his bow with a razor-faced arrow.
Then, taking up another bow in anger in that battle, / that lover of combat rendered all of Puṣkara's horses lifeless.
And Puṣkara, having mounted Takṣa's excellent chariot, / rained down a shower of arrows upon Śailūṣa's head in the battle.
Śailūṣa also slew the horses from Takṣa's chariot, O Yādava. / Deprived of their chariots, the two brothers, maces in hand, maddened with battle, / charged at Śailūṣa, swift and holding maces; / seeing the two brothers nearby, he then vanished from sight.
That Gandharva was an illusionist, O Yādava, and abandoned his chariot. / Seeing the floor of the chariot empty, the two brothers were then bewildered.

आदित्येऽस्तमनुप्राप्ते विनिवृत्तौ रणाजिरात् ॥
भरतोऽपि तथा कृत्वा गन्धर्वाणां महाहवम् ॥
न्यवर्तत महाराज सन्ध्याकाले रणाजिरात् ॥ 21 ॥
गत्वैव राजन्स च राजवेश्म तत्रोष्य रात्रिं रघुवंशनाथः ॥
निशावसाने पुनरेव बुद्धश्चकार युद्धं सहितो नृवीरः ॥ 22 ॥
1.264
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ततोऽह्नि पञ्चमे प्राप्ते भरतो युद्धदुर्मदः ॥
कल्यमुत्थाय राजेन्द्र कृतपूर्वाह्निकक्रियः ॥ 1 ॥
जगाम हन्तुं गन्धर्वान्बलमुत्सृज्य पृष्ठतः ॥
शैलूषोऽपि रणं त्यक्त्वा नरेन्द्रनिधनेप्सया ॥ 2 ॥
जगामैकरथेनैव रणकर्मविशारदः ॥
तयोरासीन्महाघोरः संप्रहारः सुदारुणः ॥ 3 ॥
देवासुररणप्रख्यः सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥
तयोस्तु युध्यतो राजन्गन्धर्वाणां बलार्णवम्॥4॥
छादयामास भरतः शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥
तच्च राज्ञामुदीर्णानां बलं सागरसन्निभम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.189.m:
When the sun had set, they withdrew from the battlefield. / Bharata also, having thus fought a great battle with the Gandharvas, / withdrew from the battlefield at twilight, O great king.
Having gone to the royal dwelling, O king, and passed the night there, the lord of Raghu's race, / the heroic leader of men, awake again at the end of the night, engaged in combat together with [his forces].
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, when the fifth day arrived, Bharata, maddened with battle, / rose early, O best of kings, and performed his morning rites.
Leaving his army behind, he went forth to slay the Gandharvas. / Śailūṣa, too, desiring the death of the king of men, / left the battle [line behind]
and went forward alone in his single chariot, skilled in the art of war. / Between the two of them there occurred an exceedingly dreadful, most terrible clash,
resembling the battle between gods and Asuras, towards the rising of the sun. / As the two fought, O king, Bharata covered
the ocean-like army of the Gandharvas with straight-jointed arrows; / and that ocean-like army of the fierce kings

बलमेधे विनिर्याते शरवृष्टिसदारुणे ॥6॥
धारयेतां महाराज शैलूषभरतावुभौ॥
अन्तरिक्षे शरव्रातांश्चिच्छिदतुररिन्दमौ ॥7॥
सैन्ययोश्च तथा चक्रुः कदनं घोरदर्शनम्॥

रणे विसस्रुर्भूपाल स्रवन्त्यो रक्तनिम्नगाः ॥
वहन्त्यो नरदेहानि यक्षराक्षसेविताः ॥ 9 ॥
ताभ्यां मुक्तै शरव्रातैर्गगने सूर्यरश्मयः ॥
न प्राकाशन्त राजेन्द्र एकच्छाये नभस्तले ॥
सैनिकान्घातयन्तौ तौ रक्षमाणौ च सारथी ॥ 1.264.10 ॥
छिन्दमानौ रणे वीरौ परमुक्ताम्̐स्तथायुधान् ॥
जनयामासतुर्वीरौ सुगणामपि विस्मयम् ॥ 11 ॥
तद्युद्धं पूजयामास पुष्पवर्षेण वासवः ॥
तौ प्रबुद्धौ दिनं सर्वं वरबाणधनुर्धरौ ॥ 12 ॥
1.189.m:
the Gandharva covered with arrows resembling venomous serpents. / In that offering of an army that went forth, in that terrible rain of arrows,
both Śailūṣa and Bharata held their ground, O great king; / both subduers of foes cut down the flights of arrows in mid-air.
They caused a slaughter gruesome to behold in both armies. / By the horses and elephants brought down by the arrows loosed from their bows,
rivers of blood flowed forth in the battle, O protector of the earth, / carrying human bodies and frequented by Yakṣas and Rākṣasas.
Because of the flights of arrows shot by the two, the rays of the sun / did not shine in the sky, O best of kings, as the vault of the heavens was reduced to a single shadow; / both were slaughtering the soldiers while protecting their own charioteers,
and as the two heroes cut down in the battle the weapons thrown by each other, / they aroused wonder even among the gods.
Vāsava honoured that combat with a shower of flowers. / Fully awake, holding excellent bows and arrows throughout the entire day,

athoṣyarātriṃ gṛhayoḥ praviṣṭau rātryantamāsādya tadā raṇāya ..
bhūyo mahendropama saṃprayātau praharṣayantau svabalāni vīrau .. 14 ....
1.265
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tatastu ṣaṣṭhe saṃprāpte divase bhūridakṣiṇe ..
cakratuḥ samaraṃ vīrau śailūṣabharatāvubhau .. 1..
sasainyau pṛthivīpāla śarairāśīviṣopamaiḥ ..
śailūṣeṇa samāsakto bharato vāhinīpatiḥ ..2..
sūryaraśmeśśareṇājau śiraściccheda śatruhā ..
sūryaraśmiṃ raṇe hatvā ekalavyaṃ mahāratham .. 3 ..
śareṇa pātayāmāsa rathopasthādariṃdamam ..
gandharvanṛpatirdṛṣṭvā pradhānau tau sutau hatau .. 4 ..
śaktyā bibheda vijayaṃ tathā cakreṇa puṣkaram ..

1.189.d:
नासीदेकतरस्यपि रणे तस्मिन्त्पराजयः ॥
ततोऽस्तं भगवत्यर्के प्रयाते पृथिवीपते ॥
परस्परस्यानुमते शिबिरायैव जग्मतुः ॥ 13॥
अथोष्यरात्रिं गृहयोः प्रविष्टौ रात्र्यन्तमासाद्य तदा रणाय ॥
भूयो महेन्द्रोपम संप्रयातौ प्रहर्षयन्तौ स्वबलानि वीरौ ॥ 14 ॥॥
1.265
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ततस्तु षष्ठे संप्राप्ते दिवसे भूरिदक्षिणे ॥
चक्रतुः समरं वीरौ शैलूषभरतावुभौ ॥ 1॥
ससैन्यौ पृथिवीपाल शरैराशीविषोपमैः ॥
शैलूषेण समासक्तो भरतो वाहिनीपतिः ॥2॥
सूर्यरश्मेश्शरेणाजौ शिरश्चिच्छेद शत्रुहा ॥
सूर्यरश्मिं रणे हत्वा एकलव्यं महारथम् ॥ 3 ॥
शरेण पातयामास रथोपस्थादरिंदमम् ॥
गन्धर्वनृपतिर्दृष्ट्वा प्रधानौ तौ सुतौ हतौ ॥ 4 ॥
शक्त्या बिभेद विजयं तथा चक्रेण पुष्करम् ॥
तोमरेण तथा तक्षं गदया च सुयोधनम् ॥ ॥ 5 ॥
1.189.m:
there was not defeat for either one of them in that battle. / Then, when the blessed sun had set, O lord of the earth, / with mutual consent they went to their respective camps.
Then, having entered their lodgings and stayed the night, reaching the end of the night, / the two heroes, comparable to Mahendra, went forth again for battle, gladdening their respective forces.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, when the sixth day arrived, [O king of] bountiful gifts, / both heroes, Śailūṣa and Bharata, joined in battle
along with their armies, O protector of the earth, with arrows resembling venomous serpents. / Closely engaged with Śailūṣa, Bharata, the leader of the army,
the slayer of foes, severed Sūryaraśmi's head with an arrow in battle. / Having slain Sūryaraśmi, he struck down the great chariot-warrior Ekalavya,
that subduer of foes, from the floor of his chariot with an arrow. / Seeing those two foremost sons of his slain,
the Gandharva king pierced Vijaya with a spear, Puṣkara with a discus, / Takṣa with a javelin, and Suyodhana with a mace.

1.189.s:
viviśuste rathopasthaṃ visaṃjñāḥ sarva eva tu ..
niyantṛbhiśca samarātsarva evāpavāhitāḥ .. 6 ..
tatastu bharataḥ kruddhaścaturbhistasya sāyakaiḥ ..
cakāra yudhi nirjīvāṃsturagāṃścaiva yādava .. 7 ..
cakāra ca śaravrātairvimukhīkṛtavikramam ..
tato dhairyeṇa saṃdhārya śaravegaṃ mahātmanaḥ .. 8 ..
āruroha rathaṃ śīghraṃ susannaddho mahābalaḥ ..
rathamāruhya vivyādha śareṇānataparvaṇā .. 9 ..
bharato hṛdaye gāḍhaṃ mumoha sa ca tāḍitaḥ ..
etasminnantare mukto hāhākāraḥ surāsuraiḥ .. 1.265.10 ..
aprahṛṣṭaiḥ prahṛṣṭaiśca vimūḍhe raghunandane ..
hāhākāreṇa mahatā labdhasaṃjñaḥ sa rāghavaḥ .. 11 ..
ākṛṣya balavaccāpaṃ śailūṣasya mahaddhanuḥ ..
dvidhā cakāra rājendra śailūṣaṃ cāhanadbhṛśam .. 12 ..
sa cchinnadhanvā vegena gadāmādāya satvaraḥ ..
preṣayāmāsa dharmajña bharatasya mahātmanaḥ .. 13 ..
1.189.d:
विविशुस्ते रथोपस्थं विसंज्ञाः सर्व एव तु ॥
नियन्तृभिश्च समरात्सर्व एवापवाहिताः ॥ 6 ॥
ततस्तु भरतः क्रुद्धश्चतुर्भिस्तस्य सायकैः ॥
चकार युधि निर्जीवांस्तुरगांश्चैव यादव ॥ 7 ॥
चकार च शरव्रातैर्विमुखीकृतविक्रमम् ॥
ततो धैर्येण संधार्य शरवेगं महात्मनः ॥ 8 ॥
आरुरोह रथं शीघ्रं सुसन्नद्धो महाबलः ॥
रथमारुह्य विव्याध शरेणानतपर्वणा ॥ 9 ॥
भरतो हृदये गाढं मुमोह स च ताडितः ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे मुक्तो हाहाकारः सुरासुरैः ॥ 1.265.10 ॥
अप्रहृष्टैः प्रहृष्टैश्च विमूढे रघुनन्दने ॥
हाहाकारेण महता लब्धसंज्ञः स राघवः ॥ 11 ॥
आकृष्य बलवच्चापं शैलूषस्य महद्धनुः ॥
द्विधा चकार राजेन्द्र शैलूषं चाहनद्भृशम् ॥ 12 ॥
स च्छिन्नधन्वा वेगेन गदामादाय सत्वरः ॥
प्रेषयामास धर्मज्ञ भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥ 13 ॥
1.189.m:
They all collapsed onto the floor of their chariots, unconscious, / and were all carried away from the battle by their charioteers.
Then Bharata, enraged, with four arrows, / rendered [Śailūṣa's] horses lifeless in the combat, O Yādava,
and with flights of arrows he thwarted his prowess. / Then, checking the force of the high-souled [Bharata's] arrows with steadfastness,
[Śailūṣa], mighty and well-armoured, quickly mounted [another] chariot. / Having mounted the chariot, he deeply pierced Bharata in the chest
with a straight-jointed arrow, and, struck [by it], Bharata swooned. / At that moment, a cry of dismay was raised by gods and Asuras,
the one [side] despondent and the other overjoyed, as the descendant of Raghu was stupefied. / Through that loud cry of dismay, that descendant of Raghu regained his senses;
drawing his bow forcefully, he cut the great bow of Śailūṣa / into two pieces, O best of kings, and struck Śailūṣa severely.
His bow severed, swiftly taking up a mace with speed, / he hurled it, O knower of dharma, at the high-souled Bharata.

1.189.s:
āpatantīṃ gadāṃ dṛṣṭvā bharato raṇamūrdhani ..
dvidhā cakāra cakreṇa sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ .. 14 ..
tataḥ sa parighaṃ śīghraṃ cikṣepa bharataṃ prati ..
tamāpatantaṃ ciccheda caturbhiḥ sāyakairdṛḍham .. 15 ..
tato'nyaddhanurādāya sāyakānekaviṃśatim ..
cikṣepa sa mahārāja bharatasya rathaṃ prati.. 16 ..
chittvā tānbharataḥ sarvānnavadhīttasya sārathim ..
tathā ca caturo vāhānanayadyamasādanam .. 17 ..
śailūṣaṃ virathaṃ dṛṣṭvā gandharvāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ ..
vavarṣāyudhavarṣeṇa megho vṛṣṭyeva parvatam .. 18 ..
sa mohayitvā bharataṃ mokṣayāmāsa pārthiva ..
mokṣayitvā ca rājānaṃ gate'staṃ ravimaṇḍale ..19..
kṛtvāvahāraṃ tu gataḥ śibirāya narādhipaḥ ..1.265.20..
hatvā rathe nāgarathāśvayodhānsaṃprāpya madhye niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ ..
raghupravīro'pi gṛhāya yātaḥ saṃpūjyamāno bhuvi mānavendraiḥ .. 21 ..
1.189.d:
आपतन्तीं गदां दृष्ट्वा भरतो रणमूर्धनि ॥
द्विधा चकार चक्रेण सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ॥ 14 ॥
ततः स परिघं शीघ्रं चिक्षेप भरतं प्रति ॥
तमापतन्तं चिच्छेद चतुर्भिः सायकैर्दृढम् ॥ 15 ॥
ततोऽन्यद्धनुरादाय सायकानेकविंशतिम् ॥
चिक्षेप स महाराज भरतस्य रथं प्रति॥ 16 ॥
छित्त्वा तान्भरतः सर्वान्नवधीत्तस्य सारथिम् ॥
तथा च चतुरो वाहाननयद्यमसादनम् ॥ 17 ॥
शैलूषं विरथं दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वाणां महाचमूः ॥
ववर्षायुधवर्षेण मेघो वृष्ट्येव पर्वतम् ॥ 18 ॥
स मोहयित्वा भरतं मोक्षयामास पार्थिव ॥
मोक्षयित्वा च राजानं गतेऽस्तं रविमण्डले ॥19॥
कृत्वावहारं तु गतः शिबिराय नराधिपः ॥1.265.20॥
हत्वा रथे नागरथाश्वयोधान्संप्राप्य मध्ये निशितैः पृषत्कैः ॥
रघुप्रवीरोऽपि गृहाय यातः संपूज्यमानो भुवि मानवेन्द्रैः ॥ 21 ॥
1.189.m:
Seeing the mace flying towards him at the front of the battle, / Bharata cut it in two with a discus, before the eyes of the entire army.
Then he swiftly hurled an iron club towards Bharata; / as it was flying toward him, he firmly severed it with four arrows.
Then, seizing another bow, O great king, / he hurled twenty-one arrows towards Bharata's chariot.
Splitting all of them, Bharata killed his charioteer, / and likewise sent his four horses to the abode of Yama.
Seeing Śailūṣa deprived of his chariot, the great army of the Gandharvas / rained down a shower of weapons, like a cloud [raining] water upon a mountain.
Bewildering Bharata, it rescued [him], O king; / and having rescued the king, when the disc of the sun had set,
having sounded the retreat, the lord of men went to his camp.
Having slain the warriors on elephants, chariots, and horses in their midst with sharp arrows from his chariot, / the foremost hero of the Raghus also went to his dwelling, praised on earth by the lords of men.

1.190.s:
1.266
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tatastu saptame prāpte divase yuddhadurmadau ..
samīyaturmahātmānau śailūṣabharatāvubhau .. 1 ..
1.190.d:
1.266
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ततस्तु सप्तमे प्राप्ते दिवसे युद्धदुर्मदौ ॥
समीयतुर्महात्मानौ शैलूषभरतावुभौ ॥ 1 ॥
1.190.m: 1.266 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, when the seventh day arrived, the two high-souled warriors, / both Śailūṣa and Bharata, passionate for battle, met.

1.190.s:
tatastu bharataḥ prāha śailūṣaṃ yuddhadurmadam ..
āvayoḥ prastutaṃ sainyaṃ kimetaissainikairmṛtaiḥ .. 2 ..
1.190.d:
ततस्तु भरतः प्राह शैलूषं युद्धदुर्मदम् ॥
आवयोः प्रस्तुतं सैन्यं किमेतैस्सैनिकैर्मृतैः ॥ 2 ॥
1.190.m: Then Bharata spoke to Śailūṣa, who was passionate for battle: / 'Our army is prepared; what is the use of these dead soldiers?

1.190.s:
nivārayasva sainyaṃ svaṃ vārayiṣyāmyahaṃ svakam ..
āvayordvairathaṃ yuddhaṃ paśyantu vasudhādhipāḥ .. 3 ..
1.190.d:
निवारयस्व सैन्यं स्वं वारयिष्याम्यहं स्वकम् ॥
आवयोर्द्वैरथं युद्धं पश्यन्तु वसुधाधिपाः ॥ 3 ॥
1.190.m: Restrain your own army, and I shall restrain mine; / let the rulers of the earth watch a duel of single chariots between the two of us,

1.190.s:
tvadīyāḥ sainikā ye ca suranāthāḥ sahāmaraiḥ ..
hate mayi madīyanta sainyaṃ kāmaṃ prayudhyatām .. 4 ..
1.190.d:
त्वदीयाः सैनिका ये च सुरनाथाः सहामरैः ॥
हते मयि मदीयन्त सैन्यं कामं प्रयुध्यताम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.190.m: as well as your soldiers, and the lords of the gods together with the immortals. / If I am slain, let my army fight at will,

1.190.s:
saṃgrāmaṃ vā karotvājau tvadīyantu hate tvayi ..
evamuktastathetyuktvā vārayāmāsa sainikān .. 5 ..
1.190.d:
संग्रामं वा करोत्वाजौ त्वदीयन्तु हते त्वयि ॥
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा वारयामास सैनिकान् ॥ 5 ॥
1.190.m: or let yours do battle in the field if you are slain.' / Being addressed thus, he said, 'So be it,' and restrained his soldiers,

1.190.s:
gandharvarāṭ sa śailūṣo bharato'pi tathā svakān ..
tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tayordevāsuropamam .. 6 ..
1.190.d:
गन्धर्वराट् स शैलूषो भरतोऽपि तथा स्वकान् ॥
ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तयोर्देवासुरोपमम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.190.m: that king of the Gandharvas, Śailūṣa, and Bharata likewise his own. / Then a battle began between the two of them, like that of the gods and asuras,

1.190.s:
paśyatāṃ sarva sainyānāṃ devānāmapi paśyatām ..
śarajālena mahatā chāditārkakare raṇe .. 7 ..
1.190.d:
पश्यतां सर्व सैन्यानां देवानामपि पश्यताम् ॥
शरजालेन महता छादितार्ककरे रणे ॥ 7 ॥
1.190.m: while all the armies looked on, and even while the gods looked on, / in a conflict where the rays of the sun were covered by a great net of arrows.

1.190.s:
tatakṣatustāvanyo'nyaṃ śaraiḥ sannataparvabhiḥ ..
parasparaśarāghāta visaracchoṇitokṣitau .. 8 ..
1.190.d:
ततक्षतुस्तावन्योऽन्यं शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥
परस्परशराघात विसरच्छोणितोक्षितौ ॥ 8 ॥
1.190.m: The two slashed each other with straight-jointed arrows; / sprayed with blood flowing from the strikes of each other's arrows,

1.190.s:
virejatustau rājendra puṣpitāviva kiṃśukau ..
ubhau mahārathau vīrau cobhau viśrutapauruṣau .. 9 ..
1.190.d:
विरेजतुस्तौ राजेन्द्र पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ ॥
उभौ महारथौ वीरौ चोभौ विश्रुतपौरुषौ ॥ 9 ॥
1.190.m: the two shone, O best of kings, like two blossoming kiṃśuka trees. / Both were great chariot-warriors, heroes, and both of renowned prowess,

1.190.s:
tathobhau varadhānuṣkau cobhau samaradurmadau ..
kāñcanāṅgarathasthau tau cobhau saddhvajaśobhitau .. 1.266.10 ..
1.190.d:
तथोभौ वरधानुष्कौ चोभौ समरदुर्मदौ ॥
काञ्चनाङ्गरथस्थौ तौ चोभौ सद्ध्वजशोभितौ ॥ 1.266.10 ॥
1.190.m: and both were excellent archers, and both passionate in battle; / mounted on chariots with gold fittings, both were adorned with noble standards,

1.190.s:
vījyamānau tathaivobhau yodhābhyāṃ varacāmaraiḥ ..
chatrayostau tadādhastācchuśubhāte mahārathau .. 11 ..
1.190.d:
वीज्यमानौ तथैवोभौ योधाभ्यां वरचामरैः ॥
छत्रयोस्तौ तदाधस्ताच्छुशुभाते महारथौ ॥ 11 ॥
1.190.m: and both were likewise fanned by warriors with excellent chowries; / beneath their two parasols, the two great chariot-warriors shone at that time.

1.190.s:
ubhāvastrapratāpena cakratustumulaṃ raṇam ..
astrayuddhaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā śarayuddhaṃ pracakratuḥ .. 12 ..
1.190.d:
उभावस्त्रप्रतापेन चक्रतुस्तुमुलं रणम् ॥
अस्त्रयुद्धं चिरं कृत्वा शरयुद्धं प्रचक्रतुः ॥ 12 ॥
1.190.m: Both engaged in a tumultuous fight with the power of divine weapons; / having fought for a long time with divine weapons, they waged a battle of arrows.

1.190.s:
śarayuddhe vyatikrānte astrayuddhaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
evaṃ tau divasaṃ kṛtvā yuddhaṃ saṃśrāntavāhanau .. 13 ..
1.190.d:
शरयुद्धे व्यतिक्रान्ते अस्त्रयुद्धं पुनःपुनः ॥
एवं तौ दिवसं कृत्वा युद्धं संश्रान्तवाहनौ ॥ 13 ॥
1.190.m: When the battle of arrows had passed, [they fought] again and again with divine weapons; / having fought in this way for a day, their steeds exhausted,

1.190.s:
ropayantau śramaṃ rājansamareṣu jitaśramau ..
tato gandharvarājastu lambamāne divākare .. 14 ..
1.190.d:
रोपयन्तौ श्रमं राजन्समरेषु जितश्रमौ ॥
ततो गन्धर्वराजस्तु लम्बमाने दिवाकरे ॥ 14 ॥
1.190.m: healing their weariness, O king, having overcome exhaustion in battles; / then, as the sun was setting, the king of the Gandharvas

1.190.s:
cakāra tāmasīṃ māyāṃ yayāndhamabhavajjagat ..
andhakāre tato jāte vāco'śrūyanta dāruṇāḥ .. .. 15 ..
1.190.d:
चकार तामसीं मायां ययान्धमभवज्जगत् ॥
अन्धकारे ततो जाते वाचोऽश्रूयन्त दारुणाः ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
1.190.m: created an illusion of darkness by which the world became blind; / then, when darkness had arisen, dreadful voices were heard:

1.190.s:
bharato hanyatāṃ śīghraṃ bhakṣyatāṃ pātyatāṃ tathā ..
abhyavartanta bharataṃ sarpavṛścikakarkaṭāḥ .. 16 ..
1.190.d:
भरतो हन्यतां शीघ्रं भक्ष्यतां पात्यतां तथा ॥
अभ्यवर्तन्त भरतं सर्पवृश्चिककर्कटाः ॥ 16 ॥
1.190.m: 'Let Bharata be quickly slain! Let him be devoured! And let him be struck down!' / Serpents, scorpions, and crabs advanced against Bharata,

1.190.s:
markaṭā vānarā ghorāḥ sṛgālā dvīpinastathā ..
siṃhavyāghravarāhāśca kravyādā ye ca jātayaḥ .. 17 ..
1.190.d:
मर्कटा वानरा घोराः सृगाला द्वीपिनस्तथा ॥
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाश्च क्रव्यादा ये च जातयः ॥ 17 ॥
1.190.m: as did monkeys, terrible apes, jackals, and leopards, / lions, tigers, boars, and whatever kinds of carnivorous beasts [there are].

1.190.s:
ardyamānaḥ sa dharmātmā bharatastaiḥ sudurmukhaiḥ ..
saureṇāstreṇa tāṃ māyāṃ babhañja paravīrahā .. 18 ..
1.190.d:
अर्द्यमानः स धर्मात्मा भरतस्तैः सुदुर्मुखैः ॥
सौरेणास्त्रेण तां मायां बभञ्ज परवीरहा ॥ 18 ॥
1.190.m: Tormented by those fierce-faced creatures, that righteous / Bharata, slayer of enemy heroes, shattered that illusion with the weapon of the Sun.

1.190.s:
tatastu mahatīṃ māyāṃ sa cakāra mahābhujaḥ ..
uttasthau sumahānmeghaśchādayitvā nabhastalam..19..
1.190.d:
ततस्तु महतीं मायां स चकार महाभुजः ॥
उत्तस्थौ सुमहान्मेघश्छादयित्वा नभस्तलम्॥19॥
1.190.m: Then that mighty-armed one created a great illusion: / a colossal cloud arose, covering the vault of the sky,

1.190.s:
pravavarṣa ca ghorāṇi śastrajālānyanekaśaḥ ..
nārācānardhanārācām̐stathaiva caṣakānanān .. 1.266.20 ..
1.190.d:
प्रववर्ष च घोराणि शस्त्रजालान्यनेकशः ॥
नाराचानर्धनाराचाम्̐स्तथैव चषकाननान् ॥ 1.266.20 ॥
1.190.m: and rained down manifold terrible masses of weapons: / iron arrows, half-iron shafts, and likewise cup-mouthed arrows,

1.190.s:
vatsadantām̐stathā vallānkarṇinālīkagomukhān ..
kṣuraprānardhacandrāṃśca varāhavadanāṃstathā .. 21 ..
1.190.d:
वत्सदन्ताम्̐स्तथा वल्लान्कर्णिनालीकगोमुखान् ॥
क्षुरप्रानर्धचन्द्रांश्च वराहवदनांस्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.190.m: calf-toothed arrows, vallas, barbed arrows, tubular arrows, ox-faced arrows, / razor-faced arrows, crescent-headed shafts, and boar-faced arrows,

1.190.s:
gadābhuśuṇḍīḥ prāsāṃśca bhiṇḍipālānparaśvadhān ..
huḍānguḍānsalaguḍām̐ścakrakhaḍgāṃstathā parān . .. 22 ..
1.190.d:
गदाभुशुण्डीः प्रासांश्च भिण्डिपालान्परश्वधान् ॥
हुडान्गुडान्सलगुडाम्̐श्चक्रखड्गांस्तथा परान् ॥। 22 ॥
1.190.m: clubs, bhuśuṇḍīs, darts, javelins, axes, / huḍas, guḍas together with bludgeons, discuses, swords, and others.

1.190.s:
etānanyāṃśca vividhānvavarṣa paramāyudhān..
patadbhirāyudhairghorairvādhyamānaḥ sa rāghavaḥ .. 23 ..
1.190.d:
एतानन्यांश्च विविधान्ववर्ष परमायुधान्॥
पतद्भिरायुधैर्घोरैर्वाध्यमानः स राघवः ॥ 23 ॥
1.190.m: These and various other supreme weapons he showered down. / Being afflicted by the terrible falling weapons, that descendant of Raghu

1.190.s:
vāyavyāstreṇa tāṃ māyāṃ nāśayāmāsa śatruhā ..
tato babhūva rājendra gandharvaḥ parvato mahān .. 24 ..
1.190.d:
वायव्यास्त्रेण तां मायां नाशयामास शत्रुहा ॥
ततो बभूव राजेन्द्र गन्धर्वः पर्वतो महान् ॥ 24 ॥
1.190.m: destroyed that illusion with the weapon of the Wind, that slayer of foes. / Then, O best of kings, the Gandharva became a great mountain,

1.190.s:
kṣaratprasravaṇo ghoraḥ śikharaiśca samucchritaiḥ ..
māyāṃ tāṃ pārvatīṃ śrīmānvajrāstreṇa raghūdvahaḥ .. 25 ..
1.190.d:
क्षरत्प्रस्रवणो घोरः शिखरैश्च समुच्छ्रितैः ॥
मायां तां पार्वतीं श्रीमान्वज्रास्त्रेण रघूद्वहः ॥ 25 ॥
1.190.m: dreadful with flowing torrents and lofty peaks. / With the weapon of the Thunderbolt, the glorious scion of Raghu

1.190.s:
nāśayāmāsa rājendra sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ ..
hanyamānāsu māyāsu rūpām̐ścakre sudāruṇān .. 26 ..
1.190.d:
नाशयामास राजेन्द्र सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ॥
हन्यमानासु मायासु रूपाम्̐श्चक्रे सुदारुणान् ॥ 26 ॥
1.190.m: destroyed that mountainous illusion, O best of kings, while all the army looked on. / As his illusions were being destroyed, he assumed exceedingly terrible forms

1.190.s:
yakṣāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca piśācānāṃ patattriṇām ..
siṃhavyāghratarakṣūṇāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 27 ..
1.190.d:
यक्षाणां राक्षसानां च पिशाचानां पतत्त्रिणाम् ॥
सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षूणां कुञ्जराणां तथैव च ॥ 27 ॥
1.190.m: of yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśācas, and birds, / and likewise of lions, tigers, hyenas, and elephants.

1.190.s:
babhañja tasya māyāstā divyāstrairbharato ruṣā ..
hanyamānāsu māyāsu lāghavādbharataṃ raṇe .. 28 ..
1.190.d:
बभञ्ज तस्य मायास्ता दिव्यास्त्रैर्भरतो रुषा ॥
हन्यमानासु मायासु लाघवाद्भरतं रणे ॥ 28 ॥
1.190.m: Bharata angrily shattered those illusions of his with divine weapons. / While his illusions were being destroyed, in the battle, through his agility,

1.190.s:
mohayāmāsa rājendra śailūṣo raṇadarpitaḥ ..
bharato'pi dhanuṣkoṭyāṃ śarāgre ca nilīyate..29..
1.190.d:
मोहयामास राजेन्द्र शैलूषो रणदर्पितः ॥
भरतोऽपि धनुष्कोट्यां शराग्रे च निलीयते॥29॥
1.190.m: Śailūṣa, proud in battle, bewildered Bharata, O best of kings. / And Bharata concealed himself on the tip of the bow and on the point of the arrow,

1.190.s:
dhvajāgre ca rathāgre ca turagāgre punaḥ punaḥ ..
sāyakānbhāratāñśaighryāddhvaṃsayāmāsa yādava .. 1.266.30..
1.190.d:
ध्वजाग्रे च रथाग्रे च तुरगाग्रे पुनः पुनः ॥
सायकान्भारताञ्शैघ्र्याद्ध्वंसयामास यादव ॥ 1.266.30॥
1.190.m: and on the tip of the standard, the front of the chariot, and the head of the horse repeatedly; / with swiftness, O descendant of Yadu, he destroyed Bharata's arrows.

1.190.s:
rāghavāstutuṣustasya devadaityāśca saṃghaśaḥ ..
asurā mumucurghoramaṭṭahāsaṃ sudāruṇama ..31..
1.190.d:
राघवास्तुतुषुस्तस्य देवदैत्याश्च संघशः ॥
असुरा मुमुचुर्घोरमट्टहासं सुदारुणम ॥31॥
1.190.m: The descendants of Raghu were pleased with him, as were the gods and daityas in crowds; / the asuras released a terrible, exceedingly dreadful roar of laughter.

1.190.s:
daityānāmaṭṭahāsena bharataḥ kupito bhṛśam ..
nārāyaṇāstraṃ saṃyojya śareṇānataparvaṇā..32..
1.190.d:
दैत्यानामट्टहासेन भरतः कुपितो भृशम् ॥
नारायणास्त्रं संयोज्य शरेणानतपर्वणा॥32॥
1.190.m: At the loud laughter of the daityas, Bharata was greatly enraged; / having fitted the weapon of Nārāyaṇa with a straight-jointed arrow,

1.190.s:
iyeṣa hantuṃ taṃ krodhādgandharvaṃ raṇagarvitam ..
astraṃ tatsaṃhṛtaṃ jñātvā jagāma svaṃ rathaṃ tvaran ..33..
1.190.d:
इयेष हन्तुं तं क्रोधाद्गन्धर्वं रणगर्वितम् ॥
अस्त्रं तत्संहृतं ज्ञात्वा जगाम स्वं रथं त्वरन् ॥33॥
1.190.m: he wished in fury to slay that Gandharva proud in battle. / Knowing that weapon to be withdrawn, he went swiftly to his own chariot.

1.190.s:
iyeṣa hantuṃ taṃ cāstraṃ rudrāstreṇa tu dāruṇam..
etasminneva kāle tu mumoca bharataḥ śaram..34..
1.190.d:
इयेष हन्तुं तं चास्त्रं रुद्रास्त्रेण तु दारुणम्॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मुमोच भरतः शरम्॥34॥
1.190.m: And he wished to slay that dreadful weapon with the weapon of Rudra; / and at that very moment Bharata released an arrow,

1.190.s:
kālānalasamaprakhyaṃ sapuṅkhaṃ saphalaṃ tathā ..
rājitaṃ vainateyasya pakṣaiḥ śatruvināśanam .. 35 ..
1.190.d:
कालानलसमप्रख्यं सपुङ्खं सफलं तथा ॥
राजितं वैनतेयस्य पक्षैः शत्रुविनाशनम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.190.m: resembling the fire of destruction, with shaft and point, / shining with the feathers of Vainateya, destroying foes.

1.190.s:
hatvā rudrāstravegantu rathasthasya mahīpateḥ ..
bibheda hṛdayaṃ rājanvarma bhittvātha kāñcanam .. 36 ..
1.190.d:
हत्वा रुद्रास्त्रवेगन्तु रथस्थस्य महीपतेः ॥
बिभेद हृदयं राजन्वर्म भित्त्वाथ काञ्चनम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.190.m:
Destroying the force of the Rudra-weapon, it pierced the golden armour
and then the heart, O king, of the lord of the earth standing in his chariot.

1.190.s:
rājñaśca hadayaṃ bhittvā bhittvā ca vasudhātalam ..
snātvā rasātalāmbhaḥsu tūṇaṃ punarupāgamat ..37..
1.190.d:
राज्ञश्च हदयं भित्त्वा भित्त्वा च वसुधातलम् ॥
स्नात्वा रसातलाम्भःसु तूणं पुनरुपागमत् ॥37॥
1.190.m:
And having pierced the king's heart and split the surface of the earth,
it bathed in the waters of the netherworld and returned swiftly to the quiver.

1.190.s:
gandharvarājo'bhihataḥ śareṇā nataparvaṇā ..
rathanīḍe dhanustyaktvā mamāra paravīrahā .. 38 ..
1.190.d:
गन्धर्वराजोऽभिहतः शरेणा नतपर्वणा ॥
रथनीडे धनुस्त्यक्त्वा ममार परवीरहा ॥ 38 ॥
1.190.m:
Struck down by that straight-jointed arrow, the king of the Gandharvas,
slayer of enemy heroes, dropped his bow in the chariot-box and died.

1.190.s:
pitaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā śailūṣatanayā raṇe ..
krodhaduḥkhaparītānte bharataṃ raṇakarkaśam .. .. 39 ..
1.190.d:
पितरं निहतं दृष्ट्वा शैलूषतनया रणे ॥
क्रोधदुःखपरीतान्ते भरतं रणकर्कशम् ॥ ॥ 39 ॥
1.190.m:
Seeing their father slain in battle, the sons of Śailūṣa,
filled with wrath and sorrow, [surrounded] Bharata, who was fierce in battle.

1.190.s:
vivyadhurbhūpatiśreṣṭha bāṇairāśīviṣopamaiḥ ..
āyudhairvividhākāraistadā te vai raṇājire .. 1.266.40 ..
1.190.d:
विव्यधुर्भूपतिश्रेष्ठ बाणैराशीविषोपमैः ॥
आयुधैर्विविधाकारैस्तदा ते वै रणाजिरे ॥ 1.266.40 ॥
1.190.m:
They pierced him, O best of kings, with arrows resembling venomous serpents,
and then with weapons of diverse forms on the field of battle.

1.190.s:
māyāśca vividhāścakrurbharatasya vipattaye ..
antarikṣaṃ ca tairvyāptaṃ nānāhetipravarṣibhiḥ .. 41 ..
1.190.d:
मायाश्च विविधाश्चक्रुर्भरतस्य विपत्तये ॥
अन्तरिक्षं च तैर्व्याप्तं नानाहेतिप्रवर्षिभिः ॥ 41 ॥
1.190.m:
They also wrought diverse illusions for Bharata's destruction,
and the sky was filled by them raining down various missiles.

1.190.s:
astraiśca kecidbharataṃ pravavarṣurmahārathāḥ ..
bhūribhāvātsa yodhānāṃ mahāstrāṇāṃ mahābalāt .. 42 ..
1.190.d:
अस्त्रैश्च केचिद्भरतं प्रववर्षुर्महारथाः ॥
भूरिभावात्स योधानां महास्त्राणां महाबलात् ॥ 42 ॥
1.190.m:
And some great chariot-warriors showered Bharata with divine weapons.
Because of the vast multitude of warriors and the great might of their supreme weapons,

1.190.s:
pratāpādastrajālānāṃ saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ ..
kālāstramatha sāṃvartaṃ mumoca bharatastadā .. 43 ..
1.190.d:
प्रतापादस्त्रजालानां संशयं परमं गताः ॥
कालास्त्रमथ सांवर्तं मुमोच भरतस्तदा ॥ 43 ॥
1.190.m:
and the fiery power of the nets of weapons, they fell into the greatest peril.
Then Bharata released the Kālāstra, the weapon of cosmic dissolution.

1.190.s:
tasmādastrātsahasrāṇi śastrāṇāṃ niryayustadā ..
gandharvasainyaṃ sakalamastraistaiḥ pratyahanyata .. 44 ..
1.190.d:
तस्मादस्त्रात्सहस्राणि शस्त्राणां निर्ययुस्तदा ॥
गन्धर्वसैन्यं सकलमस्त्रैस्तैः प्रत्यहन्यत ॥ 44 ॥
1.190.m:
From that weapon thousands of blades then issued forth;
by those weapons the entire army of the Gandharvas was struck down.

1.190.s:
śastraiḥ kecidviśirasaḥ kṛtvā gandharvasattamāḥ ..
vivāhāśca kṛtāḥ kaicitkecidrājandvidhā kṛtāḥ .. 45 ..
1.190.d:
शस्त्रैः केचिद्विशिरसः कृत्वा गन्धर्वसत्तमाः ॥
विवाहाश्च कृताः कैचित्केचिद्राजन्द्विधा कृताः ॥ 45 ॥
1.190.m:
Some of the foremost Gandharvas were made headless by the blades;
some were severed of arms, and some, O king, were cut in two.

1.190.s:
kecidvivāhavaścaiva kecidvyaṅgāśca yādava ..
gandharvāṇāṃ ca tāḥ koṭyastisraḥ saṃgrāmaśālinām .. 46 ..
1.190.d:
केचिद्विवाहवश्चैव केचिद्व्यङ्गाश्च यादव ॥
गन्धर्वाणां च ताः कोट्यस्तिस्रः संग्रामशालिनाम् ॥ 46 ॥
1.190.m:
Some were deprived of their arms, and some were mutilated of limbs, O Yādava.
And those three hundred million Gandharvas, renowned in battle,

1.190.s:
kṣaṇenāstraprapātena bharatena nipā titāḥ ..
gandharvasainye nihate pravavurmārutāḥ śivāḥ .. 47 ..
1.190.d:
क्षणेनास्त्रप्रपातेन भरतेन निपा तिताः ॥
गन्धर्वसैन्ये निहते प्रववुर्मारुताः शिवाः ॥ 47 ॥
1.190.m:
were struck down in an instant by the fall of Bharata's weapon.
When the army of the Gandharvas was slain, auspicious winds blew.

1.190.s:
puṣpavarṣaṃ papātātha bharatasya tu mūrdhani ..
diśaśca nirmalībhūtā devānāṃ vigataṃ bhayam .. 48 ..
1.190.d:
पुष्पवर्षं पपाताथ भरतस्य तु मूर्धनि ॥
दिशश्च निर्मलीभूता देवानां विगतं भयम् ॥ 48 ॥
1.190.m:
A shower of flowers then fell upon Bharata's head;
the quarters became clear, and the fear of the gods departed.

1.190.s:
tato devaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sarvaiḥ suragaṇaiḥ samam ..
vimānastho babhāṣedaṃ bharataṃ dharmavatsalam .. 49 ..
1.190.d:
ततो देवः सहस्राक्षः सर्वैः सुरगणैः समम् ॥
विमानस्थो बभाषेदं भरतं धर्मवत्सलम् ॥ 49 ॥
1.190.m:
Then the thousand-eyed god, along with all the hosts of gods,
situated in his celestial chariot, spoke thus to Bharata, who was devoted to dharma:

1.190.s:
indra uvāca .. ..
pitāmahavarodrekādavadhyaṃ devatāgaṇaiḥ ..
hatavānasi śailūṣaṃ devabrāhmaṇakaṇṭakam .. 1.266.50 ..
1.190.d:
इन्द्र उवाच ॥ ॥
पितामहवरोद्रेकादवध्यं देवतागणैः ॥
हतवानसि शैलूषं देवब्राह्मणकण्टकम् ॥ 1.266.50 ॥

1.190.s:
yasmāttasmādvaraṃ matto gṛhāṇa raghunandana ..
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
śatakratorniśamyaitadbharato vākyamabravīt .. 51 ..
1.190.d:
यस्मात्तस्माद्वरं मत्तो गृहाण रघुनन्दन ॥
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
शतक्रतोर्निशम्यैतद्भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 51 ॥
1.190.m:
Therefore, receive a boon from me, O descendant of Raghu.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having heard this speech of Śatakratu, Bharata said:

1.190.s:
.. bharata uvāca .. ..
tvamīśaḥ sarvadevānāṃ tavedaṃ sakalaṃ jagat ..
acireṇaiva maraṇaṃ tvadājñābhaṅgakāraṇāma .. 52 ..
1.190.d:
॥ भरत उवाच ॥ ॥
त्वमीशः सर्वदेवानां तवेदं सकलं जगत् ॥
अचिरेणैव मरणं त्वदाज्ञाभङ्गकारणाम ॥ 52 ॥
1.190.m:
Bharata said:
You are the lord of all the gods; this entire world belongs to you.
Death comes before long because of disobedience to your command.

1.190.s:
bhavaṃtīha sadā loke nimittaṃ madvidho janaḥ ..
prajāpatikṛtaṃ bhedaṃ ko moktuṃ jagati kṣamaḥ .. 53 ..
1.190.d:

॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
आदित्येऽस्तमनुप्राप्ते सन्ध्याकाले सुदारुणे ॥
निवर्तयामास रथं युधाजिद्भरतस्य च ॥ 1 ॥
निवर्तयानश्च रथं भरतं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
संग्राममेदिनीं पश्य स्वकृतां रघुनन्दन ॥ 2 ॥
गन्धर्वाङ्गसमाकीर्णां हतकुञ्जरभूषणाम ॥
तुरङ्गमगणाकीर्णां वरायुधधरां धराम् ॥ 3 ॥
संपूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमैर्दष्टोष्ठै श्चारुकुण्डलैः ॥
भृकुटीतटदुष्प्रेक्ष्यैर्मस्तकैर्भाति मेदिनी ॥ 4 ॥
पञ्चशीर्षोरगाकारैर्वराङ्गदविभूषणैः ॥
बाहुभिर्भाति शूराणां वसुधा वसुधाधिप ॥ 5 ॥
पद्मपत्रदलाकारैर्गेन्धर्वाणां तथा करैः ॥
भाति सायकविच्छिन्नैः सपद्मेव वसुन्धरा ॥ 6 ॥
1.190.m:
That foremost hero of Raghu's race as well, having slain the enemies of Maghavan in battle and received the granting of boons,
shining with supreme renown, O king, went to his own city in great joy.
1.267
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When the sun had set, at the dreadful twilight hour,
Yudhājit caused Bharata's chariot to turn back.
And turning the chariot back, he addressed Bharata with these words:
'Look upon the field of battle made by yourself, O descendant of Raghu,
strewn with the limbs of Gandharvas, decorated with slain elephants,
covered with herds of horses, and bearing excellent weapons upon the earth.
The earth shines with severed heads resembling full moons, their lips bitten,
adorned with beautiful earrings, dreadful to behold with knitted brows.
The earth shines, O lord of the earth, with the arms of heroes,
resembling five-headed serpents, adorned with excellent armlets.
And with the hands of the Gandharvas resembling lotus petals,
severed by arrows, the earth shines as though covered in lotuses.

हस्तिहस्तसमाकारैर्गन्धर्वाणां तथा करैः ॥
विभाति वसुधाकीर्णा वरचन्दनभूषितैः ॥ 7 ॥
त्वदेकशरनिर्भिन्नैर्गण्डशैलोपमैर्गजैः ॥
उद्भ्रान्तजीवितैः पश्य विनिकीर्णधरातलम् ॥ 8 ॥
आविष्कृतरदैश्चाश्वैर्विवृताक्षैस्तथैव च ॥
पतितैरावृता पश्य तुरङ्गैर्मेदिनी रणे ॥ 9 ॥
आतपत्रेः शशाङ्काभैश्चामरैश्च विराजिताम्॥
योक्त्रैः खलीनैः पल्याणैः कुथाभिः कम्बुभिस्तथा ॥ 1.267.10 ॥
केशैर्दण्डैस्तथा चापैः प्रासैः खडगैः परश्वधैः ॥
शरैर्नानाप्रकारैश्च नानानामाङ्कितैः शुभैः ॥ 11 ॥
मुकुटैरङ्गदैर्हारैः कुण्डलैरपि शोभिताम् ॥
रघुनाथ भुवं पश्य कारुण्येऽपि मनोहराम् ॥ 12 ॥
गन्धर्वान्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च क्रव्याद्भिर्मृगपक्षिभिः ॥
पश्य त्वं चारुसर्वाङ्गं सर्वाभरणभूषितम ॥ 13 ॥
1.190.m:
The earth, strewn with the arms of the Gandharvas,
which resemble the trunks of elephants and are adorned with choice sandalwood, shines resplendent.
Look upon the earth's surface strewn with elephants resembling massive boulders,
pierced by your single arrow, their lives fled.
Behold the earth in battle covered with fallen steeds,
their teeth bared and their eyes wide open,
adorned with parasols shining like the moon and with chowries,
with straps, bits, saddles, housings, and conches,
with hair, clubs, bows, spears, swords, battle-axes,
and with various kinds of auspicious arrows marked with diverse names,
and adorned with diadems, armlets, necklaces, and earrings.
Behold the earth, O lord of the Raghus, charming even in its pathos!'
And behold the Gandharvas being eaten by carnivorous beasts and birds, / their every limb handsome, adorned with all kinds of ornaments.

1.190.d:
आकृष्यमाणं निम्नेषु क्रव्याद्भिः कुणवद्रणे ॥
गात्रैश्चलद्भिर्दृश्यन्ते जीवन्तैरिव पार्थिव ॥ 14 ॥
सन्निधानं तु योधानां विद्रुतं करपङ्कजम् ॥
धनुर्ग्राहाज्जातकिणं भक्षितेन पतत्रिभिः ॥ 15 ॥
अर्धसम्भक्षितैर्वक्त्रैस्तथा सम्पूर्णभक्षितैः ॥
दुर्वृत्तान्पश्य गन्धर्वाञ्शापादिव महीक्षिताम ॥ 16 ॥
अनागसां नरेन्द्राणां गन्धर्वैर्यत्पुरा कृतम् ॥
भूयस्तदेव समरे गन्धर्वाणां त्वया कृतम् ॥
रणाजिरे पिशाचानां गन्धर्वान्पश्य राघव ॥ 17 ॥
यक्षाणां राक्षसानां च शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
गन्धर्वमांसलुब्धानां सततं क्षतजाशिनाम् ॥ 18 ॥
समुद्रदाराः सम्प्राप्ताः क्रव्यादाः क्षुधिता भृशम् ॥
त्वयैतेषां परा तृप्तिः कृताद्य रणमूर्धनि ॥ 19 ॥
नानाविधानि रूपाणि पश्य क्रव्यभुजां रणे ॥
केचित्स्थूलाः कृशाः केचित्प्रांशवो लघवोऽपरे ॥॥। 1.267.20 ॥
1.190.m:
Being dragged into hollows like corpses in battle by the flesh-eaters, / with their limbs moving, they seem as if alive, O ruler of the earth.
The lotus-like hand, familiar to the warriors, has fled [and is severed], / scarred from holding the bow, eaten by birds.
With faces half-eaten and fully devoured, / behold the wicked Gandharvas, as if [struck down] by a curse of the kings of the earth.
What the Gandharvas previously did to innocent kings, / you have done once more in battle to the Gandharvas. / Behold, O Rāghava, the Gandharvas [lying] on the battlefield for the Piśācas,
and for the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas by the hundreds and thousands, / who crave the flesh of Gandharvas and continually feed on blood.
Flesh-eaters [from as far as] the sea coasts have arrived, exceedingly hungry; / by you their highest gratification has been made today at the front of battle.
Behold the various forms of the flesh-eaters in battle: / some are fat, some lean, some tall, and others short.

स्नपयन्ति रुधिरैश्चान्ये पाययन्ति परे' सृजम् ॥
रक्तं कृत्वा कपालेषु कृत्वोत्सङ्गे पुनःपुनः ॥ 26 ॥
भार्याभिश्च सहैवान्ये पिबन्ति रुधिरं रणे ॥
पाययन्ति तथैवान्ये रामा रामानुजः स्वयम् ॥ 27 ॥
भार्याकरधृतेष्वन्ये कपालेषु पिबन्त्यसृक् ॥
कौञ्जरेषु कपालेषु पिबन्त्यन्येऽसृगुल्बणाः ॥ 28 ॥
1.190.m:
And likewise their hair stands erect; they have huge fangs and huge mouths; / terrible in front and at their flanks, others [are hideous] behind their limbs.
With faces resembling various kinds of creatures, / wearing diverse garbs, fierce, and of various grotesque appearances,
clothed in lion skins and clothed in tiger skins; / some are summoned, others bite, and others carry off the excellent blood.
Others, hoisting flesh and blood onto their shoulders, marched off; / they sport as they please in the rivers of blood created by you.
Others bathe [one another] in blood, and others make [their companions] drink blood, / pouring blood into skulls and placing it again and again in their laps.
Others drink blood in battle along with their wives; / likewise others, [their] women, make [their companions] drink, O younger brother of Rāma.
Others drink blood from skulls held in the hands of their wives; / other fierce ones drink blood from elephant skulls.

1.190.d:
शिशून्स्कन्धगतान्कृत्वा तृप्ता नृत्यन्ति चापरे ॥
हस्तमादाय पत्नीनां नृत्यन्त्यन्ये तथैव च ॥ 29 ॥
नृत्यन्त्यन्ये हसन्त्यन्ये विकृतैश्च तथा स्वरैः ॥
गायन्त्यन्ये स्वपन्त्यन्ये कलहायन्ति चापरे ॥ 1.267.30 ॥
कुणपाम्̐श्च तथैवान्ये त्यजन्त्यन्ये महीतले ॥
अन्यांश्चादातुमिच्छन्ति गृह्णन्ति च तथापरान् ॥ 31 ॥
कुर्वन्ति कलहाम्̐श्चान्ये कुणपार्थाय कुत्सिताः ॥
उत्कृत्य मांसान्यश्नन्ति केचिद्गात्रैर्विभूषिताः ॥ 32 ॥
भुक्त्वा चास्थीनि मज्जाश्च केचिदश्नन्ति राघव ॥
भरतस्य प्रसादेन तृप्ताः स्म इति चापरे ॥ 33 ॥
परस्परञ्च भाषन्ते परं हर्षमुपागताः ॥
नित्यं भवतु राज्ञाञ्च युद्धं वैरं नृशंसता ॥ ॥ 34 ॥
बलं सहायाः पुष्टिश्च येन तृप्यामहे वयम् ॥
एवमेते वदन्तश्च स्वरैश्च विविधैर्जगुः ॥ 35 ॥
1.190.m:
Having placed their children upon their shoulders, others, satisfied, dance; / taking the hand of their wives, others dance likewise.
Others dance, others laugh with grotesque voices; / others sing, others sleep, and others quarrel.
Others drop corpses on the ground; / they desire to seize others, and grasp yet others.
Vile beings quarrel over corpses; / tearing off flesh, some eat, adorned with severed limbs.
And having eaten, some chew on bones and marrow, O Rāghava; / and others say, “We are satisfied by the grace of Bharata!”
And having attained supreme joy, they speak to one another: / “May there always be war, enmity, and cruelty among kings,
and strength, allies, and nourishment, whereby we are satisfied!” / Speaking thus, they sang with diverse voices.

rathaṃ tathānye vīkṣante sasnehā bhṛśadurdṛśāḥ ..

1.268
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..

gandharvaputradārāśca rājapatnyastathaiva ca .. 1 ..
1.190.d:
रथं तथान्ये वीक्षन्ते सस्नेहा भृशदुर्दृशाः ॥
एवं स भरतः श्रीमान्मातुलेन प्रदर्शितम् ॥ 36 ॥
पश्यन्रणाजिरं प्रायाद्येन राजगृहं पुनः ॥
सोऽपश्यन्नगराभ्याशे वायव्यास्त्रविमोहितम्॥ 37 ॥
सैन्यं तत्पार्थिवेन्द्राणां व्रजन्तं समरादिमम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा ते भरतं सर्वे रणरेणुसमुक्षितम ॥ 38 ॥
संग्रामे जयिनं वीरमभ्यनन्दन्त पार्थिवाः ॥
स समेत्य महाभागैः परिष्वज्य च पार्थिवान् ॥
सान्त्वयित्वा च धर्मात्मा शिबिराणि व्यसर्जयत् ॥ 39 ॥
ततः स तां मातुलराजधानीं प्रहृष्टयोधार्यजनाभिरामाम् ॥
विवेश रात्रौ रघुवंशनाथः संस्तूयमानः स्तुतिभिर्नृसिंहैः ॥ 1.267.40 ॥
1.268
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां गन्धर्वनगराज्जनाः ॥
गन्धर्वपुत्रदाराश्च राजपत्न्यस्तथैव च ॥ 1 ॥
1.190.m:
Likewise, others, extremely hideous to look upon, gaze affectionately at your chariot. / Thus glorious Bharata, having been shown [the field] by his maternal uncle,
beholding the battlefield, went again toward Rājagṛha. / Near the city, he saw, bewildered by the Vāyavya missile,
that army of the foremost of kings. Seeing Bharata, sprinkled with the dust of battle, / returning from the battle,
the kings cheered the hero victorious in combat. / Having met with the illustrious kings and embraced them, / and having consoled them, the righteous one dismissed them to their camps.
Then the lord of Raghu's line entered by night that capital of his maternal uncle, / delightful with rejoiced warriors and noble folk, being praised with hymns by lions among men.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When that night had passed, the people from the Gandharva city, / the sons and wives of the Gandharvas, and likewise the wives of the king,

1.190.d:
रणाजिरं तु संप्राप्य रुरुदुर्भृशदुःखिताः ॥
अहो कृतान्तो बलवान्येन नो बलदर्पिताः ॥2॥
अजेयाः सुरसंघानां संग्रामे विनिपातिताः ॥
नातिभारोऽस्ति दैवस्य नाशक्यं तस्य विद्यते ॥ 3 ॥
येन नागायुतप्राणा गन्धर्वतनया हताः ॥
ये पुरा शयनीयेषु परार्ध्येषु मदोत्कटाः ॥ 4 ॥
न निद्रामभिगच्छन्ति शेरते तेऽद्य भूतले ॥
तालवृन्तानिलैर्ये त वरस्त्रीभिश्च वीजिताः ॥5॥
वीज्यन्ते पतितास्तेऽद्य गृध्रपत्रैर्महीतले ॥
परार्ध्यचन्दनाक्ताङ्गा ये विरेजुः समागताः ॥6॥
न राजन्तेऽद्य ते सर्वे शोणिताक्ता महातले ॥
आलिंग्य सुषुपुः पूर्वं वरोरुजघनाः स्त्रियः ॥7॥
ये तेऽद्यभूमिमालिङ्ग्य दुःखशय्यासु शेरते ॥
हा राजन्देवदर्पघ्न हा राजन्भृत्यवत्सल ॥ 8 ॥
हा राजम्̐श्चारु सर्वाङ्ग हा राजन्सूतवत्सल ॥
बाहुच्छायामुपाश्रित्य वयं कस्य जनेश्वर ॥9॥
1.190.m:
having arrived at the battlefield, wept, deeply afflicted with sorrow: / “Ah, mighty is fate, by which our [warriors], proud of their strength,
invincible to the hosts of gods, have been struck down in battle! / There is no burden too great for destiny, nor is anything impossible for it,
by which the sons of the Gandharvas, having the strength of ten thousand elephants, were slain! / Those who formerly, insolent with pride, upon priceless couches
did not attain sleep, lie today on the surface of the earth! / Those who were fanned by excellent women with the breezes of palm-leaf fans,
having fallen on the surface of the earth, are fanned today by the wings of vultures! / Those who, having assembled, shone with limbs smeared with priceless sandalwood,
all of them do not shine today, smeared with blood upon the great earth! / Those who formerly slept embracing women with excellent thighs and hips,
embrace the earth today and lie upon beds of sorrow! / Alas, O king, destroyer of the pride of gods! Alas, O king, affectionate toward your servants!
Alas, O king, handsome in every limb! Alas, O king, affectionate toward your charioteers! / Taking refuge in the shadow of whose arm, O ruler of men,

nirbhayā devadaityānāṃ nivatsyāmo yathāsukhama ..

1.190.d:
निर्भया देवदैत्यानां निवत्स्यामो यथासुखम ॥
संपूर्णचन्द्रवदनं पुत्र कोटिभिरावृतम् ॥ 1.268.10 ॥
विषमस्थमितो दृष्ट्वा यास्यामो यमसादनम् ॥
सभास्थं त्वामपश्यन्तो यास्यामो यमसादनम ॥ 11 ॥
एवं जने तु शोकार्ते करुणं विलपत्यथ ॥
गन्धर्वराजपुत्राणां पत्न्यस्ताः सुमनोहराः ॥ 12 ॥
ततस्ता दुःखशोकार्ताः कारुण्ये महति स्थिताः ॥
भर्तारं शिरसा हीनं काचिद्बाहुविनाकृतम् ॥ 13॥
द्विधा कृतं तथैवान्या काचित्क्रव्यादभक्षितम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा रुरोद दुःखार्ता काचिन्नासादयत्यपि ॥ 14 ॥
कुणपेषु स्खलन्त्यस्ता बभ्रमुस्तत्र दुःखिताः ॥
उरांसि पाणिभिर्घ्नन्त्यो लूनयन्त्यः शिरोरुहान् ॥ 15 ॥
नावाप यासां भवने पुरा सूर्योऽपि दर्शनम् ॥
दुःखिता मुक्तकेशास्ता जनः सर्वोऽथ पश्यति ॥ 16 ॥
1.190.m:
shall we dwell as we please, free from fear of gods and Daityas? / Having seen you here in distress, whose face was like the full moon,
surrounded by crores of sons, we shall go to the abode of Yama! / Not seeing you seated in the assembly, we shall go to the abode of Yama!”
While the people, distressed with grief, were thus lamenting piteously, / those most charming wives of the sons of the Gandharva king,
distressed with pain and grief, plunged in great sorrow, [lamented], / one [finding] her husband deprived of his head, another [finding hers] without arms.
Another [saw her husband] cut in two, another devoured by carnivores; / afflicted with sorrow, [each] wept on seeing [him], while one could not even find [her lord].
Stumbling over corpses, those sorrowful women wandered there, / beating their breasts with their hands and tearing out their hair.
They whom formerly even the sun could not behold in their palace, / all the people now saw, sorrowful, with dishevelled hair.

1.190.d:
पतन्त्युपरि भर्तॄणां समालिङ्गन्ति चापराः ॥
रुदन्त्यन्यास्तथा राजन्नुत्कृत्यमधुरस्वराः ॥ 17 ॥
रुदन्तीनां तथा तासां राजपत्न्यः सुदुःखिताः ॥
रुरुदुः करुणं राजन्विप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहाः ॥ 18 ॥
हा कान्त हा महाराज हा महाजनवल्लभ ॥
हा सुरेश्वरदर्पघ्न हा शशाङ्कनिभानन ॥ 19 ॥
हे भर्तः केन ते बुद्धिर्मरणं प्रति गाहिता ॥
हा राजम्̐स्त्वमिमां भूमिं समालिङ्य प्रियामिव ॥ 1.268.20 ॥
वसुधां प्रियबाहुभ्यां समाजे किं न लज्जसे ॥
किं शेषे पुरतोऽस्माकं विशेषेण रजस्वलाम् ॥21॥
खेचरस्यापि ते राजन्सततं वसुधा प्रिया ॥22॥
नाडायनवचस्तद्धि त्वयानर्थाय न श्रुतम् ॥
प्रिया ते यद्यपि मही तथाप्यस्मासु पार्थिव॥
युक्तं हि कर्तुं दाक्षिण्यं यतस्त्वं मत्कुलोद्भवः॥23॥
अतर्कितप्रयाणेन त्वया स्म परिपीडिताः ॥
वाङ्मात्रेण कुरुष्वास्मान्सान्त्वनं रिपुसूदन ॥24॥
1.190.m:
Some fell upon their husbands, others embraced them; / others wept, O king, crying out with sweet voices.
As they were weeping thus, the king's wives, deeply distressed, / with dishevelled hair, wept piteously, O king:
“Ah, beloved! Ah, great king! Ah, darling of the populace! / Ah, crusher of the pride of the lord of gods! Ah, moon-faced one!
O husband, by whom was your mind plunged towards death? / Ah, king, having embraced this earth like a beloved woman,
[having embraced] the earth with your loving arms, are you not ashamed in the assembly? / Why do you lie before us, especially [upon one who is] stained with dust?
Though you were a sky-wanderer, O king, the earth was ever dear to you.
For you did not listen to the word of Nāḍāyana, to your own ruin. / Even if the earth is dear to you, still towards us, O ruler of the earth, / courtesy ought to be shown, since you were born of my family.
We are tormented by your unforeseen departure; / comfort us, O slayer of foes, with merely a word.

kṛtānto balavānrājanyenākṛṣyādya nīyase ..
nāḍāyanasya vacanaṃ tvayā yadi kṛtaṃ bhavet .. 27 ..
nābhaviṣyadviyogastu tvayāsmākaṃ janādhipa ..
niśceṣṭāṅgaḥ kathaṃ tvadya rājansvapiṣi bhūtale .. 28 ..
utthāya vīra cāsmākaṃ pariṣvajya na cumbase ..
vijitya samare vīrānhatvā ca vasudhādhipān .. 29 ..
kathamekena yuddhe tvaṃ mānuṣeṇa nipātitaḥ ..
kva te vapuḥ kva te tejaḥ kva sā lakṣmīḥ kva te balam .. 1.268.30 ..
kva te tadvimalaṃ chatraṃ kva ca te varacāmaram ..
kva tatpīṭhañca śṛṅgāraṃ kva ca te tanayā vibho .. 31 ..
1.190.d:
राज्ञो न युक्तं शयनं विवृते वसुधातले ॥
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ राजेन्द्र शयनं भज मा चिरम् ॥25॥
नुन्ना वयं महाराज मदनेन मदेन च ॥
कण्ठे नु कं गृहीष्यामस्त्वया हीना जनेश्वर ॥ 26 ॥
कृतान्तो बलवान्राजन्येनाकृष्याद्य नीयसे ॥
नाडायनस्य वचनं त्वया यदि कृतं भवेत् ॥ 27 ॥
नाभविष्यद्वियोगस्तु त्वयास्माकं जनाधिप ॥
निश्चेष्टाङ्गः कथं त्वद्य राजन्स्वपिषि भूतले ॥ 28 ॥
उत्थाय वीर चास्माकं परिष्वज्य न चुम्बसे ॥
विजित्य समरे वीरान्हत्वा च वसुधाधिपान् ॥ 29 ॥
कथमेकेन युद्धे त्वं मानुषेण निपातितः ॥
क्व ते वपुः क्व ते तेजः क्व सा लक्ष्मीः क्व ते बलम् ॥ 1.268.30 ॥
क्व ते तद्विमलं छत्रं क्व च ते वरचामरम् ॥
क्व तत्पीठञ्च शृङ्गारं क्व च ते तनया विभो ॥ 31 ॥
1.190.m:
It is not fitting for a king to sleep on the open surface of the earth; / therefore arise, O best of kings, take to your bed without delay!
We are impelled, O great king, by love and intoxication; / around whose neck shall we throw [our arms], bereft of you, O lord of men?
Death is mighty, O king, by whom you are dragged away today. / If you had acted upon the counsel of Nāḍāyana,
there would not have been separation from you for us, O ruler of men! / How is it that today you sleep motionless on the ground, O king?
Having arisen, O hero, and having embraced us, you do not kiss us. / Having conquered heroes in battle and slain rulers of the earth,
how were you felled in battle by a single human being? / Where is your form, where is your splendour, where is that royal glory, where is your strength?
Where is your spotless umbrella, and where is your excellent chowrie? / Where is that ornate throne, and where are your sons, O lord?

1.190.s:
kva sā līlā kva sā lakṣmīḥ kva ca te varavandinaḥ ..
varacāmaradhāriṇyaḥ kva ca tāḥ paramāṅganāḥ .. 32 ..
adyaivasmastvayā hīnā adyaiva spṛhayāmahe..
adyaiva smaraṇīyastvaṃ gato'sijanavallabha .. 33 ..
nūnaṃ kāntataraḥ svarge rājendra pramadājanaḥ ..
yattyaktvā svajanaṃ tasya ratirbaddhā tvayānagha .. 34 ..
svacchandacāriṇā kena matiḥ śūraniṣevitā ..
tvayā prārthayatā loke yuddhaśraddhā vivarddhitā ..35..
vallabhasya janasyāsya lālitasya tathā tvayā ..
dīrghaprayāṇe kartavyo vāṅmātreṇāpyanugrahaḥ..36..
visarjaya janaṃ rājankrīḍāmaḥ sahitāstvayā ..
udyāneṣu vicitreṣu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca ..37..
vayamīrṣyāṃ na kurumaḥ sarvalokasya paśyataḥ ..
vajrasāramidaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ kṛtam..38..
gatāsumapi dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ śatadhā yanna dīryate..
karpūracandanārdrāṅga mahārhaśayanocita ..39..
1.190.d:
क्व सा लीला क्व सा लक्ष्मीः क्व च ते वरवन्दिनः ॥
वरचामरधारिण्यः क्व च ताः परमाङ्गनाः ॥ 32 ॥
अद्यैवस्मस्त्वया हीना अद्यैव स्पृहयामहे॥
अद्यैव स्मरणीयस्त्वं गतोऽसिजनवल्लभ ॥ 33 ॥
नूनं कान्ततरः स्वर्गे राजेन्द्र प्रमदाजनः ॥
यत्त्यक्त्वा स्वजनं तस्य रतिर्बद्धा त्वयानघ ॥ 34 ॥
स्वच्छन्दचारिणा केन मतिः शूरनिषेविता ॥
त्वया प्रार्थयता लोके युद्धश्रद्धा विवर्द्धिता ॥35॥
वल्लभस्य जनस्यास्य लालितस्य तथा त्वया ॥
दीर्घप्रयाणे कर्तव्यो वाङ्मात्रेणाप्यनुग्रहः॥36॥
विसर्जय जनं राजन्क्रीडामः सहितास्त्वया ॥
उद्यानेषु विचित्रेषु वनेषूपवनेषु च ॥37॥
वयमीर्ष्यां न कुरुमः सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः ॥
वज्रसारमिदं नूनं हृदयं सुदृढं कृतम्॥38॥
गतासुमपि दृष्ट्वा त्वां शतधा यन्न दीर्यते॥
कर्पूरचन्दनार्द्राङ्ग महार्हशयनोचित ॥39॥
1.190.m:
Where is that playful grace, where is that splendour, and where are your excellent bards? / And where are those foremost women holding excellent chowries?
This very day we are bereft of you, this very day we long for you; / this very day you are reduced to a memory, O beloved of the people, departed!
Surely the women in heaven are more beautiful, O best of kings, / since, abandoning your own kin, your delight has been fixed upon them, O sinless one!
By what independent rover was that mind cultivated by heroes [conceived], / by you who, desiring [glory] in the world, nurtured your zeal for battle?
To this beloved folk who were so pampered by you, / favour should be granted on this long journey, even if only by a word.
Dismiss the people, O king; let us sport together with you / in varied gardens, forests, and groves.
We do not feel jealousy while all the world is watching. / Surely this heart was made very firm, with the essence of a thunderbolt,
since it does not shatter into a hundred pieces even on seeing you lifeless! / O you whose limbs were moist with camphor and sandalwood, accustomed to a costly bed,

1.190.s:
virājase na rājendra rudhirākto mahītale ..
kva te bhinnaghaṭā nāgāsturagāḥ kva ca te gajāḥ .. 1.268.40 ..
kva te yodhā gatā rājañśakravispardhino raṇe ..
sainye mahati tiṣṭhantaṃ khaḍga bāṇadhanurdharam .. 41 ..
kathaṃ tvāmanayadrājanparalokāya rāghavaḥ ..
kṛtāntasamadṛṣṭyaiva vepathuste janeśvara .. 42 ..
sa kathaṃ mānuṣeṇādya saṃgrāme vinipātitaḥ ..
tadvayaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmo nirāśāstava jīvite .. 43 ..
na mesti kalpo dṛṣṭirvā me nasordṛṣṭisaṅgatiḥ ..
evaṃ vilapamānāstā. śailūṣasya tu yoṣitaḥ .. 44 ..
āliṅgyāliṅgya taṃ rājannipatanti mahītale ..
śirāṃsi ca vinighnanti tāḍayanti bhujāstathā .. 45 ..
paśyanti bhūyastaṃ vīraṃ bhūmāvutkrāntajīvitam ..
dṛṣṭvā bhūyaśca niḥsaṃjñā nipatanti mahītale .. 46 ..
1.190.d:
विराजसे न राजेन्द्र रुधिराक्तो महीतले ॥
क्व ते भिन्नघटा नागास्तुरगाः क्व च ते गजाः ॥ 1.268.40 ॥
क्व ते योधा गता राजञ्शक्रविस्पर्धिनो रणे ॥
सैन्ये महति तिष्ठन्तं खड्ग बाणधनुर्धरम् ॥ 41 ॥
कथं त्वामनयद्राजन्परलोकाय राघवः ॥
कृतान्तसमदृष्ट्यैव वेपथुस्ते जनेश्वर ॥ 42 ॥
स कथं मानुषेणाद्य संग्रामे विनिपातितः ॥
तद्वयं किं करिष्यामो निराशास्तव जीविते ॥ 43 ॥
न मेस्ति कल्पो दृष्टिर्वा मे नसोर्दृष्टिसङ्गतिः ॥
एवं विलपमानास्ता। शैलूषस्य तु योषितः ॥ 44 ॥
आलिङ्ग्यालिङ्ग्य तं राजन्निपतन्ति महीतले ॥
शिरांसि च विनिघ्नन्ति ताडयन्ति भुजास्तथा ॥ 45 ॥
पश्यन्ति भूयस्तं वीरं भूमावुत्क्रान्तजीवितम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा भूयश्च निःसंज्ञा निपतन्ति महीतले ॥ 46 ॥
1.190.m:
you do not look radiant, O best of kings, smeared with blood upon the earth! / Where are your elephants with broken frontal globes, and where are your horses and elephants?
Where have your warriors gone, O king, who rivalled Śakra in battle? / As you stood in your vast army, bearing sword, arrows, and bow,
how did the descendant of Raghu send you to the other world, O king? / Merely by his glance, equal to Death, did trembling seize you, O lord of men?
How was he struck down in battle today by a human being? / What then shall we do, hopeless of your life?
[…] / Thus lamenting, the wives of Śailūṣa,
embracing him again and again, O king, fell to the ground, / and struck their heads and beat their arms.
Again they looked upon that hero whose life had departed upon the ground; / and having seen him, they fell unconscious once more upon the surface of the earth.

1.190.s:
tāsāṃ rodanaśabdena samākrāntamahītalam ..
tāsāmāśvāsanaṃ cakre vidvānnāḍāyano dvijaḥ .. 47 ..
etasminneva kāle tu taṃ deśamaparājitaḥ ..
gandharvendraḥ samabhyāgādbharatena pracoditaḥ .. 48 ..
sa tatsthānamathābhyetya janaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvidhi ..
āśvāsayāmāsa tadā rājā citrarathaḥ śanaiḥ .. 49 ..
satkāraṃ lambhayāmāsa śailūṣaṃ tanayaiḥ saha ..
rājñā citrarathenātha gandharvāste pracoditāḥ .. 1.268.50 ..
rājñaścakruścitāṃ kāṣṭhaiḥ suśuṣkairbahubhistadā ..
putrāṇāmasya sarveṣāṃ yodhānāmapyaśeṣataḥ ..
candanāgurukāṣṭhaiste tathā kālīyakasya tu..51..
citāṃ gandhaiśca tailaiśca prajvālya ca ghṛtena te ..
saṃskārayitvā tānsarvānnagarāya pravavrajuḥ .. 52 ..
gandharvarājavacasā tataḥ sarvo mahājanaḥ ..
nāḍāyanaṃ puraskṛtya prayayau gandhamādanam .. 53 ..
1.190.d:
तासां रोदनशब्देन समाक्रान्तमहीतलम् ॥
तासामाश्वासनं चक्रे विद्वान्नाडायनो द्विजः ॥ 47 ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु तं देशमपराजितः ॥
गन्धर्वेन्द्रः समभ्यागाद्भरतेन प्रचोदितः ॥ 48 ॥
स तत्स्थानमथाभ्येत्य जनं सर्वं यथाविधि ॥
आश्वासयामास तदा राजा चित्ररथः शनैः ॥ 49 ॥
सत्कारं लम्भयामास शैलूषं तनयैः सह ॥
राज्ञा चित्ररथेनाथ गन्धर्वास्ते प्रचोदिताः ॥ 1.268.50 ॥
राज्ञश्चक्रुश्चितां काष्ठैः सुशुष्कैर्बहुभिस्तदा ॥
पुत्राणामस्य सर्वेषां योधानामप्यशेषतः ॥
चन्दनागुरुकाष्ठैस्ते तथा कालीयकस्य तु॥51॥
चितां गन्धैश्च तैलैश्च प्रज्वाल्य च घृतेन ते ॥
संस्कारयित्वा तान्सर्वान्नगराय प्रवव्रजुः ॥ 52 ॥
गन्धर्वराजवचसा ततः सर्वो महाजनः ॥
नाडायनं पुरस्कृत्य प्रययौ गन्धमादनम् ॥ 53 ॥
1.190.m:
As the surface of the earth was overwhelmed by the sound of their weeping, / the learned twice-born Nāḍāyana offered them consolation.
At that very time, the undefeated lord of the Gandharvas / came to that region, urged by Bharata.
Having arrived at that place, King Citraratha then / gradually consoled all the people according to rule.
He caused funeral honours to be rendered to Śailūṣa along with his sons. / Urged then by King Citraratha, those Gandharvas
built a pyre for the king with many well-dried pieces of wood at that time, / and for all of his sons, and for the warriors without exception, / with logs of sandalwood, agallochum, and kālīyaka.
Having ignited the pyres with perfumes, oils, and ghee, / and having performed the last rites for them all, they set out for the city.
Then, at the word of the king of the Gandharvas, all the people, / placing Nāḍāyana at their head, went to Mount Gandhamādana.

1.190.s:
niveśaṃ kṛtavāṃstatra rāmaparvatarodhasi ..
kṛtvā niveśanaṃ tatra sarve citrarathājñayā ..
sukhamūṣurmahārāja pālyamānā mahātmanā .. 54 ..
babhūva tatrāpi purapradhāne śailūṣapautrastu janasya rājan ..
gandharvarājastu cakāra tasya saṃrakṣaṇaṃ rāghavamukhyavākyāta .. 55 ..

.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
athāṣāḍhasya māsasya śuklapakṣāvasānikam ..
utsavaṃ tridaśendrāṇāṃ samāptaṃ dinapañcakama .. 1 ..
kṣīrodatheṣaśayanaṃ bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ ..
yoganidrāṃ tadā bheje lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. .. 2 ..
bharato'pyutsavaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā janārdanam ..
mahīdānaṃ tathā kṛtvā naktāśī dinapañcakam .. 3 ..
cāturmāsye nivṛtte ca madhumāṃsasya bhakṣaṇāt ..
visarjayāmāsa gṛhātpūjayitvā mahīpatīn .. 4 ..

gandharvanagarāvāptairvibhajya dhana saṃcayaiḥ .. 5 ..
1.190.d:
निवेशं कृतवांस्तत्र रामपर्वतरोधसि ॥
कृत्वा निवेशनं तत्र सर्वे चित्ररथाज्ञया ॥
सुखमूषुर्महाराज पाल्यमाना महात्मना ॥ 54 ॥
बभूव तत्रापि पुरप्रधाने शैलूषपौत्रस्तु जनस्य राजन् ॥
गन्धर्वराजस्तु चकार तस्य संरक्षणं राघवमुख्यवाक्यात ॥ 55 ॥
1.269
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अथाषाढस्य मासस्य शुक्लपक्षावसानिकम् ॥
उत्सवं त्रिदशेन्द्राणां समाप्तं दिनपञ्चकम ॥ 1 ॥
क्षीरोदथेषशयनं भगवान्मधुसूदनः ॥
योगनिद्रां तदा भेजे लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
भरतोऽप्युत्सवं कृत्वा पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम् ॥
महीदानं तथा कृत्वा नक्ताशी दिनपञ्चकम् ॥ 3 ॥
चातुर्मास्ये निवृत्ते च मधुमांसस्य भक्षणात् ॥
विसर्जयामास गृहात्पूजयित्वा महीपतीन् ॥ 4 ॥
उक्त्वा बहुविधैः सान्त्वैः परिष्वज्य सुपीडितम् ॥
गन्धर्वनगरावाप्तैर्विभज्य धन संचयैः ॥ 5 ॥
1.190.m:
He made a settlement there on the slope of Mount Rāma. / Having made a settlement there, they all, by order of Citraratha, / lived happily, O great king, protected by that noble-souled one.
There too, O king, the grandson of Śailūṣa became the chief of the people in the city, / and the king of the Gandharvas protected him according to the word of the foremost of the Raghus.
1.269
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, at the end of the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha,
the five-day festival of the chiefs of the gods was completed.
Lying upon Śeṣa in the Ocean of Milk, the blessed Madhusūdana
then entered into yogic sleep, wishing for the welfare of the worlds.
Bharata too, having celebrated the festival, worshipped Janārdana,
and likewise made gifts of land, eating only at night for five days.
And when the four-month vow of abstaining from honey and meat was concluded,
he honoured the kings and dismissed them from his home.
Addressing them with various soothing words, embracing them tightly,
and distributing the hoards of wealth acquired from the city of the Gandharvas,

saṃpūjya varṣārātrau tu svakīyaṃ sainikaṃ janama ..

preṣayitvā janaṃ prāyātkiñcicheṣaṃ svasainikaiḥ ..

1.190.d:
संपूज्य वर्षारात्रौ तु स्वकीयं सैनिकं जनम ॥
संमंत्र्य प्रेषयामास सोत्कण्ठं दयिताजने ॥ 6 ॥
प्रेषयित्वा जनं प्रायात्किञ्चिछेषं स्वसैनिकैः ॥
उवास मातुलगृहं भरतां देवराजवत ॥ 7 ॥
अवसच्चतुरोमासान्प्रीत्या राघवसत्तमः ॥
ततः कार्तिकमासाद्य शुक्लपक्षावसानिकम् ॥ ॥ 8 ॥
उत्सवं विपुलं चक्रे संप्राप्य दिनपञ्चकम ॥
प्रबोधं देवदेवस्य त्रिदशानां महोत्सवे ॥ 9 ॥
तेषु दत्त्वा महादानं कार्तिक्यां च विशेषतः ॥
पूजयित्वा जगन्नाथं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ॥ 1.269.10॥
शुभे दिने सुनक्षत्रे पूजयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
सांवत्सरं पुरस्कृत्य स्थपतींश्च स राघवः ॥ 11 ॥
सिंधोरुभयपार्श्वे तु स चकार पुरद्वयम ॥
पुष्करं पुष्करावत्यां तक्षं तक्षशिलां प्रति ॥ 12 ॥
1.190.m:
and having honoured his own soldiers during the rainy season,
he consulted with them and sent them away, yearning for their beloved kin.
Having sent the people off, with a small remainder of his soldiers,
Bharata went and dwelt at his maternal uncle's house, like the king of the gods.
The best of the Raghus dwelt [there] with pleasure for four months.
Then, at the beginning of the month of Kārttika, ending with the bright fortnight,
when the five days arrived, he celebrated a great festival
for the awakening of the God of gods, amid the great festival of the gods.
Having bestowed great gifts on those [days], and especially on the full moon of Kārttika,
and having worshipped the Lord of the world, who bears the conch, discus, and mace,
on an auspicious day, under a favourable lunar mansion, having honoured the best of the twice-born,
and having placed the astrologer and the master-builders in the lead, that scion of Raghu
founded two cities on both banks of the Sindhu:
Puṣkara in Puṣkarāvatī, and Takṣa in Takṣaśilā.

1.190.d:
आरम्भं पुरयोः कृत्वा सोभिषिच्य सुतावुभौ ॥
पुरद्वये महाराज विधिवद्भूरिदक्षिणः॥ 13 ॥
पुष्करे पुष्करं पुत्रं तदा तक्षं च यादव ॥
पुरुद्वये समाकीर्णे वणिग्भिर्ब्राह्मणैस्तथा ॥ 14 ॥
शिल्पिभिश्च महाराज नानाशिल्पोपजीविभिः ॥
गृहपुञ्जसमाकीर्णे देवायतनभूषणे ॥ 15 ॥
प्रतिष्ठिते तदा राज्ये पुत्रयोर्भरतस्तदा ॥
धनरत्नाश्वनागैश्च विभज्य तनयावुभौ ॥ 16 ॥
युधाजिति परीदाय गते संवत्सरे तदा ॥
अतीते कार्तिके मासे नक्षत्रे तु गुणान्विते ॥ 17 ॥
जगाम भरतः श्रीमान्रामं द्रष्टुं नराधिप ॥
सोनुयातः सुतैर्वीरो मातुलेन युधाजिता ॥ 18 ॥
तीरे स्वधाम्नस्तौ पुत्रौ मातुलं तु युधाजितम् ॥ ।
विसर्जयामास गृहान्परिष्वज्य च पीडितम् ॥ 19 ॥
भरतः साश्रुनयनो बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा ॥
स्तोकेन काञ्चनाङ्गेन रथेन च तथा ययौ ॥ 1.269.20 ॥
1.190.m:
Having commenced [the building of] the two cities, and having duly consecrated both sons
in the two cities, O great king, he gave lavish sacrificial fees,
installing his son Puṣkara in Puṣkara and Takṣa [in Takṣaśilā], O Yādava.
When the two cities were crowded with merchants as well as brahmins,
and with craftsmen, O great king, who lived by various crafts,
crowded with clusters of houses, and adorned with temples of the gods,
and when the kingdom was thus established for his two sons, Bharata then
divided wealth, jewels, horses, and elephants between both his sons.
Having entrusted them to Yudhājit, when a year had elapsed,
and the month of Kārttika had passed, under an auspicious lunar mansion,
the glorious Bharata went to see Rāma, O king of men,
the hero followed by his sons and by his maternal uncle Yudhājit.
On the border of his own realm, he dismissed both his sons
and his maternal uncle Yudhājit to their homes, embracing them tightly.
His eyes full of tears, Bharata set out with a small
fourfold army and on a chariot of gold.

1.190.d:
संरुध्य च रथात्ते तु गच्छन्तं भरतं तदा ॥
ददृशुर्दीनमनसः किंचिदागतविभ्रमाः ॥ 21 ॥
मुहुर्मुहुः परावृत्य भरतः कथमप्यगात् ॥
परस्परमपश्यन्तो त्वरावन्तस्तथा गताः ॥ 22 ॥
भरतोपि तथा देशान्सरांसि सरितस्तथा ॥
ग्रामपत्तनसंगाद्यान्व्यतिक्रम्य पुरीं ययौ ॥ 23 ॥
अथाससाद चायोध्यां दीर्घकालप्रवासकः ॥
प्रविश्य नगरं तत्र पताकाध्वजसङ्कुलम् ॥ 24 ॥
सुधावदातभवनं सिक्तं चन्दनवारिणा ॥
कृतं रामाज्ञया सर्वं पूजितामरबालकम ॥ 25 ॥
निर्ययौ पुरतस्तस्य चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः ॥
रामाज्ञया महातेजा नागरैः सह लक्ष्मणः ॥ 26 ॥
भरतं लक्ष्मणो दृष्ट्वा चिरकालप्रवासकम् ॥
अभ्यवादयत प्रीत्या शिरः कृत्वा महीतले ॥ 27 ॥
भरतो मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय सम्परिष्वज्य पीडितम् ॥
सर्वत्र कुशलप्रश्नं तत्र कृत्वा यथाविधि ॥ 28 ॥
1.190.m:
Turning back from the chariot, with downcast minds
and somewhat bewildered, they watched Bharata departing.
Bharata departed, turning back again and again with great difficulty.
Ceasing to look at each other, they departed in haste.
Bharata too, passing through countries, lakes, rivers,
and gatherings of villages and towns, went on to the city.
Then he reached Ayodhyā after his long sojourn abroad,
and entered the city, which was filled with banners and flags,
its mansions white with plaster, sprinkled with sandalwood water,
all arranged by Rāma's command, with the children of the gods worshipped.
By Rāma's command, the intensely radiant Lakṣmaṇa came forth
to meet him, accompanied by a fourfold army and with the citizens.
Seeing Bharata after his long stay abroad,
Lakṣmaṇa greeted him with affection, placing his head on the ground.
Bharata smelled his crown, embraced him tightly,
and duly inquired after his well-being in every respect.

1.190.d:
यथार्हं पूजयामास जनं नगरवासिनम् ॥
कुशलप्रश्नयोगेन स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिता ॥ 29 ॥
स तेन जनवृन्देन पूज्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
विवेश नगरं श्रीमान्भरतो नागधूर्गतः ॥ 1.269.30 ॥
विमानहर्म्यप्रासादगवाक्षकगतेन तु ॥
स्त्रीजनेन महातेजा वीक्ष्यमाणस्तु सस्पृहम् ॥ 31 ॥
आससाद महातेजा नरेन्द्रद्वारमायतम् ॥
तत्र वादित्रनादोऽभून्महान्कलकलस्तथा ॥.32 ॥
राजद्वारमथासाद्य सोवरुह्य गजोत्तमात् ॥
आदाय लक्ष्मणं पाणौ प्रविवेश तदा सभाम् ॥33 ॥
तत्र सिंहासने रामं स ददर्श महाभुजम् ॥
चन्दनेनानुलिप्ताङ्गं सर्वाभरणभूषितम् ॥ 34 ॥
संपूर्णचन्द्रवदनं नीलोत्पलदलेक्षणम् ॥
दृष्ट्वैव रामं भरतः कृत्वा भूमिगतं शिरः ॥ 35 ॥
निपपात महातेजा लक्ष्मणेन विशेषतः ॥
रामोपि भरतं दृष्ट्वा समुत्थाप्य महाभुजम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.190.m:
He honoured the townspeople according to their rank,
addressing them with smiles while exchanging inquiries of well-being.
Honoured repeatedly by that multitude of people,
the glorious Bharata entered the city mounted on the neck of an elephant.
Gazed upon with yearning by the women
standing at the windows of celestial cars, mansions, and palaces,
the intensely radiant one reached the wide royal gate.
There arose a great sound of musical instruments and a vast tumult.
Then, having reached the royal gate, he dismounted from the excellent elephant,
and taking Lakṣmaṇa by the hand, entered the assembly hall.
There he saw the mighty-armed Rāma seated upon the lion-throne,
his limbs anointed with sandalwood and adorned with all ornaments,
with a face like the full moon and eyes like blue lotus petals.
As soon as he saw Rāma, Bharata placed his head upon the ground;
the intensely radiant one fell prostrate, and Lakṣmaṇa likewise.
Rāma too, seeing Bharata, raised up the mighty-armed one,

1.190.d:
जग्राह पीडितं कण्ठे मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय चासकृत् ॥
आदिदेशासनं तस्य पृष्ट्वा कुशलमव्ययम् ॥37॥
निवेद्य रत्नमुख्यानि गन्धर्वाणां स राघवः ॥
रामाय धर्मनित्याय यथा भेजे वरासनम् ॥ 38 ॥
पृष्टस्स रामेण निवेदयित्वा वृत्तं यथावत्पुरुषप्रवीरः ॥
विसर्जितस्तेन गृहाय गत्वा संपूजयामास तदा स विष्णुम् ॥ 39 ॥
स्वप्ने तथोवास स रामपादौ चासाद्य वीरः समरेष्वजेयः ॥
रामोपि राज्यं सहितस्तु तेन चकार सम्यङ्निहतारिपक्षः ॥ 1.269.40 ॥
ततश्चतुर्थे परिवत्सरे तु शुश्राव रामः पुरयोः प्रतापम् ॥
कृत्वा सुताभ्यां भरतस्य विष्णोर्मुदञ्च लेभे परमां प्रहृष्टः ॥ 41 ॥
एषोऽद्य प्रोक्तो विजयो मया ते रणाजिरे राघवनंदनस्य ॥
श्रोतव्यमेतन्नियमेन पुंसा विज्ञानधर्मार्थयशोभिरामम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.190.m:
clasped him tightly by the neck, smelled his head again and again,
and, inquiring after his imperishable welfare, offered him a seat.
Having presented the foremost jewels of the Gandharvas
to Rāma, who is constant in dharma, that scion of Raghu took the excellent seat.
Questioned by Rāma, that hero among men reported the events as they had occurred;
and dismissed by him, he went to his house and then worshipped Viṣṇu.
In peace the hero, invincible in battles, dwelt attending Rāma's feet;
and Rāma, having utterly crushed his adversaries, ruled the kingdom together with him.
Then, in the fourth year, Rāma heard of the glory of the two cities
established by the two sons of Bharata, and he, exceedingly pleased, attained supreme joy in Viṣṇu.
Thus has been recounted by me today the victory of the son of Raghu on the field of battle;
this, delightful with knowledge, dharma, wealth, and fame, should be listened to by a man with regular observance.

इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे द्वितीयभागे श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे श्रीरामचंद्रभरतसमागमो नामैकोनसप्तत्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 269 ॥ ॥ ॥
समाप्तश्चायं प्रथमखण्डः ॥
1.190.m:
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Meeting of Śrī Rāmacandra and Bharata,' in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the First Book of the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara, [which is] the second part of the Śrī Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa.
And the First Book is completed.
